title: Usable all year round!
text:
I did a lot of research before choosing a grill and stopped on this one for multiple reasons (and still don't regret it).
- Very easy to control temperature with adjustable vents
- Ashpan and cleaning lever is an amazing feature/design! 
- Very convenient for 2 zone cooking
- Has many additional accessories (can be bought separately) 
- Great for low-n-slow cooking/smoking
- Great price for the quality and amount of features you get!

Couple of features/accessories that I would like to see in the next generation (if that will ever happen)
- Marking on lower vent to show when it is closed or half/fully open, so I don't have to open the lid to check- (My fix: drew little indicator marks with permanent marker)
- Add ceramic ring to sit on the lower grate to retain heat when it's 6F outside (My fix: Placed bricks around the circumference of a lower ring which makes it more efficient in the extremely cold weather, IMHO)
- Create an accessory stand/fixture for kabobs (My fix: place kabobs on a grilling grate, but it's not the same as caucasian kabob grilling)

title: Back To the Beginning
text: I hadn't used a charcoal grill since I was in college 25 years ago.  I bought a propane Genesis after graduating, and it lasted 23 years (outside the whole time).  That is 23 Chicago winters.  Great product.  So when the cart finally disintegrated 2 years ago, of course I bought another one!  Last year I received a 22" Original Kettle Premium as a present.  Except for the copper color, it looked pretty much the same as the one I used in college.  Which looked the same as the one my father used when I was a kid.  I didn't think I'd use it much (since I have a new propane Genesis), so I took it to the cabin.  Getting the charcoal ready the first time seemed like a chore, but I finally got it lit.  Hint: get a chimney starter.  Once the meat hit the grate; the smoke, and the smells filled the air.  That is when the memories hit me.  Seeing my Dad tending the kettle at the neighborhood parties.  The smell of burgers, ribs, chicken, and steak being tickled with oak and hickory smoke.  At that moment I knew I was in trouble!  Soon after I got a second copper kettle to go next to my Genesis.  This led to a Smokey Mountain, Summit Charcoal Grilling Station, and I even pulled out my early 1970's Smokey Joe.   They ALL get used!   I think I need a "Q series for the cabin.  Sorry, I got a little off track on my review.  The Original Kettle Premium is everything you'd expect from a Weber grill.  The best outdoor cookers on the market.  The little extras like the ash catcher and the hinged grates are unbelievably handy.  Be warned though; just like Girl Scout cookies, it is hard to stop at just one.

I received my copper Original Kettle Premium as a Christmas gift from my father-in-law in 2016.  I’ve always been a year round griller, but had traditionally been using gas for years. Steaks, burgers, brats, and chicken are so much better on the Weber! It’s been easier to control the heat, and the smokey flavor really ads to food. Plus, the 22” cooking surface offers tons of space to cook for plenty of people.  And learning to smoke.... easily the best ribs and pork shoulders I’ve ever made!  I’m pretty sure my neighbors get jealous when they smell the smoke from firing it up!

Not only is operation and cooking so easy, but so is clean up.  The one touch system makes clean up a breeze, and keeps the Kettle operating consistently. text: Bought it a year ago along with the collapsible stand. The cast iron grill is not wide open like a typical wire type grill. You almost need to remove the grill and wash it, which is kind of a messy job.  The cast iron grill also makes it very heavy. On the plus side, it cooks great. title: LOVE!LOVE!LOVE!
text: This was a Christmas gift to me from my family. Its been years since I've owned a grill. I mostly bbq on a large smoker which is great if you're cooking in large quantities. So after researching various styles and brands, the one that stuck out the most was Weber.Weber has one of the largest and most loyal communities I came across. One of the things that impressed me the most was how long these grills were lasting, some in excess of 20 years! That spoke volumes to me. So, Christmas morning 2017, I got what I asked for the Weber  Master-Touch Charcoal Grill 22". I chose this because of the features . The grate allows me to insert accessories from the Weber BBQ Gourmet system. The grate is hinged on both sides to easily add charcoal or wood chunks during a cook. The ash catcher and one touch make clean-up a breeze, and the tuck away lid holder keeps the lid secure while I'm checking the food or fire. This grill holds temperature for hours before having to add any fuel. I love the charcoal baskets, they keep the fuel off the sides, and keep you from using more than you need. A full weber chimney will fill both baskets up perfectly.  I've added some pics of my favorite grill sessions. It was my first time doing a bone-in pork roast and the Weber made it easy and so enjoyable. If your contemplating buying a Weber, my advice is buy it! you won't be disappointed.

If you are looking for someone to test your products, please do not hesitate to choose me.

Thank you to whoever reads this!
Ben

title: Spoiled
text:
It's been decades since I grilled using charcoal. I've got a Weber Genesis gas grill and a large smoker so I thought I had my bases covered. Wrong. What a great addition to my outdoor cooking options. The Master Touch is a great size for most of your grilling needs.  Extremely well constructed, the included accessories and options are really nice. Warming rack, the ability to add charcoal to the grill without having to remove the grilling grate, venting options on both the lid as well as the charcoal bowl, the ash bucket, being able to add other cooking options on the grate and other items.  This is a really terrific charcoal grill.  I've used it some but not as much as you like (weather issues) and everything that I've cooked has been outstanding.  When I decided to get this grill, my wife looked at me like I was nuts. After the first meal, jerk pork tenderloin and grilled sweet potatoes, she became an immediate fan.
This is just a fabulous piece of cooking equipment that you should not deny yourself. I should add that I got a bag of Weber charcoal when I purchased my grill and man, that stuff last forever.
There's simply not enough good things to say about this grill.  Thanks Weber for continuing a long tradition of outdoor enjoyment.

text:

I did have an issue attaching a large LP fuel tank; tank was full, a new gas line but no fire!
Found out there was an issue with the old tank.  I replaced it with a new one and I was now in business!

I went to the local butcher shop, picked out a beautiful ribeye, cooked it as instructed:  BEST STEAK I’VE EVERE HAD!

My only complaint would be the Weber Stand I purchased, a like wobbly for me!

title: Nice Compact Grill
text: I was disappointed at first as I was expecting the earlier version with the enclosed base.  After consideration I realized that the open base and side mounted tank was a better idea. Assembly was easy but the directions were a little vague.  I found that certain steps were better performed out of order in order to access some fasteners. Once assembled, I was surprised how sturdy it is.  The grill body and drip pan are designed for easy clean up - love that.  Now let's get cooking.  The grilling surface heats uniformly and properly seasoned the grates are almost stick free.  The flavor bars prevent uncontrollable flare ups and produce great smoky flavor from the grease drippings.  The burner controls are very affective in maintaining desired temperature.  The negative aspect for me is the stainless steel side trays and control face.  I would have preferred something easier to clean.

title: Quality parts make for a quality product
text: I bought this grill the day I closed on my new home. While priced higher than similar sized grills, the quality of the parts and the overall construction convinced me to buy this one. It has even cooking zones and heats up rapidly. It's also very easy to clean. It was a great decision to buy it and i recommend it highly as a first and last grill.

title: Great upgrade for the kettle grill.
text: Recently I needed an extra grill to cook up some food for a large group so I ran out to buy one. I shopped around before I decided on a new Weber master touch grill. I like the grill’s new features. That’s why I bought it. I don’t like the two piece grate though. It’s a bit of a pain to clean. I do like the ash catcher underneath. It’s a way better design than the old style. The thermometer in the hood is a plus. It gives you a good reference of how hot your coals are inside at least. My biggest gripe with the Weber kettle grills is that the hoods aren’t hinged. The hoop rail thingie they’ve added helps but it’s not a final solution. The hood needs to be hinged. Many times I considered trashing my old Weber for that one and only reason. Overall I’m happy with my newest Weber grill. It cooks hotter than my old Weber. I have no idea why but it does seem to and it’s taller. I might even benefit from a few more inches in height still but it’s at least better than the old. I hate hunching over to check my food.

title: Easy Assembly, simple cooking
text:
I have had this grill for about 2 months now, and I am slowly putting it through its paces.  The assembly was pretty easy, instructions are picture oriented instead of word, which can cause confusion, mainly in the placement of the wires/harness.  
   As for the use, best gas grill I have ever owned or used.  I grill a lot for family and friends, and we all agree this has taken the food to the next level.  It fires right up first thing every time, heats up fast, very easy to adjust the temp to the desired range.  Food does not stick terribly, first use there was some as expected.  
    It may look small but it handles large jobs as well was small with ease, the dual side shelves are nice along with the tool holder.  I have zero complaints about this product up to this point.
    Do not let the price tag scare you away.  It is worth every cent, you get what you pay for, especially an outdoor item that sees the weather.  I have learned that the hard way.

title: New Design
text: We have had this grill now for about a month. So far so good. I do like the open base design very much. The large wheels are perfect when repositioning the grill. Much better than those tiny casters that never actually roll well. Overall I like the design. It appears to be better designed than our Char Broil (Professional series) that we had before. Although, I seem to have turned out a better steak on the 'ol Charbroil, I think it has to do with my inexperience with this new Weber grill. The grill works fine and I just need more training miles on it. Also, as stated in the manual, "Resist the urge to lift the lid and peek". The first few times I was surprised that the Weber did not burn the meat even though it was on there longer than I felt comfortable. So it just works different than our previous grill. And that is not a bad thing, just a fact. Additionally, I am not used to a temperature gauge that actually works. I look forward to more grilling occasions but so far we really like it. Simple and less parts that can fail. Time will tell and I sure hope that it won't rust as much as the previous grill did, but overall I am happy with the purchase.

title: My 2nd Weber Spirit in 25 Years!
text:
Purchased a Weber Spirit 2 burner grill 25 years ago and it still works like new today (one set of new burners, one set of SSteel grills/flavorizer bars, a few igniters over the years). Needed a larger 3 burner grill for entertaining, so bought this new 3 burner version.  

The E-310 is improved in nearly every way. Taller lid so that I can cook vertical "beer can chickens,"  greatly improved grease collection system, 3 powerful burners, two usable side tables, the temperature gauge is finally in the right place (the middle of the lid instead of on the side), much better igniter system, much smoother burner controls that can make finer adjustments, no more rubber end plugs on the chassis (which used to fall out after a few years), much improved gas gauge, and I prefer the "open cart" design of the area under the grill vs. the enclosed pedestal with doors found on some Weber models (hard to keep clean of bugs, etc.).  

IMO, the very best feature of this Weber is that it has a much larger area for indirect heat cooking (roasts, ribs, ham, fish).  Very useful!

Reliability: I expect this one to last as long as my previous Spirit, which is still happily grilling for my son's family!

Cons?  Just one that prevents me from giving a 5 star rating;  the left side table folds down and is supposed to be used as when moving the grill (one hand on either side and lift to put the grill on its wheels to move like a cart).  This mechanism needs serious redesign, the table will pop out of its upper locking lugs no matter how carefully this is done.  Moving the grill using this side table will eventually damage the table so that it will not lock.  And I need to move our grill each time that it is used.  [One more Con that is not really about the grill, Weber's grill cleaning sprays and non-stick cooking sprays don't work very well.]

My kettle is at a point where there is absolutely no leaks. It's a tight snug fit. I smoked a pork but for 13 hours without making vent adjustments. Once you understand your grill it's truly "set it and forget it". I bought this grill because I wasn't happy with my gas grill. The food tasted like chemicals sometimes. I also wasn't happy with my pellet smoker or electric smoker. After having food off of this grill I sold all of my cookers and replaced them with Weber charcoal grills. I now own a Summit Charcoal, 22.5 Weber Smokey Mountains and a new 26" Kettle. I will not go back to any other method of cooking. Charcoal and wood chunks make food taste amazing. text: The last gas grill I had used lava rock. It ruined a LOT of meat. I swore I would never have another gas grill. But, that was many years ago and since then many of the flare up issues have been fixed. Yesterday was the first test of my new Weber Gas Grill. We were going to have some beautiful Porterhouse Steaks for dinner but I wanted to test this grill out and season it with cheaper meats first. I cooked a grill full of burgers first, with no problems and then some fatty brats. I stayed right there and watched. It did flare up a little but stayed manageable. They turned out great. Finally the steaks. I got nice grill marks and the flavor was great. So far, I am happy with the grill. It heats up fast and has plenty of heat. I have always been a fan of charcoal grills because I like good smoky flavor. You get good smoky flavor with this grill, it's just not hickory or oak. I think I will order a smoke tube and experiment with that. I like the convenience of a gas grill. Turn on the gas, fire it up, this grill heats up fast, cook it up and your done. If you use charcoal, do you have charcoal on hand? Lighter fluid? Are you just wanting to cook some hot dogs? A few burgers? A Steak or two? It can be a waste of charcoal pretty easily. This grill produces good results faster and easier. I'm impressed so far!

text: This is my second Spirit grill; the first was a Spirit two burner. It cooks as good as ever, and I really like the new propane tank holder design. The frame engineering leaves much to be desired, and after following the assembly instructions to a T, I have run into multiple issues that are minor but nonetheless annoying. First, the two little plastic feet that are supposed to be hammered on with a rubber mallet would not stay attached after the grill was assembled. Then, one of the wheels fell off while carrying it up a few deck stairs. The space-saving fold down shelf (still an awesome feature, and one of the main reasons we bought our original Spirit grill!) is supposed to be used to move the grill, but it never feels secure, and has even slipped out in transit. I like the big wheels for moving the grill in grass, but the whole design of using the foldable shelf as a handle just feels half-baked. In all, I’m happy with the grill, especially if I don’t have to move it, but these minor issues just seem like something that should have been taken care of in the R and D phase.

text: I purchased this grill upon retiring my 19 year old weber.  The old frame finally had rusted.  19 years later I purchased my new grill for less than the one I did 19 years ago.  At first I thought it alarming that they had to have really cut corners.  Nope.  I think the new grill is better engineered and the manufacturing tolerances are tighter than ever.  The attention to detail from the welded nuts already in place, to the plastic washers that won't scratched the parts so they don't rust is awesome.  Everything was in the box, no missing pieces and although it took me several hours I feel really good about the quality of things.  What also struck me was putting on the grill cover.  I though it would be difficult but it slid right down.  There are no sharp edges, no 90 degree corners for the cover to get hung up on.  Great Job Weber!  I suspect I will get another 19 years from this one.  I not sure there will be a next one.  I may be too old to grill any longer at that point.

title: Best Gasser I've Had
text:
I purchased my Spirit II back in April to compliment my 22" Kettle. Some nights when I get home Late I just cant wait to heat up the charcoal to make dinner. That being said, this is my 3rd propane grill, and 1st from the Weber collection.

The Good: The cast iron grill is amazing! I really did my home work before purchasing this grill and some peopler were complaining about food sticking. I think one of two things was happening, not properly pre heating the grill, and not using Weber's no stick cooking spray. I get perfect sears on all my steaks with this grill. The heat displacement is amazing! It feels even across the surface and I don't feel like there are any hot/cool spots; just an even temp displacement. I kissed flare ups goodbye with this grill. The heat shields work perfectly and I get an amazing sear. 

The Bad: I wanted to give this grill 5 stars; it's originally what I was going to rate it. I have a short list of areas for improvement. One, the stainless steel table tops are pretty easy to scratch up just from placing some cooking tools on the table. So, I tend to lay a wood cutting board on the table top to help prevent that. I'm also not a fan of the table folding in on the left hand side. It can make it a bit of a pain when moving it around, I understand it's for storage purpose but I have considered replacing the bolts for the table with screws that would hold it in place permanently. I've seen some people scratch up some of the interior while removing the warming rack too. It took me a second to Last jab at the grill is I purchased this item in red. There are some areas on the lid that have some flaws or almost look like some black specks where I suppose it wasn't painted quite right, nothing worth complaining about but I am writing a review so I thought I'd mention it. 

All in all this is an amazing grill. The price and the few flaws I had mentioned are the only reason I didn't give it a 5 star. I'll probably end up replacing the tables years down the road. The grill is easy to clean, cooks like a dream, is easy enough to move around with the large wheels. It's a top notch product and I doubt I'll ever buy anything other than a Weber again

title: First time Weber owner
text:
I recently broke down and joined the ranks of a Weber owner. I am 40 years old and have always had the relatively cheap gas grills that last a few years. You know the ones – the 200.00 job at the hardware store that looks fantastic when you buy it. And it was! It cooked great for the first year. Then the 2nd year, it was ok. The 3rd year, you said to yourself “Well, I am going to rebuild the baby and get a few more years out of it!” 
Here is where you ran into your first issue – there were no parts to be found anywhere! The same hardware store is now selling the “updated” version. The parts don’t match and they want you to buy another grill. 
I looked over at the Weber grills and something caught my eye – a 10-year, top to bottom warranty! This can’t be true. I read the fine print, and sure enough, it is. Anything that breaks, outside of normal wear and tear, is covered. Ok – as Peter Griffin would say … “Keep going” … 
Next, I see all these parts on the wall at my local hardware store. There is a section for weber parts that is 4 times as big as the generic parts. I did not get the impression that “Weber’s were cheap because of all the replacement parts offered” I got the impression that, just like a car, you will need to replace items over time. And look! You can actually purchase them at a local hardware store! This means when something breaks, and your wife has 10 people coming over for an impromptu cookout – you can run to the store and get what you need. And bonus – these parts are reasonably priced! 
Ok – I bit. I bought the 3 burner Weber Spirit 2 in sapphire blue. Being a nerd, I read the owner’s manual cover to cover – I wanted to take care of my new investment. After burning it in for 20 minutes, I threw on some chicken. 
The first thing I noticed was how hot the grill got. I think it got up to around 550 degrees with the lid closed. I was worried I would not be able to wrangle this beast. I opened the lid and it cooled off quick. Superior cook box that hold in heat when needed and lets it go after. 
The grill cooks fantastic! The rear of the grill is hotter than the front consistently. This is by design and I like it. The 2 side tables are worth their weight in gold! Previously, I had a side burner I would never use. I went from a side burner to 2 sturdy side tables that I love. 
The components of the grill are top notch as well. The grates weigh about 5 pounds each, the lid closes quietly, and the overall structure of the grill is solid. It lights every time on the first try and grease is funneled down into a replaceable tin pan. It is clean, neat, and easy to maintain. 
If I were you, the next time your generic grill goes out, quit playing around. Buy a grownup grill that will last you awhile. Don’t take my word – do your research – ask your friends and google till there is no tomorrow. You will find that the little area in your mind that likes to grill will be very satisfied.

I also do not like that the burners run front to back, instead of side to side, which leaves one much less usable space on the grate, and forces one to sometimes push the meat up under the hanging warming rack connected to the grill lid. I replaced a Genesis Silver II with this one and I had no problems with it, even if I wanted to slow cook in the 250 degree range.  The Spirit, if I start out on low eventually works itself up to 350 to 375 degrees.  I have to turn a burner off to get it to run around 350 degree.  I haven't even tried slow cooking on it.  I don't know if it is the design of the lid or what.  I do think Weber needs to make some modifications on them and correct or replace the ones in consumer use.  Certainly a major problem which needs correcting. I'm hoping in cold temperatures it has enough to get the temperature up in the higher range. We’ve also grilled corn on the cob and asparagus on it. Lighting it is a breeze since you only have to press a button. Clean-up is super easy since the grates come out. I typically spray them with nonstick spray the same as I do when I cook inside on the stove, and I haven’t had an issue with anything sticking. The drip pan underneath is awesome since they make the disposable pans. I just clean out the main pan and put it in there. The grill isn’t heavy, and I look forward to taking it camping someday. I’m officially hooked on grilling now, thanks to my little blue Weber Q1200!

I've used it for about month, at least 3x/week and couldn't be happier with the results every time, whether I'm just grilling a steak and some veggies or roasting a chicken. text:

You can view every step in 3D, zoom in/out, and spin the view to see the unit from a different perspective--it was very intuitive. 
After it was built, I ran out and bought a propane tank and fired that baby up. It's been an absolute staple at my home since I purchased it and with a name like Weber, I'm sure it will be around for many years to come.
I couldn't be happier with it.

title: What a great little grill!
text: I bought this because I live by myself and in a condo development where we are not allowed to keep full size propane tanks on our patios.  Because this can use the small 1 LB propane tanks, I can leave it there, and also use it.  It is the perfect size for me and actually holds more food than I realized.  I also think it is very easy to clean, and because the grill grates are so small I can easily take them into the kitchen to hand-wash.  They clean up easy without much elbow grease too!  I also bought the portable cart, and love the functionality of it as well.  This grill has made a splash in our neighborhood because there are only one or two residents per unit and because we can keep and use this on our patios.  My only request is to have a cover made that will fully cover the grill and the cart.  The little grill cover is great, but I would prefer to cover both.  Don't hesitate to buy this, it cooks good, and doesn't require much more time than larger grills.  Keep the lid down, and only turn food once....you will be rewarded!

The Bad

text:
I bought my Webber kettle about two months ago, after reading about them and watching others use them. I can honestly say, that I am not in the least bit disappointed. I have used it for grilling and smoking meats. It just took one time using it, to figure out the vent system. After that, it was fairly easy to keep a consistent temperature. The only item I swapped out, was the cooking grate. I wasn't to crazy about the removable center on the cooking grate and it bothered me a bit. For only $20.00, that took care of any concerns I had. I bought mine at a bit box store, non assembled. When I got it home and started to assemble it, it was missing the assembly instructions. No problem, I watched a few YouTube videos and it went very well. The kettle itself, didn't have the holes pre drilled for the lid holder. I called customer service and they had one sent out and I received it within a week. I bought it for a memorial day cook out and decided to drill the holes myself. It was very easy to do and it works great. I have an extra kettle if I ever need to replace the bottom in the future. I could have probably took it back to the store and replaced it, but the wheels were in motion and I took care of it myself. It's my first kettle grill and I actually am very pleased with it. I plan on building a counter top for it and setting it down in it, as counter space is a must at the grill.
I would recommend this kettle grill to anyone wanting a new grill, you just can't go wrong with a Webber.

Here in Michigan, my family and I grill at about 1-2 times per week almost year round.  I've grilled quite a few times with it, even took it to the beach at a state park. I'm still getting used to how efficient it is.  I've over cooked some meat a couple times but it was still juicy despite being cooked past my normal preference because of searing the meat. My neighbor has done some indirect cooking by placing the food in a container that was slightly elevated and off the cooking grate.  I might try that.  I bought the adapter hose to hook up to the large propane tank I have left from getting rid of the old grill. That works great.  I bought a 16" x 30" two shelf steel tool cart for from a local tool and freight store because the Weber Q 1200 cart cannot accommodate full size propane tanks.  I wish all of the Weber Q carts could accommodate any Weber Q.  I've called customer service a couple times just for tips and tricks and they've been super helpful. title: Great little grill overall, but bad low range
text:
This is a very solid little grill, probably one of the best made small portable gas grills on the market. I've cooked some great wings, chicken breasts, burgers, and veggies on it. Unfortunately, the low range isn't very low, especially when ambient temperatures get up above 80F, 90F, 100F. Recently, with the lid closed on low, I measured temps from 550F-650F at 1" above the cooking surface in a variety of places with my ThermaQ. That's 100F-200F above the ~450F-475F indicated on the lid thermometer. I contacted support and they sent out a new regulator and valve assembly, but that made no difference.

So, you can probably forget any kind of low and slow cooking on this thing, but it works well at higher temperatures. I need to rig up some type of block or adjustment that will hold the lid cracked open a set amount. That'll be the only way to achieve lid-"closed" cooking temperatures in the 350F-400F range or lower. Or maybe an adjustable vent on the top of the lid would help cool things down on low.

Anyway, the too-hot performance on low is the only thing keeping this from getting 5 stars and excellent from me.

title: Great product. Everything I had expected.
text:
I have grilled and roasted numerous times on my new Q1200, and overall I am quite pleased. There were a couple flaws I have encountered. With the great Weber support, I am working through them. 

I am having the original regulator replaced, for the temperature ran too hot while on LOW setting while roasting. On low, it ran between 390 and 410 degrees, instead of  what Weber stated should be 325 to 350.  I have yet to install the replacement on my next day off. Hopefully this will resolve the  temperature issue.

When attempting to install the recommended portable 16.4 oz propane cylinder, it does not line up, due to the grill  structure being in the way, not allowing the 90 degree angle needed to thread onto the regulator. When I contacted Weber, they said it was a known design flaw, and I would have to place slight pressure on the regulator housing in order to align the portable propane tank, allowing it to thread properly. 

The optional roasting pan is no longer available, so I created my own that works just as well if not better.

Although not necessarily a flaw, but one needs to watch for grease drippings from the lid, when opened. This happens when grilling 80% lean burgers, or any meat with fat. I have my Q1200 on the collapsible, portable Webber stand, and the grease will drip on the cross members of the stand and to the wooden deck, or whatever surface. I now periodically wipe the back edge of the lid (where the grease accumulates) while grilling burgers. Afterwards, I wipe the inside of the lid.

The grill surface is great. I always coat with peanut or grape seed oil prior to preheating. Nothing sticks when grilling in accordance with recommended grill times before turning/flipping. It also makes clean up much easier. I also seasoned the optional griddle. This now permits me to cook pancakes, french toast and even eggs without sticking at all. I did find out when placing the griddle on the grill surface, the griddle has even heat distribution, no hot spots. Unlike when you remove on half of the grill, as recommended, replacing with the griddle, there is a circular hot spot.

I am quite please with the Q1200 and have recommended to those who have inquired.

title: Pesky drop-down table
text:
This is my third Weber (first gas Weber), and I am anticipating the same quality and longevity as I’ve enjoyed with my others. I love the fine tuning adjustability of the Spirit II 2-burner grill, which allows for those maintained tempurature ranges necessary for longer cooks.

The overall construction of this Weber is top notch, with one exception — that pesky drop down table. As it is on the side one would intuitively use to wheel the grill from place to place, it seems equally counterintuitive that the drop down table is as flimsy as it is. My first attempt to move my grill resulted in the front side attachment point disengaging. I checked to make sure everything was fitted as indicated in the manual and reattempted to wheel the grill across our deck. Again the table disengaged. This really isn’t a deal breaker for me because I do not anticipate moving the grill all that much. As a matter of fact, I doubt I will even utilize the drop down feature. Perhaps I’ll simply bolt it solid to the frame and be done with the issue altogether.

This design feature aside, I would still recommend this grill. The two burner size is perfect for the couple who like to grill for themselves and/or a handful of friends.

title: Phenomenal grill, second to none, but small flaws
text:
First of all there’s nothing better than cooking on a Weber kettle. I’ve used them before but this is the first that I’ve owned and I’ll have a hard time going back to gas (even if it is quicker) because the flavor is so much better. so that said the reason I’ve given it 4 stars instead of 5 is because of the assembly. 

The leg material is a little thin and flimsy but plenty strong enough for the application. My main complaint is how the legs attach. The spring loaded pins that hold the legs in place on the kettle are annoying to work with and took some frustrating manipulation to get them to lock in place properly when following the directions. Weber would’ve been much better served using a pin with a cotter pin to hold them in place, it would’ve been much faster and easier for both assembly and disassembly (in the odd event you’d need to take it apart). Also on my grill one of the legs didn’t want to cooperate going into its home and was so tight that the finish on the inside of the kettle has a circle shaped crack in it because I had to push so hard. Also the lid hook is largely useless because it’s difficult to get it to stay on the rim of the grill. I just ended up placing the lid on the ground initially because if you hang it on a handle it melts the plastic grip cover. I was thankfully able to find a clip on lid holder on Amazon that fixed the issue. I probably sound petty for that but I’ve had back issues recently and it makes it much easier to not have to bend over. 

All in all I love this grill, it’s near perfect and you can’t beat it for the money/value. With a few small inexpensive tweaks on Weber’s end it would be completely perfect.

title: Replacement for my old Silver B
text:
My mother-in-law purchased this as a replacement for my Silver B.  Things weren't going well with that one.  The first thing I was disappointed with was the orientation of the burners.  They run vertically in the grill as opposed to the Silver B's horizontal configuration.  This is a problem because of the way the convection is used during indirect heating.  I suspected this new grill would not heat the same, and I was correct.  It takes much longer to preheat and burn off debris than the Silver B.
I do like the electric start button and the large knobs.  It lights right up, but it is new, so I don't know how long that will last.  The handle stays cool, which is another plus.  I was frustrated to find the chrome coated metal "bun warmer" situated on top of the cast iron grate.  You'd think they could make the bun warmer of the same material to make it last longer.  I use it as a place to cook hot dogs while grilling hamburgers.  It would be nice if there was a bumper on either side so the dogs didn't roll off the ends.
The gas gauge appears to not be reliable; not surprised because it's very stiff.
Cooking has gone relatively well.  I was not expecting it to work as well as my Silver B because of the burner configuration.  However, food is cooked evenly across the large surface.  There are no hot and cold spots like my Silver B, which, I suppose is a good thing.  The grate is easy to work with and somewhat easy to clean.  I have not cooked a bird on it yet, but I am concerned about the shallowness of the lid and how well it will handle larger birds. 
Overall I am pleased with the cooking experience.  I suppose it will take some getting used to.

title: Not a perfect grill, but close
text: I have always owned fairly inexpensive grills from big box stores, thinking that Weber grills were overpriced and you were mostly paying for the name. My previous grill was mostly stainless steel, had tons of features, and was very nice...when new. After 4 years of ownership, it was not so nice anymore. The electric starter lasted for exactly one season, the vaporizoer/flavorizer/whatever bars were rotting away, the grates were getting harder to clean, etc. It was clearly time to replace it.  This time, instead of heading to the big box and picking up a mid-priced grill with as many features as I could find, I went online and started reading reviews. I read them on the websites that sold grills, I read articles, basically whatever I could find. And they all said basically the same thing, get a Weber Spirit. Seriously, that's what they said. Just get the Weber Spirit. So I did. Yeah, its costs twice as much as the other grills I've bought, and yeah, it is lacking many features (no side burner, no sear station, etc). But what it is lacking in features, it makes up for in spades in quality. To be honest, at first, I wasn't that impressed with its quality. The metal is of a lower gauge than I expected, maybe the wheels aren't quite what I'd expect. But the first time you actually grill with it.....yup, there's the quality. The evenness of the heat is remarkable. No more moving burgers around to get them to all cook the same. Put as many on there as you want, flip them in place, and they will all be cooked exactly the same. And somehow, they taste better, much better. That must be a byproduct of the evenness, but what I grill tastes much better than it did on my old grill. Abnd with a 10 year warranty, this will be the longest I will ever have a grill, and I couldn't be happier about it. Way to go Weber, you nailed it.

title: Waste of money, disappointed. You were warned...
text: We had bought this grill about 9 months ago, the first few months it was hardly used due to winter. From the beginning the grill did not cook evenly, the temperature was much lower in the front than the back, which is not what you want when spending this kind of money on a "smaller" grill. It got much worse though, around spring we started to use it more, and one day cooking steaks it had caught fire, to the point where we needed a fire extinguisher to put it out. At first due to the severity we thought it was maybe a propane leak either from the tank or lines, or maybe improper assembly. But after we deep cleaned the grill we tested everywhere and could find no leaks. Literally the next time grill, or time after, the same thing occurred. This time we caught it faster but still had to use an abundance of baking soda to stop it, again requiring a deep clean. Pretty much every other time we have used this grill since then it occurs, the last time causing the damage in the pictures attached, and the grill peaked a temp at over 600 degrees. We noticed that for whatever reason the small amounts of grease and debris are being ignited and catching whatever other material is in the bottom of the grill and grease pan on fire, hence it being hard to put out. BUT with having owned a few BBQs in the past, since when does a whole BBQ catch on fire due to a little grease and debris? It is a grill, it's purpose is to get down and dirty and produce good food, not require a deep clean after every use. The pictures should show how clean it is and still it ignites... Well while at the store the other day we had noticed the grill had a new design change both on external looks but also the internal design, pretty sure this isn't a coincidence... This isn't a cheap grill for the size, one would say on the higher end even, but after this experience we will never buy a Weber again.

title: Well Designed Grill, Good Value for the Price
text:
Overall I'm really happy with the grill and I think you're getting what is probably the best Value/Price ratio out there. The Ten-Year Guarantee was what clinched the deal for me.

One Star Off for Shipping: It arrived with a crack in the a cast aluminum grill box; essentially the largest and probably most expensive part. It was clearly a shipping issue and why they skimped on the packing around such a large/expensive product, I can't say. Weber was great about immediately honoring the warranted however so that's a plus (and the new grill-box was sent in much better packaging). It took almost a month to actually arrive though, which was definitely a little annoying. In the end it all worked out though and is now good to go.

ASSEMBLY REVIEW: This is the type of project that, if you like building things and are a regular DIY type of person, it will be all pretty straight forward. For me, it was sort of fun, and I'd rather see how it all is built than have it just "show up." If this is not you, then it'd be best to pay the extra for assembly I guess, or get a friend who's "mechanical" to help. I think it took maybe 2-3 hours overall and I really took my time with it. It's packed together really densely and that sort of slows things down. AGAIN: With some much packed in there, they really need another layer at least around the outside to better protect it. Anyway,I unpacked ALL of it first and I suggest you do that too. I made sure to have each section all laid out on a swept garage floor and sets of screws next to them.

INSTRUCTIONS: Mostly pretty well written and illustrated. Certain sections were lacking in explanations; others gave more info than needed. Some of the guidance is frankly crazy though, like the admonition to "not" use a powered drill/screw-driver for for the several dozen screws! Seriously? Just set your drill to a low torque setting so nothing gets stripped out; otherwise plan to add at least an additional hour or more for the build. Also, they say you'll need two people to do it, which I really can't see why. No section is all that heavy, nor anything truly needing more than two hands.

ACTUAL ASSEMBLY AND BUILD: For the most part I was pretty happy with the way it came together, and I could see that some decent engineering when into it. Having heavy coated screws is a good idea so you won't be getting any rust at those points. Some of the structure is not as heavy as I'd liked, but I'll grant that once all put together, the structure overall is pretty well tied together and should be relatively strong. 

Areas that are important for durability definitely are well-made: the grill box is heavy cast aluminum, and that's the section that normally would rust out (all my previous grills did, and I'm sure yours have too). I've had heavy cast aluminum pots and pans before and basically the never wear out no matter how times they get used or cooked with, so that's what I expect with this too. The grill "grids" (the portion you actually grill on) are really heavy duty cast iron parts and I also expect these to last at least the decade that they are guaranteed for. The KNOBS I am not a huge fan of, being plastic and probably the type of part that might wear just from weather  or age; we'll see.

Once I was done assembly I "cooked it in" for about 45 minutes (meaning I fired up all three zones at high and just let it go without any food inside). It definitely had some (but not a lot) leftover manufacturing oils or cleaners on some surfaces, so you want to burn all that off first. I put in a little foil bowl of wood cooking chips to get some smoked flavor to coat the inner surfaces too. It probably was a few days before it got to a more optimal "flavor" which is just like any new cook pan.

USAGE and FEATURES: I'll state upfront that the idea of this being "app connected" is absolutely ridiculous to me, and counter to the reason for getting outside and grilling in the first place. And even if I did use it, I have a hard time believing the electronics it uses will last more than year or so, especially once it goes through a few hard winters. I always cover the grill after each usage, but that won't do much for a weeks of below freezing temps that we get in New England.
The integrated Fuel Tank Scale is genius and such a simple but useful feature. I usually have a spare gas tank on-hand but in the past there have been a few occasions when the fuel ran out unexpectedly and that's never fun when you food is half-way cooked. This will at least give me a heads-up when things are getting low.

GRILLING/COOKING: After having this for around two months and using it on average 3-5 times a week I have to say, it works great. I get consistent, great tasting burgers, steaks, pork-loin and veggies out of it every time. It heats up really quickly, but I have yet to have anything burn at all. The cast iron grill grids are excellent, and the thermometer in the lid seems repetitively accurate (I'm not looking for anything exact, just a decent idea). Super easy to keep clean the inside and the outside for the most part as well. I use a little spay oil on the stainless steel sections for cleaning and polishing, figuring that I don't want to keep putting steel chemical polish on it all the time. Otherwise, get yourself a grill cover and you'll be good to go.

title: EASY TO LIGHT AND PLENTY BIG!
text: Grilling should be easy, and the Weber Spirit II E-210 makes it so. It is a well designed and refined grill and a joy to use. Mounting the propane tank is easy, and the tank weight gage is a nice bonus feature. The grill lights easily and the ignitor batteries are easily accessed when replacement is needed. The temperature controls work very well and heat is distributed evenly across the entire cook surface. The porcelainized cast iron grates are reversible - a feature I don't normally use, but it is there for those who do. The grease control system on this grill actually works and grease is collected in an easy to reach foil pan which can be dumped out or replaced entirely. It is a rare occasion that I would need more cooking space than this grill offers, as this one can probably hold 16 burgers at a time. Most of the time it is just my wife and I, so this grill was the perfect choice. I am confidant that I will get many years of use, but it is too new to know how well it will perform over time, hence the 4 star rating.

title: Bad Design
text:
I had a Spirit 210 from years ago.  Comparing this Spirit 310 to it, I can see major design differences.  The grill components appear cheaper.  The stainless steel used isn't high quality.  The absolute worst part of the grill is the design of how the grilling enclosure sits within the frame.  The grill is bolted in to the frame at the front but nothing in the back.  As a result the back of the grilling compartment can move around within the frame, left or right.  This is a problem because when the lid is opened, the back of the lid scrapes the frame unless it is sitting perfectly in the center.  The previous Spirit 210 I had sat above the frame.  So the hinge point didn't matter.

Despite the major design flaw and the lesser quality steel, the grill functions very well.  Heat is evenly distributed.

If I had realized what I was buying I may have chosen a different grill.  I'm not too worried about lesser quality components as Weber in the past has always stood behind their products.  If something rusts out, they generally just replace it for free if you call them up.  Standing behind their product counts for a lot.

text:
Have never owned anything but weber grills (30+ years.) Bought this one as a replacement for a very old but highly performant propane grill.

My old grill would fire right up very quickly, simply and reliably. On occasion, with this model of Weber, it will fire up to 250 deg. and not heat up further. The 1st time I used it, we actually had guests over and it was quite an embarrassment. Eventually the food got cooked but the delay was unexpected and socially awkward. I later called your cust service line and a very nice CSR guided me through a methodical process for slowly filling the gas lines/burners before sparking the flame and it solved the issue.  I had not read any instructions because I had used a Weber gas grill for years and saw no reason to use it any differently...pretty straightforward stuff after decades of using a Weber gas grill. I thought this must just be for the 1st use of a new Weber but it happened again last night---fortunately it was just our family this time, but it did cause some delay in getting the food ready. After following the instructions to shut it off for 5 minutes and trying again (this time being more methodical), it did fire up properly.

However, I am also finding that I am having more grease fires than I ever did with the old grill. And of course, that means more flames and smoke--to the point, where it is uncomfortable opening the grill to check on the progress. I smell like a volunteer fire fighter afterwards and the amount of heat and smoke I am exposed to is actually uncomfortable. So not a good user experience at all.

title: How much do I love this grill? C'mon, it's a WEBER
text:
We bought this Weber to replace our previous one that had weathered the Florida weather outdoors for 13 years.  We upgraded to the model that was a little bit fancier--thermometer on the lid, ash catcher at the bottom--and have been MORE than pleased with the results.  Both of these additions are welcome.  I know my fire is at the right temperature AND the ashes go right into a little bowl.  MUCH easier to clean up!

I'm using this grill two or three times a week, and have NOT YET screwed up a dinner or lunch!  I am no cook, believe me, but the Weber makes grilling dinner very easy. The only difficult part (for me) was making certain the coals were ready for the food. Using lighter fluid, at least for me, is a guessing game.  How much is too much, and if you use too little, the coals won't properly ignite.

I wised up a few weeks after getting the grill and ponied up $15 for the Weber Rapidfire Chimney starter.  Quit wasting $$ on lighter fluid; this contraption gets the coals going in about 20 minutes.  And you can pour them out on the charcoal grate as you please!

One particular triumph I'd like to add: barbecuing CHICKEN was something I had avoided until getting this new grill.  You don't want to UNDERCOOK chicken, and that was my fear.  Fortunately, Weber's manual gives you all sorts of guidelines about how to cook meat.  And when I followed their instructions, the chicken has turned out delicious!  Now my family looks forward to me grilling chicken for an evening dinner!  

Bottom line?  This grill is well worth the money!  I look forward to grilling on this Weber for another 13 years!

title: What happened to you?
text:
It’s Thanksgiving and for the past 18 yrs I have grilled my turkey’s on my original 22. Sadly this August, had to retire it due the bottom rusting out. 

This year would be no different, soo I went out the Tues before and picked up a new one from The Home Depot. 

Right out of the box as I put it together, I realized what I was not putting together an upgrade to what I previously owned, but rather an inferior knockoff! 

WEBER… WHAT HAPPENED TO YOU???

The heavier grates, the thermometer, the wheel covers… nice, but they seem to be distractors to the fact that kettle itself is clearly made from a much thinner gauge steel than my original 22. 
 
In all the years I owned my original, the handle never got so hot that I needed a heat shield. I can only imagine it’s due to the thinner gauge steel. 

Another ting about the lid… it just sits on top of the drum, and with no weight… there is no seal as you can see by my photos. The lid to my original hugged the lip of the drum creating a seal. 

One positive… the thermometer works well. It confirmed that the drum holds less heat resulting more coal to retain a consistent temperature.

Lastly… I ask you again…,”Weber, what happened to you?”

title: A good mid size grill
text:
I purchased the Spirit II E-210 to replace an older Spirit II grill. The newer Spirit II has a simpler design and lacks the cabinet on the bottom, which I think is an improvement. The cabinet served no purpose and made replacing the tank difficult. The open legs are less prone to rusting and the drip tray is a better design than the older setup. It still uses the same type of disposable aluminum dip tray. 

The cast iron grate is top notch and one of the better features to the grill. I've owned all types of grills in the past with a variety of materials used for grates; steel with porcelain coatings, chromed steel, stainless steel and cast iron. The cast iron is the only one that holds up. 
The Weber burners are fairly durable and the cooing surface is perfectly sized for all but the largest jobs. Unless you're cooking for large groups, the Spirit II is more than large enough. 
The scale that the tank hangs from is a useful feature to give you an idea of the amount of fuel you have left and the tank is very easy to change.   
The stainless steel side trays are a nice touch and are easy to clean. The igniter and control knobs are well placed and the battery for the igniter is easy to replace. 

If you're looking for a good basic grill that isn't huge, the Spirit II is the way to go.

The size of the grill surface is perfect for mostly cooking for a couple people by using just two burners. It adequately handles the need to occasionally cook for a larger group employing all three burners. I've had an entire beef tenderloin cut into steaks (about 15 steaks) on the grill at one time. The only problem and the one that keeps me from giving it 5 stars is the side table opposite the wheels (left side - facing the grill). It is the one that will fold down (the other, right side, is stationary). The latch just will not hold when you tilt the grill off its legs to roll it around. If you fold it down, there is nothing to hold on to so that you can lift one side up and move the grill about. It's a disappointment every time I have to move it for any reason. title: Excellent Grill - Easy to assemble, easy to use
text:
This grill was a gift at Christmas.  It took me about 2.5 hours to assemble, but it was actually easy considering how many parts there are.  And I take time to read directions and double check drawings etc.  I didn't have to redo anything.  The grill is sturdier than any grill I have owned before (I have has several). I love the starter button which makes lighting it so easy. The cooking grates are so good, the meat doesn't stick to them and the brushes Weber sells are perfect for cleaning the grates. 
Suggestions: Before you ever use the grill, buy the correct cover and use it whenever the grill isn't in use.  But, do wait until it cools to put the cover on.  Clean the outside after every use with stainless cleaner and a cloth.  Change out the little drip pan after every two or three grillings.  They are a little small and if they overflow you will have a mess. Finally, this grill can get hot! I only turn it all the way up except to clean it after use.  If you set it on the bottom setting it will keep the grill at 350 - 400 with the lid closed. Nothing should probably ever be cooked hotter than that, except searing a steak. 
Aside from buying the brushes and cover, go ahead and buy a smoker box.  At least in Texas we know the difference between grilling and BBQ. And if you want to BBQ, you can't do that without smoke.  With a smoker box (Weber sells one), you can soak some hickory, oak or mesquite wood chips, put them in the smoker box and set if on the back of the grill.  Then is you smoke (BBQ) a brisket or chicken for fajita meat, it will have good smoke flavor (not as good as a wood fired pit, but this is close enough and not nearly as difficult). 
FYI - please don't call grilling hotdogs on the grill Barbeque!  It is just grilling!

text:
I bought this grill about four months ago to replace the Weber gas grill I had used hard for 20+ years.  THAT was a great grill.  This is a fantastic grill!  It actually has more usable flat surface for putting things down, yet has a slightly smaller footprint than its predecessor.  Added bonus:  One of those surfaces folds down against one side of the grill, which decreases the space it takes up when "at rest".

This grill is more sturdy as well.  I was skeptical about the use of plastics in the base, but it really does seem more rugged, nearly indestructible, because of that material.  It's also lighter.  I loved my old grill, so I can't believe I'm saying this:  The burner system is a big improvement over the older design.  I didn't think I would like the front-to-back design, but now I love it.  It also gives much more flexibility for things like indirect heat.  The old one, about the same overall dimensions, just had two long burners running side-to-side.

The control knobs seem more sturdy as well.  Everything about this grill just screams high quality.  Gotta love what Weber has done to improve their product line over the years.

I'm not planning to use the wireless access features, but it's cool that it's ready for that.  Overall I have to say that this is a wonderful grill, well worth what I paid for it, and I'm glad I stuck with the Weber brand.

title: Love My Q1200
text:
I use a large charcoal grill most of the time, but I almost never grilled during the rainy Seattle winter (and fall and spring).  Finally, I decided to buy a small gas grill for use in the shelter of my small back porch.  I'm so glad I found the Weber Q1200.  It fits nicely on my porch and will move out to the patio when the rain ends.  Even now, during the rare snowstorm, I'm able to grill under cover.

I've grilled asparagus, steaks, fish, chicken and burgers, all to perfection.  Tonight I even grilled the corn tortillas for fish tacos.

I have no complaints after almost 10 weeks, grilling a few times each week.  The shelves are handy, and the electronic ignition is flawless.  One reminder, though, to brush off the top of the burner after you've brushed the grates, since the burner has no drip cover protecting it from the falling debris.

I've also followed the recommendation from others and have lined my drip pan with aluminum foil, allowing it to be used indefinitely.

One thing that Weber should really make clear on the website is that the grill cannot accommodate the Coleman camping propane canisters, as they're too large in diameter to fit between the grill body and the connector.  However, I've also bought the adapter hose and use a large propane tank instead of the small canisters, which I'll only use when grilling in the park.

text: I took delivery last Thursday and assembled it last Friday.  It took me 2 1/2 hours to assemble as I did not have any help.  The assembly instructions are a delight, all pictures and no words. So, a pleasure to assemble.  Performancewise, it is fare superior to my old Weber Genesis, which was falling apart as the fasteners holding the lid had corroded.  I was very impressed with the packaging inside the box.  Apart from the plastic bags, which are all recyclable like grocery bags, all of the other packaging was cardboard, which was also recycled.  Years ago it would all have been plastic foam.  So, kudos to Weber for being environmentally aware.

title: 3-Burner Grill Is The Right Way to Go
text: Excellent online consumer-report reviews of this E-310 led to our purchase. Great heat - 2-burners I'd bet is fine if you really need an even smaller grill, but 3 is the way to go to get a little more grate-space and heat. Weber customer service team has been awesome and prompt with any issues concerns I've had - that service alone makes the big-ticket price for this grill well worth the investment.

title: Just amazing!
text: I was going to rehab my 2001 Silver B, but the cost for replacement parts and time just didn't seem worth the effort.  Sooo, I went to the big orange store and bought a Spirit II E-310 completely assembled.  First cook last night was some Nebraska sirloins. Perfect!  Granted, the newer grill is not as heavy duty as the older Weber gassers, but with the 10 year warranty I think I will get many years of great grilling.  Only negative is the pesky left side table.  A little hard to move the grill when the table is in the up position, but I'll get the hang of it.  If there was a way to place the left table in a permanent "up" position, that would be great.   Get one...I don't think you'll be disappointed! Very reasonably priced too.

This is a versatile and affordable product. Mine is used at the cottage where we enjoy entertaining groups of 6-8.  The bbq has enabled me to gain a bit of a reputation for doing this, to the point where I have considered moving up to a more substantial unit. But before I pull the trigger on that, I find myself back at the cottage enjoying another incredible meal from this simple little unit. I think I'll keep the extra $$$ and buy more beef. 

Adjustments to the air intakes at the bottom as well as the exhaust damper at the top allow you to easily control the temperature. The integrated thermometer on this unit is fundamental in this process. You can cook hot and fast or as slow as you wish with this pretty basic bbq. For my skill set, this temperature control allows me to develop recipes with confidence that I can repeat consistently.

Plus, the parts that wear out over time are available from this established brand. I have one that is probably 15 years old because I have been able to replace worn parts.

This is a quality product from a quality company.

title: Excellent BBQ
text:
I've bought the cheapest BBQ's I could find for years. They'd last one season, and then next season the grill / burners would be rusted out / degrading, or the sparker wouldn't be working, or the heat distribution would be terrible, having almost cold spots in some area's or extremely hot spots in other areas. The last cheap one I bought shot flames out the back when cooking anything at all.

Finally decided to spend a lot more than I usually would have and buy a Weber. Home Depot had this model on sale so we picked it up. Was it expensive? Yes. Almost a year later, was it worth it? Definitely!

This grill has excellent heat control and heat distribution. The ignition system is reliable. It's sturdy and well built. It burns propane efficiently. Much better than some of the ones I had in the past.

I only have 2 gripes. 1) Where the BBQ base rests on the metal stand it's starting to show signs of rust, even though the BBQ has been under a genuine Weber cover since day 1 and never exposed to rain. 2) All the Weber accessories are really expensive compared to similar products made by someone else. The only accessory that I bought that is genuine Weber was the cover. Everything else was 3rd party.

title: Terrible Customer Service
text:
I Bought this grill yesterday. It was the only one in this color which I had been looking for. There was no obvious damage to the packaging. Upon getting this grill home and opening the box and unpacking the grill to make sure I had all the pieces I found quite a few upsetting damages. First I was presented with the crack to the handle and a chip in the paint of the lid. I then found the crack to the rear of the lid. Further inspection I found the crack in the grill box. The control console has a crack in it as well. The Weber emblem in the lid is missing a threaded bolt and the nut and washer to hold it on. Finally the warming rack doesn't even fit the slots. 

It appears this grill must have been made and packaged on a Monday. I reached out to customer service to see if I can get these parts replaced and was told it wasn't there problem and I need to contact the dealer (awesome warranty) So now I will be dealing with the dealer and will be without a grill for who know's how long. 

I am no expert but there was no damages to the exterior packaging and the amount of carboard for protection on the inside it appears this happened prior to shipping. Some of the issues the warming tray not even fitting the grill box and the missing emblem pieces are just poor craftmanship. I did not expect this with a Weber grill and just being told to take it back to the dealer is not acceptable. Guess It is back to reading reviews for another grill company.

title: Worth the money
text:
My dad always had a Weber kettle grill. He and I would grill all year, in the winter we’d wear our winter gear and cook.
As a wedding gift my parents got me a Weber kettle grill, green. 
25 years later that grill is in need of being replaced. The wooden handles rotted off years ago. The cleaning system and ash catch pan fell off. I melted the wheels while burning sticks and pine cones in the grill. 
My grill sits outside year round. Covered in ice and snow. It’s been blown over by straight line winds. Ridden hundreds of miles in the utility trailer on vacation. 
These are expensive for a charcoal grill. I have no idea how much mine cost when new. But I am buying another and I will keep my current one for backyard fires. 
I have cooked everything on my grill, pizza, using my cast iron skillet I’ve made breakfast. I’ve used it as a smoker...
The nice thing about charcoal grills is you know exactly how much charcoal you have left. There is no running out of propane half way through your meal. You have your bag of Kingsford and you can see how much you have left. 
Buy one. It is the best there is. It will last forever and you will not be sorry you did.

text: Our third Weber.  The igniter switch died.  In order to light the grill without the switch, you need to insert the "spring" with a lit match on the end, through the grill.  Aside from the obvious fact that there will always be a wind to blow out the match, if your igniter fails and you opt to use a hand-held propane lighter, you run the very real risk of setting your arm on fire!  Our previous Weber grill had a hole drilled into the box so you could SAFELY insert a match or propane lighter into the box to light the grill when the igniter failed.  It is obvious that whomever designed this feature never had to use it.  And, to make matters worse, the website makes it virtually impossible to find the manual needed to address replacement of the igniter.  Just going around in circles of advertising and self-kudos.

text: I originally purchased my Spirit E 210 in early Spring of 2013, for approx. 400.00, I have cooked on this grill 365 for 6 years. I replaced the enameled cast grates and flavorizor bars last fall after 5.5 years but the burner assembly is still going strong. The grill has been used weekly 365 and always fires on the first click! Cooking on this grill with the high heat and indirect fire box design and simple 2 burner control has proven successful from everything from steaks, chops, ribs and veggies. My only issue was that after short 6 years of the grill sitting outside on our deck, the caster base completely rusted and fell off the body when I went to move the grill to give it a good summer season pre clean to get rid of the winter and wet spring gunk. The base will always be the most exposed (catching the snow/rain) where the cover leaves a little exposure, but I can easily still argue that I got 2x the life out compared to the 2-3 “big box” brand grills I owned previously and the grill box is still in great shape. Now keep in mind this grill gets used frequently sometimes daily in the summer and my maintenance program and cleaning consists of a soft nylon scrub brush and sponge + garden hose with dish soap on the exterior 3-4 times a year and it “usually” stored under a cover ½ the year in-between cooks in the very sloppy late fall and winter months in NE Ohio. The interior gets cleaned with a plastic putty knife 2-3 times a season after lots of marinade or bbq cooking. I loved this grill and almost tossed it last week after the base disintegrated. I reached out to customer service and ordered a replacement base and side panels and for less that ½ the price of a new grill and a few hours replacing the parts (same amount of time of building a new grill), I am pleased that I am up and grilling again. I am optomistic and hopefully will get another 3-5 years of grilling out of my “partly new” Weber at this point. Customer Service (available on Sunday on a holiday weekend) was awesome and product quality is top notch! I also have a 22” kettle grill that is at a minimum of 25 years “new” and still is my go to for smoking using the classic snake method and wood fired grilling and pizza cooking with great success!

title: Best (only) BBQ I've ever owned!
text:
My spouse and I needed to buy a BBQ for our family (we have two small children) and there are so many to choose from it can be overwhelming! But using all the internet reviews as our guide, we settled on the renowned Weber name to guide us. We decided to go with a smaller BBQ as opposed to larger, and this Spirit II is suiting us just fine. We have plenty of room to cook enough to feed the family and have some leftovers for lunches. If we have a larger party over at some point we will likely need to cook in batches, but we don't host much so I think we'll be good.

Oh my gosh, the unmistakable BBQ flavour on our hamburgers, steaks, chicken breasts and chicken thighs is unbeatable! I haven't gone much outside the box yet (cooking pizzas or veggies, for example), but I'm interested in mixing it up at some point. 

One thing I've noticed is that I can't get it to heat up past 500 degrees - not sure if this is a flaw or just part of the design specs. The thermometer reads up to 600 degrees, so I assumed it would go that high. Either way, 500 degrees seems to be hot enough to cook things so far.

The only downside I can see to the BBQ (to any BBQ, for that matter) will be when it comes time to deep clean it. text:
Great family-sized, corner-of-the-deck grill. I was a cook for 10 years and a chef for 5, and have owned and used more than a few grills over the years. I would have liked to see a bigger pivoting upper deck on this mid-sized model as the stationary one included is quite small for roasting veggie trays or keeping medium-large steaks hot.

Also with the wheels on the right, and the fold-down side-tray on the left, rolling it around without having the tray popping off the cleats is a challenge. Simply putting the folding tray on the same side as the wheels, or having an option to permanently fix it in place, would have made this a non-issue.

I was concerned when I saw the 5 heat distribution plates and only 3 burners. But heat seems pretty even-spread, with minimal hot-spots.

First impressions, are great; these two minor gripes the only things keeping it from being a 5-star grill for me. The 10 year warrantee on all parts seems to be worth it's weight. The open, simple build will make cleaning inside and out relatively fast and easy.

title: Last two have been a disappointment
text:
I have been a fan of Weber for a couple of decades and the few I bought back then where and are great grills and are still being cooked on. Concerning the newer innovations that Weber has added, I’m very impressed with the new lid handle design and the clips that keep the legs attached to the bowl. I have an older 18.5 that doesn’t have the leg clips and every time I move it I have to hold the front leg to keep it from falling out of the socket. The lid bail on the back of the kettle is handy instead of the hook inside the lid. As far as performance, the Weber 22.5 kettle can’t be beat with the exception of the 18.5 kettle, which I like better. But for a family of four or more you really need the larger 22.5 to cook on. The new colors the Mastertouch comes in are a nice change. The Spring Green is my favorite and the Ivory is my wife’s. The Ivory with the black handles and black ash pot looks very classy while the Spring Green just pops with color and demands to be paid attention to and used (it’s my favorite).

However I’m not impressed with the quality control. Both the Spring Green and the Ivory upon arrival had issues. The Spring Green had two 2” scratches on the lid down to the metal and the Ivory had a smashed leg from the bowl resting on it and the bowl has some scuff marks from the leg that won’t come off. I contacted customer service and explained the problems, sent pictures of the damage and was promptly sent out the replacements. I commend Weber on their excellent customer service. But then the new lid arrived, no scratches or dings but the vent wheel is so loose and sloppy, I feel like I’m spinning the wheel on that game show that comes on at 6:30 at night. I guess I will pony up and just order a new vent so I can get the proper bolt to mount it back on. 

I ordered an Ivory 18.5 from Germany (as that’s the only place you can pick those up). I hope I don’t have any issues with it as it will be a nightmare to get any fixed. I would still recommend a Weber simply because the customer service is so great and when you get a good one out of the box it will last you forever.

text: I bought this grill a few months ago and it has performed exactly as I had hoped. The grill is consistent at providing even heat across the entire surface with one exception. One of the drawbacks I noticed is when the wind picked up the grill had difficulty getting up to temperature and the wind would actually blow out the flames if set to medium or lower. The other design problem I had with the grill is the ease of mobility. The instructions tell you to lock the folding shelf in place and use that as a handle but I would strongly discourage this unless you want to damage your grill. The folding shelf is not made to handle the weight of the grill and a propane tank. If you lift it by this then the shelf will slide out of it's locked position and damage the shelf while also dropping your grill which may damage the more fragile components like the ignition system. Since I roll my grill around quite a bit I have to grab it by the frame which is much lower and awkward so this can be a major annoyance. Other than these two problems I have experienced, I am satisfied with the grill's performance and hope that it will last for many years.

I have had my eye on the Weber kettle as long as I can remember but the cost always left me apprehensive. I was recently surprised when I found a previous year model on clearance and the offer was too good to pass up. I owned the smaller version for years and while I have zero complaints overall it's not something you can cook for a crowd on. The 22" Original Kettle Premium has enough elbow room (more specifically wings, legs and thighs) to cook for family and friends.

The biggest surprise out of the box was the heft and build quality of the components. I expected lightweight materials and flimsy legs, handles, etc.. What I got was a heavy duty, ruggedly built grill that will last a lifetime. There is a reason that Weber has the reputation it does. It's quality.  

The 22" size is perfect for offset cooking so cuts that require low and slow can get the perfect cook you are looking for. Toss in a chunk of wood every now and then and you essentially have a smoker. While my electric smoker has the ease of 'set it and forget it' it doesn't hold a candle to the authentic smoked character that the Weber provides. Charcoal adds flavor that you just don't get in other cooking methods. 

If you have been on the fence with a Weber Kettle of any size or model I would enthusiastically encourage you to do so. I never thought a simple charcoal grill would have so much impact on my day to day grilling and help me to become a better pit master in such a short time. Try it! You'll love it too!

title: Great Kettle Especially for the Price
text:
I purchased this 22" master touch kettle from home depot back in May 2019. I have a WSM 14.5" charcoal smoker and love it, but I typically grill with my Weber Genesis gas grill so this was my first time using a charcoal kettle. The one touch cleaning system and the ash catcher are great (I've used the basic kettle that only has an ash catch pan and it's a pain/less safe, especially when it's windy). I love that this version has the lid holder (the premium version only has a hook on the inside. I wouldn't mind having the hook also on the lid so you can use both holders. Sometimes I feel the hook would work well when starting your chimney and the current lid holder is great when flipping your food. 

The accessories work well overall. Once my chimney is ready and I pour the coals into the charcoal baskets, I set my chimney on the shelf on the bottom of the kettle on it's side until it cools. The charcoal baskets allow you to easily push them together for direct heat v. put them on the sides, using the sides as direct zones and the center as an indirect zone (this is primarily how I cook, I sear on direct heat and cook the meat through on indirect heat if needed). The main grate has the flip up sides which are great for adding coals during a longer cook or adding wood chips/chunks. The grate also has the center removable section for the custom cooking accessories. This is nice for flexibility, but I'd like to see clips or something to keep this attached to the base grate when you aren't using the center cooking accessories. I like to hang my grate on the kettle when using my chimney and the center grate being loose is a pain. The additional raised/elevate grate works well for burger buns, etc. 

Overall this is hard to beat for $200-$220. I'm used to paying $600 or more for a weber gas grill and love the cheaper charcoal option for cookouts on nicer days. If you have a deck or patio, buy a separate grilling mat to catch drippings. Otherwise this is a great kettle.

title: Almost perfect
text:
I bought my Spirit II E-310 as a replacement for an older grill from a different manufacturer who no longer had grate and flavorizer bar replacement available for my model.

On the whole, it's a great grill.  Very even heat distribution.  Classic solid Weber construction.  Looks great.  The composite plastic on the sides keeps you from burns if you accidentally brush the sides with your hand.  It's still hot but not like metal sides would be.

The iGrill3 mount is very handy and seemless looking.  I got one so I wouldn't accidentally burn my meats.  I assume it also would work with the iGrill2 which is a magnetic mount and it has the two stainless side tables.  

I only have two minor quibbles.  First, the knob throw is only a half turn from start/max to minimum intensity.  That means when trying to get all three burners the same intensity being off a bit means more than I'd like, so you have to be precise when setting them.

Second, the spring loaded gas gauge can be a bit "sticky."  It's useful to give your propane tank a bounce every few uses to get a more accurate reading.

But on the whole it's a wonderful, solidly built grill that cooks everything wonderfully.
