title: Quality Could be Better
text:
I bought this first through Amazon. It arrived with broken pieces of the grill cover/lid, which I attribute to Weber's decision to employ cheap plastic composite material to save money. Many similar reviews on Amazon about this problem, which could have been avoided had Weber used better (albeit slightly more expensive) material. You get what you pay for I suppose.

Overall, however, the grill does its main job proficiently: it cooks food well - via both direct and indirect heating methods. The ceramic coated cast iron grates are a nice touch and relatively easy to keep clean. I purchased the iGrill accessory (toy) and regret it. A waste of money unless you're cooking giant roasts all the time. Not needed whatsoever (i.e., doesn't work well) for burgers, fish, chicken, steaks and dogs, since they're too thin to consistently get accurate temperature readings. More tried and true methods such as keeping track of time to rotate the food work better IMO. 

I do enjoy using it. It does its job. I'm used to if and will keep it. That said, I think I overpaid for what I got given the quality issues. I'm sure there are other grills out there that provide more bang for the buck.

title: Longtime Griller, finally bought the Cadillac
text:
I always wanted a Weber grill. So for starters, I may be a little biased. As a Father’s Day gift in 1991, we bought my father a Genesis for Father’s Day. It was handed down to my brother and he still uses it to this day. I would consider myself to be way above average as a griller. I’ve been through two grills since being a homeowner, one used and one new (approx 10 years). Neither hold up to the quality that is my Weber. I also own a Kamado style grill, however I will not compare that to the weber as it is charcoal. As far as propane grills go, this is the best brand you can get. Remember you get what you pay for. My second grill was ok, however a powerful wind gust blew it over head over heels and dented it severely. I thoroughly clean my grilling apparatus 2x per year, and yet they still rusted. The Weber quality is clear as day. It is heavier. It is sturdier. The temp control is so sensitive that I recommend firing it up before your first cook just so you can get an understanding of 1) how hot this can get and 2) how you can micromanage the temperature down to every 5 degrees. 10 year warranty. They stand behind their grill. My next grill, if I ever need one, will be Weber. 
I’ve done 4 cooks on it and am very satisfied. If you can splurge on the cost, it will be money well spent. Why spend $200 every 5 years when you can spend $400 once? Finally some background on my grilling experience. I’ve done pork butts, ribs, steak, chicken, fish, brisket. Cold smoke, high sear, 6 racks of ribs at once. Believe me when I tell you, I’ve done al of those and will be trying them at some point on this Weber.

title: Just the right size!
text:
Easy to assemble, clear instructions, but give your self plenty of room to spread out the parts, there are a "fair amount" of screws and washers and assorted small items. The actual assembly took only about an hour using a power driver (hand thread all screws to make sure they are not cross threaded before using the driver to tighten). Unpacking is another thing though, Wow! every part is surrounded by cardboard or foam wrap, it another hour just to unpack, but everything was in perfect shape. This grill is quite sturdy!

Lights easily, starts to heat well but does take more time than I'm used too to reach 550 degrees (15 min.), grates are fabulous, nice sear marks. non stick and super easy to clean. Temperature control is good but I noticed that the back is a little hotter than the front, if you add items from front to back, it works out very well, the front will be done about the same time as the back. 

I've tried all the basics, burgers, hot dogs, brats, chicken breasts and even grilled zucchini (a first and it was excellent). Everything turned out very well, the chicken was the best I ever made in fifty years of grilling and I look forward to trying different recipes.  My old grill was 30 years old and was now too large for a reduced family size. Amazingly, this small grill does have enough room to cook for a small group, a dozen burgers and some Brats or hot dogs will fit. 

Love the folding shelf ! But I think you will have to be very careful if you have move the grill a long distance on rough terrain for winter storage, should have another handle 

All in all, I'm quite happy with this purchase and would highly recommend the Sprit II 210E to anyone interested in a smaller footprint grill. Treat your self to the Weber Tank Sock for a classier look !

title: So far so good, but I've only it for a month
text:
I wish companies would wait longer before asking customers for a review, especially on something like this; something used intermittently.  In any case, the several times I've used my Weber E-210, it has done just fine.   I replaced a 5yo, rusted out [everything under the lid in the hot box was gone] Char Broil 4-burner with this Weber 2-burner.

I assembled the grill myself and all went well.  I appreciate the nice instructions.  All parts were in the box and it took about 2 hours to complete.  I picked up the black lid as that is all the store had on the shelf.  Any of the other non-black lids were special order through the store website; however, I needed the grill sooner rather than later, so black lid it was.

I like the hanging propane tank gauge.  Only time will tell how well it holds up, (no pun intended).  The 2-burner grill area is just fine for my family of 3.  If you need more than 4-5 servings of food, I suggest looking at the E-310 or larger.

I like the folding shelves.  The store display made it look like only 1 shelf folded, but having both fold is a nice feature.  I don't need a side burner so this works out well.

The only rear downside I've experienced so far is a hot lid handle near the ends where it attaches to the lid.  The center is good to grab.  I've reminded myself several times, on the hand and arm, that the outsides of the handle can be hot. I'm sure with time, I'll learn how to navigate the handle to not touch the hot parts.

Overall, I am happy with my grill.  If Weber stands behind their 10 year warranty, that will make it that much fabulous.  I just need more on-time with the grill, so I hope the weather cooperates this summer.

title: Overall Impression
text:
I am very pleased with the Spirit II.  

Positives:  

It cooks evenly - no hot or cold spots.
Both burners cook the same.

It gets very hot.  (Some reviews I had read prior to purchasing this grill said it did not get up to temperature.)  In fact, I have to have the burners turned way down, about 3/4 or more, to keep it from going over 400 degrees.

Temp setting is very sensitive.  Moving the knob just one line will change the temp by about 5 or 10 degrees. 

Preferences (I can't really call these negatives, just a wish list):

I miss the wheels on the left side.  I understand I am suppose to pick it up like a wheelbarrow, but the wheels were easier and more convenient for moving the grill.

I miss the fold-up tray extension on the left side, like I had on my 20-year-old Genesis.

I miss the old-fashioned igniter that I had on my old Genesis.  It did not need a battery.  Just push the button to create a spark.  It never failed.

It is difficult to see exactly where the temperature knobs are lined up because of their vehicle angle.  I actually have to bend down or squat down to see where they are set.  On my old Genesis, the knobs  were sitting horizontally, so were much easier to read.

My biggest complaint is the design and texture of the grates that make them really hard to clean.  They are flat and bumpy, and have a bar that runs through them from left to right.  This makes it impossible to use anything other than a wire brush to clean them.  Wire brushes are hazardous as the wire bristles can break off, stick to the grates, and get on your food, causing you to ingest them and getting lodged in your throat or digestive tract.  
These grates will not come clean using the new wooden spatulas scrapers. Nor will they come clean using a stainless steel scraper.  
I could use both these tools on my Genesis grates as they were shaped like a triangle.
In fact, does Weber offer a different set of grates similar in design as those I described on my 20-year-old Genesis?  If so. I would consider changing them out.

Overall, I do love this new grill.  It cooks wonderfully.  It is obviously well made.  And after having researched other grills, I am pleased and satisfied that I chose the Weber Spirit II.

Thank you for the opportunity to share my perspective.

text:
We bought the grill anticipating the quality we'd heard so much about. For the most part we've experienced that with the grilling characteristics. The attention to detail on most features are great... until I go to move the grill each time we use it. We keep the grill covered and against the house until we use it, then we move it about 8-10 feet away from the house further out on our deck. The left fold-down table, intended to be used to lift and roll the grill worked marginally the first 3-4 times (worth a 4-star rating if it had not got worse) and has since gone downhill to become unusable as the means to maneuver the grill. It's unfortunate that moving the grill comes before I actually use the grill because I start out frustrated before I can begin grilling. That small detail starts our frequent grilling experience (the actual grilling I'm very pleased with) out on the wrong foot each time.

I would recommend this grill with the caveat that, if you intend to move the grill around at all, you'll need to add a thick washer to each peg that the left table hooks on, and tighten it down, which in effect negates the easy fold-ability of that left table.

title: Rust killed grill in 3 years
text:
I need to start to say that my love of Weber all started helping my father use his charcoal Weber grill. As a kids I was amazed at how good the food would taste with that grill and how much my dad loved to use it. I grew and after college I bought my dad the first Weber gas grill. He loved that as well and I bought one as well. My original Genesis lasted me 14 years, only ever replacing the parts that were supposed to wear out. I had a Weber cover that sometimes went on and others it did not. My point is it sat in the elements in the North East and never failed me.  I actually gave it to my neighbor who still uses it. I now wish I kept it.
3 years ago I decided to replace my Weber Genesis for a Spirit E-310 which was a big 's spurge for me. I love the grill, the way it makes the food taste and its performance. Love it until this spring. When I cleaned the grill for spring use the large door came loose and then came off due to rust at the bottom. I used it anyway and it did not affect the performance of the grill. 

I still have the sticker that states a 10 year limited warranty. Weber has always had EXCELLENT customer service so I called. The Weber representative said that the frame was not covered for 10 years, only 2 years. When I bought the grill I would have never thought in a million years that this would totally rust out in 2 years. 
When I discussed the situation the Weber representative they told me I could order a new base for $87.00 shipped. I bought it and tonight tried to install it and unfortunately the rust issue is far worse than I anticipated. There is literally nothing on side or back to attach the new base to. The back and one side are severely rusted. 

So to sum it up-I spent well over $500.00 to buy the new grill 3 years ago. The base side and back have totally rusted out and I have spent $87.00 on a part that cannot be installed to fix the problem. I'm going to call Weber tomorrow to see how much essentially the 3 sides of the grill are to replace it all.

In my entire life with Weber I have never encountered mechanical or rust issues-ever. I cannot explain how disappointed I am over this entire situation. We make a modest living and this grill was a reach and expected more.  I may not ever buy Weber again.

I wanted a quality grill, and was willing to pay a premium for it since it came with a great warranty. So I bought the E210. I don't grill that often, just occasionally. I love the convenience of turning on the grill, having it come straight up to temp for burnoff, then scrape and cook in about 10 minutes. It maintains a steady, safe temperature without flare ups.
  Even though my family is moving away from red meat, there are still a wide variety of things to cook, and this grill makes it easy. The compact size is perfect for our needs. We don't do entertaining and parties, so the E210 is just right. And if we did entertain, it really wouldn't be a problem with this grill. Love the look and function. Would recommend watching an assembly walk through video before assembling. Instructions are pretty good, but there were a couple of things I had to redo during the process. title: Cooks Fine but Wish It Was Like My Old One
text:
I had a 22" grill for over 20 years. The lower air vent blades had burned and rusted to the point where they no longer could control the air flow, were rusted beyond replaceability, and I finally decided to replace it with the current model of what I've been using, the Premium. After assembling it and finding some annoyances, most significant, the loss of the "bail" lid holder, I returned it and exchanged it for the Master Touch. I've been using it for a month now and I'm reluctantly trying to accept it because it's as good as I'm going to get. Still, I find several things that are, for no reason I can see, have been changed from my older model, and make it more inconvenient to use. They may seem small and insignificant, but they're annoying.

1. Things have been turned around. The lower air vent handle used to be on the left and is now on the right where I always seem to have something in the way when I want to adjust it.

2. The handle on the lid has been turned 90 degrees relative to the upper vent and thermometer so now I have to stand to the side of the grill rather than in front in order to raise the lid and "park" it in the bail. 

3. The "hole in the grill" is just plain dumb! I've wired it in place so it doesn't fall out when I remove the grill to load in the charcoal. I'll probably weld it. It would make more sense to offer the removable center as an option and make a full surface grill standard. 

I could go on and on, but really, I liked the old one better and I'm really having difficulty adjusting to the new one. But what's a Weber fan to do?

title: Great Grilling for a Small Unit
text:
I keep repeating to my wife "I feel like I've been grilling with a handicap until now". 

The Weber Spirit II E-210 has been everything I wanted. It didn't look as fancy to me as some other grills, and I'm glad I got over that. The Weber creates such an even heat distribution that it's a dream to grill on. It heats up fast, get's the grates hot and ready, and retains it's heat as I open and close it to add food. I've seen mentions that "the flames don't reach the food!" and this is irrelevant. The grates add the grill marks to your food, not the flames. Flames over-cook your food, but the Weber's design keeps over-flaming from happening and let's me cook my food just how I want.

The extra heat also comes primarily out the back of the grill. This is a great design as I'm able to stand in front of my grill and be a cook, instead of trying to avoid flames and heat pockets. Do not put it right up to your home siding though, this grill needs some room behind it to vent. 

The grease tray is also a wonderful design. When the tray is full you slide it out and put in a new one. It's so simple! Yes they are over priced aluminum tray's, but they are darn convenient. 

Lastly, the weighted propane spring holder is nice to have. I've owned the grill for 2 months and have already ran through a propane tank. Either this grill uses a lot of propane, or I was severely underfilled on that propane tank. I've added 3 gallons of propane and the spring has said it's "full" for a lot longer now, so I think I had an underfilled tank before. As I'm able to just refill my tank instead of replace, it's nice to have the weighted spring that let's me know when I may be low and not ready for a heavy grilling weekend. 

Ultimately this 2-burner Weber grill has let me grill for an 8 person house party, without any issue. The grill didn't skip a beat when I loaded it up with hamburgers and hot dogs, and never created a mean flare-up from a fully loaded cooking top. I thought I had a good grill before that lasted me for years, but I would of bought a Weber 5 years ago had I known it was this good. 

If that last line sounded too cheesy, it's because I can melt cheese on a hamburger like it's an afterthought now. I'm that happy with the grill that I've become a walking Weber advertisement. I don't give a flip either, good food equals happy reviews.

text:

Have also used this with a smoker box and can smoke meat for hours with ease to get that great flavor and smell. 

Cons: The scale for the propane tank can stick a bit and isn't too helpful. Assembly was a bit challenging when I couldnt find a part. Unit came with a bent stand that was replaced by Weber.

Key reasons why you should consider this grill: intensely high heat, even heat, ease of assembly.

More and more places do not allow charcoal grills, so Weber Q at the local Home Depot was the obvious choice. I bought mine on sale along with the cart, cover and conversion propane hose for big tanks. I am impressed with how fast the grill heats up. Burgers and hot dogs grilled in no time. Flare ups, non-existent. I used to dis-like the grates, until I noticed they’re designed in a way that prevents burners from getting dirty. Still able to have awesome sear marks on chicken. Love the side tables, but hate waiting for the grates to cool to fold back into place. Cart is perfect, very(one hand) mobile, fits in the trunk of my wife’s two door Nissan, completely assembled. Love the cover, stays in place in windy weather. Haven’t used the big propane conversion line. Clean up is very easy. Don’t ignore the drip pan, it’ll build up quickly. Cart has two tool holders, wish Weber sold mini tools for smaller grills. If it’s like my other Webers, it’ll last forever. My Smokey Joe is 10+ years old. Replaced the grates once, that’s it. Back to Q, it’s awesome, who am I kidding. Does exactly what I need it to do. Take it with you, or use it at home. I’ve started using it for quick grills at home vs using the big grills. Caveat:  when you first turn on the propane, give the grill 10 or so seconds before lighting the burners.  If done too soon, the regulator will decrease the gas flow and the grill will not preheat above 250-300 degrees.
My primary complaint is placing a  propane tank on the gravity scale.  I am 70 plus years old with a reverse total shoulder replacement for my right shoulder and I do not have the strength to lift the tank straight up from the ground.  I either do not hook the tank to the scale, or have someone do it for me.  Surely Weber could have done a better design.  I skipped ease of assembly as the grill was assembled by Lowes.

Just rolling them down my old but relatively smooth driveway really took a lot of chunks out of them.  Would be better with metal wheels with rubber rims.
3. The propane bottle scale is a good idea but the tank rests directly on the axel. So the scale will not work until the tank is almost empty and lifts off of the axel. Trying to figure a way around this by using bolts to push the tank further away from the axel.
4. Finally, the entire unit is difficult to move because there are no good hand grips on the left side to lift the unit and push it.  The left sided, collapsible shelf is there, but it is too flimsy to lift the grill off the ground and push it to move or re-position it.

Have had this grill for only two months. A chef and professional cook for over 15 years I've owned and/or used a lot of propane grills, and have always appreciated Webber. The Compact size is perfect for the corner of a small deck and family of 4. The three burners with 5 distribution plates leaves two very narrow very minimal cool spots, though this thing heats up FAST and can be controlled quite accurately from 300 to 500 degrees. Putting it together wasn't as easy as many other grills, but the end result was worth the extra effort. The folding side tray is opposite the wheels and because the tray seats using a pop up key hole on a cleat screw, lifting that end always leads to the tray becoming unseated, making moving the grill very awkward (even unsafe when hot). 2 castors opposite the wheels or a simple locking pin on the tray would have made this a non-issue (WEBBER~I'll be altering mine). Lastly the upper level is such a tight fit it bows upward a bit and often unseats while grilling. And it's very narrow making it unusable for roasting veggies in a tray or even keeping a few larger steaks off the direct heat. Would have preferred a pivoting tray, this one's mostly just in the way.

Overall though this is a very good compact to midsize BBQ that I'm sure will last a very long time. Aside from two or three issues, I can't imagine anyone regretting this purchase.

The instructions that came with the Weber Grill were very easy to follow, using the lighter cubes in the charcoal containers is very easy. But, that’s not the best part. The best part is without question the ridiculously good taste of steaks and chicken that I cooked on the grill. It is so easy to fire up the charcoal, preheat the grill, put the meat on the grill, close the hood, wait 7-8 minutes, open the hood flip it over and close the hood, wait 7-8 minutes and then have high-quality restaurant tender meats. Count me in as somebody who will never go back to propane.

text: I bought my grill from Home Depot and was crushed upon opening it to find, without any evidence of damage to the shipping box, to find massive damage to the grill inside including a broken off chunk of the lid, damage to the lower half of the upper grill and a shattered grate. Weber moved into action as soon as I tweeted about the terrible find and within just a couple of days had replaced without any grief whatsoever, the grill bottom, the lid and the grates, essentially like 70% of the grill. All free, all wjth FedEx shipping and even more protected than previously. There were extra instructions to move a few pieces over to these new replacement grill lid and burner box parts and the process took no more time that really it would have been to build it in the first place. The build was easy and sensible, the design made it impossible to build things accidentally in the wrong way. The grill just feels better made than any I’ve had before. As to using it, it’s awesome. After about 8 meals on the grill in the first couple of weeks, it’s an A+. The service and support I’ve already received give me great confidence about the future with this grill.

title: This is a no brainer purchase.
text:
I had to buy a grill to serve as my main cooking device while renovating our cabin (it was gutted & had no kitchen the entire summer).  This little guy blew my mind.  I had a Silver Genesis for 13 years before buying my new Genesis so I knew I was buying a Weber.  This grill has been a lifesaver.  I literally do all my cooking on it.  Breakfast on the griddle and all the normal grilling tasks on the grates.  I had NO expectations that this thing would do a good job but it really has.  On my big Webers I could control the temperature and cook indirectly because of the size so I figured with this being small I wouldn't be able to control things as well.  Boy was I wrong.  Car camping feels like cheating it cooks so well.  Cleaning it is quick and easy because you simply lift the grates and wipe it out, the drip pan helps a lot too because I cook a lot of chicken thighs which produce a lot of fat which runs right into the removable drip pan.  Lastly, this think is so portable I find myself taking it everywhere.  I can easily get through a week of camping with a couple little fuel bottles which means I don't have to lug a huge propane tank and trip over the hose all day.
Just get it, you'll have it forever and each time you use it you will find something else you'll like about it.

I could have gotten a $200 special, and probably be fine, but I didn't want to buy a grill and have it be flimsy and rust out after a year. I picked up this one at my local HD, and I opted to put it together myself so I could get to know every square inch of the thing. Taking my time, it took about 2 hours to assemble it. It wasn't that bad, the instructions were easy. Everything fit together seamlessly! You can REALLY see the material quality this way. Everything has a high quality finish. Even the screws are coated to prevent rust. I also added the igrill3 to help me with my "man card" issue so there is no guessing on food temperatures. I put it together by 1pm Sunday, did the 20 minute "burn off" and prepared chicken and shrimp for my family. The grill got up to temp faster than I expected. I keep reading that these grills are designed to work best with the hood down, so I followed that order. Everything came out perfect! (well, almost perfect, the chicken could have used juuuust a little more seasoning) Temperature was easy to control. Do yourself a favor, and get the igrill3! And don't forget the regular Weber app, lots of good info on there. I doubt other cheaper manufacturers have this much support and information that Weber does. Kudos to Weber for making such a high quality product and amazing support and information! My only issue is that I will now get addicted to grilling, and will wind up buying a bigger Weber! THANK YOU WEBER!!

title: One Heck of a Grill
text:
My purchase requirements:

1) Solid build (stainless steel shell, iron grates, etc.)

2) Warranty (wanted a company to stand behind its product)

3) Easy to use (quick to start, fast to heat to 500 degrees, easy to clean, etc.)

4) Good value (didn't need to be cheap, but my budget can't afford a $2,500 grill)

I did a few hours of Internet research to try and find the brand and model that met the 4 criteria.  I zeroed in on the Spirit II bc the feedback I read seemed to hit all of my requirements.  

I have been using it now for about 2 months...here is what I learned:

1) The build is rock solid.  I roll it in and out of the covered deck and does so with ease (not feeling like it is going to fall apart:)))).)

2) Can't say anything about the warranty other than what we all know...10 years.  I feel good that they will stand behind the product.  I called their customer service to ask if I could use a stainless steel brush on the iron grates.  The service rep was professional, timely and knowledgeable.

3) No kidding, it is up to 500 degrees in minutes w all three burners on.  Further, I use the brush on the grates each time and cleaning is easy.  We have taken the grates and bars off once for cleaning...all very easy.

4) So far, my feeling is that I paid a little premium for the Spirit (as compared to other brands), but the product is delivering.  That is all I can ask from a brand...deliver on your promises.

I cook for a family of 6...steaks, chicken, burgers, hot dogs, etc...it is big enough for us even with three teenage boys.  Happy grilling!!!!

text:

Wasn't worried about a large ash catcher, I have no issue with the ash pan.  Didn't need a lid thermometer since those aren't accurate. I know how to arrange charcoal for zones, so didn't need separators.  I have mitts so didn't need a top grate with hinges.

title: One significant design flaw
text: The changes between the Spirit I and Spirit II are pretty minor, I don't mind the open air design, and I would prefer 4 spinner wheels instead of two big wheels so that it can be moved without risking tipping something over.  My bigger gripe is the obvious design flaw of having the one foldable table be on the LEFT side, so that when you move the grill you have to lift the LEFT table, potentially causing it to pop off as though you planned on folding it.  That's a major annoyance and a totally unforced error as the right side could just as easily been the folding side.

title: Worth It!
text:
I have owned a basic Weber kettle grill for most of my adult life. I like the basic models because I hate paying for options I don't use or need. The only reason I had to replace grills was due to moving or my negligence; mainly dropping the lid (multiple times) which is why I had to buy a new grill. 

I skeptically decided to spend a little extra money Master Touch primarily for the lid holder. Spoiler alert, best decision on my part.
- The lid holder is a much better and secure design and already saved me a couple times.
- The lid handle has a heat shield which is very nice, for obvious reasons, and also helps with not dropping the lid.
- The removable center grill is a nice option that I never thought I'd use, but I was wrong. It's fantastic for maintaining heat for indirect grilling and I use their Gourmet BBQ gridle insert for "grilled" vegetables with the smoke flavor. 
- The temp gauge is another feature I never thought I use but is now the key when slow cooking to maintaining that perfect temp. 
- The ash catcher attachment is better and easier to use than my previous models, but I'm not sure if this design is now incorporated on all Webber kettle grills with ash catchers. Either way, it's much easier to use compared to the insert and turn method. 
- Assembly is typical and not too hard when you follow the instructions. I however used my two steps forward, one step back and then read the instructions method which still only took 20 minutes.

Bottom line, the Master touch is well worth the money.

title: Practical Grill with Very Useful Extra Features.
text: I bought this grill model primarily due to the ash clean out method. The ashes can easily be dumped into the ash catcher by opening the bottom vents and moving them back and forth. It requires a little more action on my part to get more ash past the bottom vents and into the catcher, but this is no big problem. Regardless, it is a much better ash removal system that the aluminum plate method which always proved a bit of a problem. I would remove the plate by bending it a little bit to get past the clamps and this always produced an ash cloud no matter how careful I tried to be. I also like the simplicity of this grill. I for one do not need an outdoor kitchen appliance. The only extras are highly practical: small, semi-circular unattached stainless steel grate (about 10 inch wide and five inch high); good for keeping hot dogs or other smaller pieces of meat warm, but off the cooking grate.  The thermometer on the lid is another nice extra feature. I could maybe have used the model with the tray to place a cooking dish on; but, other than that, the model does everything I need it to do.

title: I LOVE my new Weber grill!!!
text:
I’ve had my Weber Spirit II grill now for about a month. It is easily the best grill I have ever owned, bar none! I elected to do self assembly at home which wasn’t a terrible ordeal. Packaging was top notch. Full assembly in approximately 2 hours. The instructions were very well illustrated and the parts well organized to facilitate an easily assembly. 

The magic, however, is when you turn on the grill and cook your first meal. I initially had issue with getting the temperature up above 250 degrees F. I disconnected the propane line and reconnected and that solved the problem. On the next ignition, I was up to 400 degrees F in minutes. This grill gets HOT!!! I was cooking my first round of beef tenderloins at 600 degrees F and the end result was awesome!
I have since cooked chicken, pork, flank steak and burgers and all have turned out perfect! 

The primary reason for going with this years Weber Spirit II was because of the crazy number of positive reviews online. To add in a 10 year warranty made it a no brainer. I was originally going to go with the Weber Genesis II, however, I didn’t think that the cost of feature set warranted it for my personal needs. I’m your average weekend griller and just wanted a solid, basic grill to achieve my needs. The Spirit II has given me just that. I opted for the 3 burner offering. Now, I get excited to fire up this grill as often as I can. 

This is my first Weber purchase and I have been extremely pleased to date. Weber also has a pretty cool app that provides access to your personal grill, recipe ideas and other miscellaneous items. It’s very user friendly and offers just one more way to get the most out of your Weber grill. 

For anyone on the fence about purchasing the Weber Spirit II grill, just do it. I promise you won’t be disappointed. My philosophy is that you get what you pay for. Sure, I paid a little more for the Weber compared to some of the other offerings from other brands, but I honestly feel that I got the most bang for my buck with this one. Happy grilling to you all!!!

title: Hendrix had his Fender; I have my Weber
text: Got this from the family as a Father's Day gift this year, a friendly nudge that my 17-year old Weber Silver B needed to be put to pasture. At first I thought it might be too small, but it has been absolutely fine. I am the king of a family of five and there is plenty of room to grill meats and vegetables for all of us at the same time. The grill of Silver B was rectangular, with the 3 burners running horizontally; the E-310's burners go top to bottom, which I think makes more sense. It allows for grilling wider foods when grilling indirectly. This grill is definitely a bargain; the grilling area  is only marginally smaller than other Weber models that are $300 more expensive. The one thing I miss is that on the Silver B had fold-out tables on each side, giving me lots of room for bowls, utensils, etc. I don't think any of the newer models have them, though. I would suggest bringing them back. One other small comment is that the hooks for the utensils are a little small and the utensils fall off the side of the grill a little more easily than they used to. But these are all small grievances. This is a great grill at a bargain price and I'm looking forward to making many masterpieces on it.

text: I love my Weber grill. It does a great job grilling, heats up face and the grates are nice and sturdy.  I wish that Weber would start including side burners for keeping sauces warm or cooking up a side dish.  Also, the side tray/tables do not fold down; a huge design flaw because it makes moving the grill to another location beyond cumbersome if you have to carry it.  The biggest problem is the propane tank and gauge connector hook.  Clearly this was not designed with women in mind.  It takes quite a bit of shoulder strength to lift a full propane tank onto that little gauge hook....not cool.  I can’t do it myself.  It would be easier if the grill had a full bottom instead of that hole cut out, for women anyway.  Instead of having to jigger the heavy tank onto the gauge (which you must do otherwise the tank sits on the ground thanks to the big cut out), couldn’t you find a way to connect the gauge to the tank? I know it works by weight, but trying to maneuver that inside the tiny cabinet space is just awful.  Love the way it cooks but for what they charge it should be much easier installing a propane tank. The gas line connector is fine and very easy; I am referring to the gauge that keeps track of the amount of propane.  I would definitely recommend this grill to strong men or ladies who have them, but not to single women.  Even the guy from the stor had trouble  getting the tank positioned correctly on that hook.

text:

The lowest temperature I get is around 600 F with the burners running at the lowest gas setting on the knobs.  If I turn the knob below "low", the burner shuts off.  To achieve lower temperature, I must turn one or more burners off which means the temperature distribution is lousy, hot on the burner that is on, colder on the burner that is off.  

This means practically, I have no temperature control because the grill is running extremely hot even at its lowest setting.  Which means burnt food on the outside and raw on the inside. This is a deal breaker.

title: I'm convinced...Weber is better
text:
After replacing grills every few years that really never cooked consistently to begin with, all I can say is Wow!  I've only had this grill for a couple of months, but what a difference.  Everything I've cooked on it has come out perfect.  No more half cooked/over cooked items from uneven heat.  My family has even made compliments on the quality of the burgers and chicken, the only difference was the grill, the recipe has remained the same.

The fold out shelf is very convenient when needed, and simple to get out of the way for storage.  Only two suggestions.

1. The accessories hooks on the side are too shallow.  Anything I have hanging on them gets knocked off every time I remove the cover.

2. I struggle with finding a good place to hold the grill when I want to move it around.  I hesitate to use the folding shelf.  It's sturdy enough but I know it's not meant to be a handle.

I look forward to seeing how it stands up over the years.  From the construction quality I think it should do so very well.

text:

The two areas i feel could have been better are the wheels, which are held on by small cotter pins, and the fold down side “table”. I have had the wheels come off when moving the grill, which just shouldn’t happen. For the foldable side, it has these guide holes that go over some bolts to hold it up; the metal is fairly thin so it can flex and not stay on those rails/guides. This is more of an issue when moving the bbq as the foldable side is also the side that you have to lift when moving the bbq (it’s opposite the wheels) and it too easily misses getting locked in due to the folding ability.

Other than those two issues, the bbq has been great and has a good build quality.

title: Retour à la base
text:
Après 25 ans de cuisson au propane, j'ai fait le saut à la cuisson au charbon de bois! C'est un changement stimulant et amusant! J'ai acheté ce modèle car je ne voulais pas investir un gros montant alors que je n'étais pas certain d'aimer ce type de cuisson. De plus je voulais un appareil assez léger pour le déplacer du patio supérieur au patio inférieur sans forcer et sans l'endommager.

Acheté il y a 6 semaines avec quelques accessoires (cheminée d'allumage, racloir à cendres, grille gourmet en fonte, plat rond en fonte, housse et assiettes d'aluminium).

Assemblage facile (environ 15 minutes). Allumage du charbon de bois très facile avec la cheminée d'allumage. Il suffit de déterminer quelle est la quantité optimale de morceaux de charbon, ce qui prend quelques essais. Cuisson directe et indirecte utiles. C'est facile de maintenir une température stable pendant >1 heure avec une seule charge de briquettes. Peu d'ajustements pour le maintien de la température mais avec l'usage des entrées d'air supérieure et inférieure, on y parvient assez bien. Thermomètre assez juste. Le livre "La Bible du Barbecue" de S.Raichlen m'a été d'une grande utilité et m'a permis de progresser en ne faisant pas de faux pas. 

Bref, j'utilise le Master Touch 22 po de Weber en complément de mon BBQ au propane. Je m'amuse à fond et j'ai toujours hâte au prochain repas!

RDes de Lévis, Québec

title: Very smart design!!!
text:
I am not ordinarily in the habit of leaving product reviews, but occasionally a product comes along that is so well-made that it would not be fair if such a product were to go unmentioned. This is such a product.

My hat is off to the person or team that designed this grill. Such smart design!!

Start with the cooking grates:  they are porcelain-enameled cast-iron so they build up a nice heat such that you can get those beautiful grate lines on your burgers and hot dogs, and yet are easy to clean when all is said and done. Another smart-design aspect of the grates is that they do not allow drippings from the food to fall directly on to the burner thus avoiding the potential for clogging the small holes where the propane burns.

One should know that while the grill appears small, there is plenty of surface area to cook upon. I can easily get a dozen or more burgers cooking simultaneously, or two or three dozen hot dogs/bratwursts.

The fold-in side tables are such a smart idea! They are covered and protected (by the lid) during transport where they also help to stabilize the cooking grates, yet provide an instant work space when you're ready to grill.

The bottom half of the grill is bowl-shaped with an opening at the bottom. This bowl design channels drippings to the center whereupon they fall through the opening and into a catch pan which accommodates disposable drip pans. If you need to clean the interior of the grill, there is adequate space between the burner and the grill wall to allow you to wipe down the grill wall. Again, smartly designed.

Let me conclude by noting that I bought this grill for the purpose of tailgating at my son's AAU baseball games. I also bought the portable cart that goes with it (another great product by the way). I wanted to be able to cook a burger for him and any of his teammates who were hungry. Long story short, I used this grill weekend after weekend to feed my son and his team. It performed like a champion and I was able to easily cook enough burgers to feed the team between games.

Simply put, I love this grill. Well done, Weber!!

title: Defective Hose, & not for all propane tanks.
text:
The hose/regulator part was defective after 2 weeks, and Weber replaced it, although it took 1+ weeks to arrive, so I bought another in the meantime.  

After I replaced the propane tank, the hardware store gave me a tank that had a forward-positioned propane faucet and not the normally side positioned one.  So, when I attached the smaller hose provided for my model (and sent by Weber), gas leaked when I turned on the faucet.   So who controls the Blue Rhino tanks being sold - properly, for the right model grill?   Or does the consumer have to know the above incompatibility.  I exchanged it at the hardware store.

For an average consumer, grills are a fire hazard, and this grill is not perfectly designed, just cost-effective for all buyer and seller.  Of course, use with precaution. Always turn off the propane tank (so gas cannot flow into the grill unintentionally), or a child could turn on the grill knobs (which are fun and easy to turn) and let gas leak into the grill, without actually pushing on the ignition button to light the gas.

title: Finally, my third Weber Kettle Charcoal Grill
text:
I already owned a Weber Genesis 1000 gas grill and wanted to get a charcoal grill to go along with it. It turns out that my neighbor was replacing his Weber Kettle with a gas grill and had put the Kettle out to the curve. I asked him about it and he said that I could have it. I brought it home and fixed it up with new parts and used it for a few years before giving it to my cousin who was looking for a charcoal grill of his own.

I spotted another Weber Kettle outside a neighbors house and inquired about it. Sure enough, I brought that one home and fixed it up. I ended up taking it to my shop so that my guys could use it for making burgers and hotdogs. After I sold the shop, I left the Kettle with the new owner and again I was left without one of my own.

Years went by and recently I was able to make an opportunity buy to get a brand new Weber Original Kettle Premium Charcoal Grill. As I put it together I noticed many improvements in the new design. The built in ash catcher now snaps into place as opposed to old twist and lock design. The lid handle now has a heat shield and is bolted on, where before it was welded to the lid. The kettle bottom handles now have hooks molded into them for holding utensils. The addition of a thermometer is a welcome feature for keeping an eye on cooking temperatures. The hinged grill grate is a convenience that allows you to add more charcoal to each side without disturbing the main cooking area.

I am very with my Weber grills and would highly recommend them to anyone interested in a getting a grill for barbecuing whether it is gas or charcoal. My Weber collection has grown through the years although I replaced the Genesis 1000 with a Spirit E-210. I currently own Weber Performer SSP Touch-N-Go, Weber Spirit E-210 Gas Grill, Weber Smokey Mountain Cooker Smoker 18", Weber Original Kettle Premium Charcoal Grill 22" and a Smokey Joe.

title: Love my Weber Kettle!
text:
I bought a small Weber Kettle in 1991, and used it for about a year, until I backed over it with my car!  That Christmas, my dad bought me a Weber Original Kettle to replace the one I killed. He said he bought me the big one, so I could see it better behind the car!

 Since 1992, I used that Kettle to cook everything, including burgers, steaks, hot dogs, fish, vegetables, and briskets.  I loved that Kettle so much, in 2007, I bought a small Kettle to take to the beach, picnics, and camping trips. 

  The Kettle my dad gave me finally rusted through in 2018, but had always been stored outside, uncovered, in rain, snow, hail, sleet, cold, and blistering heat. It had been blown over in strong winds so many times, I have lost count.  The small Kettle I bought in 2007, still has the original grates and looks brand new. 

Today, my daughter’s boyfriend surprised me with a new 22” Original Kettle, to replace the old one I had had for over 25 years. I’m 50 now, and as well as these Weber Kettles are built, I expect this one to last well beyond my grilling days!!

text:
We ordered our Spirit II E-210 after doing a lot of review reading and research.  This grill and the bigger 310 version seem to have some of the best reviews out there. He apologized and overnighted us a replacement lid. We were using our grill the very next day.  I’m very pleased with how this company treated us.  
	We have had the grill for several weeks now, and loving it.  I’ve never been much of a griller, Just the occasional hamburgers, or hotdogs, but decided to try some steaks. title: Is it a grill or is it a blast furnace for food?
text:
I like my grills hot, the hotter the grill the faster my food cooks. For fragile foods that need lower temperature I still want an ultra hot sear temperature so I can get that grill char on the surface. You ignite this thing and leave it for five minutes on full blast and when you open it up you wonder if you’re looking inside of a grill or a blast furnace. 

I’ve been grilling since I was 7 years old. Started on an old Weber coal dome then went to a small propane grill from a knock off brand to a massive grill. Then I moved out of my parents house and needed a grill at my own place, not too small not too big. This grill is just right.

Where it really excels is in searing and high temperature cooking. I got this grill about a month ago and about a month ago is the first time I myself have been able to get reliable grill sear marks day in and day out. 

The build quality is what you expect from Weber, built like a tank and made to last. 

I use a grill cover on mine and recommend anyone buying one get a grill cover right off the bat, there’s a lot of electronics in these grills these days and no matter how many times the manual says “Electronics are sealed against water ingress” you will get problems eventually! 

It has a 10 year warranty so I know I made a good investment and also know because I bought from a company that produces their product domestically.

title: Not Quite What It Could/Should Be for the Money
text:
After 13 or so years of solid useI had to lay my previous Spirit E-310 to rest. It was a sad moment for us. It was truly a member of our family. So I decided to purchase another based on how WELL our previous was built and how LONG it lasted. I again, like I did previous, purchased the newer Spirit II form a "big Box" store because I wanted one that I could put together myself right out of the box. I personally feel like that is part of the overall experience and there is no better way to really get to know your grill than when you have a hand in giving it life. Or, I just have a ton of time on my hands. Here are a few observations that may or may not help you in deciding if this is the right grill for you. Outside of the basics, here are a few Pros & Cons from my camera angle...

Pros: 
1) Easy to assemble - took about an hour. 
2) Low Profile Lid - I dig it.
3) 2 Stainless Steel Shelves -munch better than the older plastic ones
4) Large Control Knobs
5) Electronic Ignition - although it doesn't ignite right away from some reason.
6) Flame Bar & Flavorizer Design & Layout.
7) 10 Year Warranty
8) We are big fans of Weber in General

Cons (with some explanations for clarity):
1) Warming Rack Does Not Fit - one out of the box and the replacement rack are too wide to "easily" slide into place as the manual noted. 
2) Not Easy to Move Grill - shelve used to move grill is foldable. when you lift to move the shovel comes unhinged which is utterly annoying. 
3) Lower Box of Grill was Warped on Left Side Out of the Box - left side of lower heat box was warped and as result, grates do not sit flat and lid does not sit flush. Which in turn allows heat to escape would assume. Also could be a factor in why the warming rack doesn't fit.
4) Flames Are Inconsistent - Burns orange/yellow more than blue. 

With all that said, It's an okay grill and I can see why it comes with a 10 year warranty.
Not sure it's worth what we paid but after 10+ cooks on it, it does the job in spite of some of the concerns I may have.  It may be goos to note that we also have a pellet smoker that we use on occasion but for us and our lifestyle, gas is where its at. If you are in a position to afford it, I would recommend the Genesis line. Better quality.

After about an hour, I was finally on to step 2. Things went fairly smoothly after that until I got to the lid hanging attachment. I installed it and noticed one side wouldn't spin like it was supposed to. After further review, the hole that the screw goes in was drilled about 1/2" too high. Because of this, the knob of the spinner was directly on the lid instead of under the lip. Instead of drilling a new hole in my brand new grill, I spent the next 45 minutes trying to whittle the end of the knob off so it would fit under the lip of the grill like it was supposed to. After that was done, and the lid hanger worked like it was supposed to, I thought I was finally home free. All that was left was to install the thermometer...and that looked super easy. I put the thermometer face in the insert, put the probe through the top of the grill and grabbed the included wing nut to fasten it in place. I spun and spun that wing nut and just could not get it to catch the threads. After closely inspecting the nut, I realized they sent a nut WITHOUT ANY THREADS!!! So I had to drive across town to a local hardware store with my thermometer and find a nut that would fit. After all this, I finally got my grill together and the first coals burning in it a mere FOUR HOURS AFTER I OPENED THE BOX!!!   Good thing we had already made other plans for dinner that night!!

title: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill
text:
Pro:  Good value; Cooks well; color selections (red!)
Con: Purchase of additional bulk LP flow adapter kit

I purchased this grill on-line last month.  It was packaged extremely well and easy enough to assemble (2-3 hours at a very leisurely pace).  Because we have a large LP tank in ground at our new house and had the builder run a line to our deck I was anxious to hook up my grill to the line and finally avoid the need to purchase 20lb propane tanks (you need an extra one because the propane always runs out while you are in the middle of grilling) and drive 60 minutes round trip to town for refills. 

What could be easier?  Perhaps inclusion of the bulk LP flow adapter kit?  Apparently, if you buy the natural gas version of the Spirit II E-210, the hose is included (because you cannot buy small tanks of natural gas, and Weber assumes you have a natural gas line nearby to connect) but if you buy the LP version Weber assumes you will use 20 lb propane tanks.  The conversion kit is a separate purchase.  To my knowledge the kit can be bought only from Weber, and they will sell you one only after you register your grill (probably to safeguard you from buying the wrong item) which means you cannot receive your grill, assemble it and cook the same day.

So after registering my grill online (very easy process) and shelling out an addition $60 for the conversion kit and waiting a week for it to arrive, I eagerly open the package and instructions and see....PROFESSIONAL INSTALLER INSTRUCTIONS (THIS INSTALLATION SHOULD BE DONE ONLY BY A LICENSED PROFESSIONAL...).  Now, this has me thinking, best case I pay for an install ($85.31 plus tax from my local propane dealer) or worst case, I try it myself and blow up the house, injure myself, or maybe ruin my new grill.  After talking the situation over with several more knowledgeable folks I come to the conclusion this is language that Weber legal beagles insist be included to cover their butts and, if I use common sense, I can do the install myself despite my plumbing inexperience.

OK, ready to go.  I refer to the instructions and notice there are three different conversion kits depending on which model grill you buy.  All three kits, however, show the same five components: 1) quick-disconnect--this is at one end of the hose included in my kit; 2) a 3/8" threaded pipe nipple; 3) a reducing coupling, 3/8" - 1/2"; 4) a 1/2" threaded pipe nipple; and 5) a locking shutoff--this I see is at the end of the gas line the builder installed.

Being the logical guy I am, I presume the kit contains the threaded pipe nipples and reducing coupling. Nope, nowhere to be found.  Is this an oversight, or am I supposed to purchase these?  Well, all three kits show the need for these so they must be included.  Check again,. Nope, not in the box.  I call up Weber Customer Service, explain what is missing and am told, "I'm so sorry.  We can take care of that."  The person tells me they will send another kit, and not to bother returning what I just opened since it is not economic to do so. Cool, but I do have to wait another week to grill.

Another week goes by and my package comes.....with the hose only!  Now it is evident to me the kit does NOT INCLUDE the two threaded pipe nipples nor the reducing coupling and the Customer Service people have systems that do not inform them of the kit contents since neither person I spoke with (one for the original order, another for the replacement) mentioned this additional purchase to me.  In fairness, the Customer Service folks were very pleasant and professional, so I believe this is a Weber training failure.

Since we do not live real close to a home improvement store I waited until our weekly trip to town to purchase $20 of pipe nipple and reducing coupling hardware and pipe thread compound to make sure my connections were secure.  Got out a couple of wrenches, watched a You Tube video how to disconnect the LP hose and regulator that I had assembled originally, (honestly, this was the most difficult step--once it was off, there was only one way to make everything fit together) I hand-tightened everything as a dry run, then took it all apart and reassembled with the pipe thread compound and cranked it down with my wrenches, making sure not to over tighten.

Waited 24 hours just to be sure the pipe compound had dried and formed a good seal, sprayed soapy water over all the connections and...opened...the...shutoff valve to the LP gas line.  NO BUBBLES!!!!

Now for the moment of truth.  Reviewed the ignition instructions. Turned the dial, pressed the ignition button...and...and...3-4 seconds later..a soft whoosh.  Turned the other burner dial and another soft whoosh.  Held my hand over the grill and...heat.  It worked!!!

First cooking experience was salmon. Fired up the left burner only and after 7-8 minutes the thermometer was "only" 300 degrees.  Was only intending to use one side of the grill so I was a bit disappointed that I would have to use the other burner to get to 400-450, but 3 minutes later I was at 500 degrees so this baby heats well!!!  Turned down both dials to halfway and the temp quickly dropped to 450.  Put on the salmon and came back in 7 minutes to see the temp was back at 500.  Hmm...very efficient....guess I didn't need both burners after all and the grill temp is much hotter than the temp near the lid where the thermometer is.  Anyhow, the salmon came out perfectly done. It was all in foil so I did not have a chance to evaluate the grease drip system or other features. Steak tonight!  That will be a bit more messy. 

So, all in all, I'm happy with the grill, but I did have to spend $80 more than I thought would be necessary.  On the other hand, I saved myself $90 of install costs and probably $80 on propane tanks that I no longer need.

title: Great grill
text:
Really love this grill. So far everything I have cooked on it, even stuff I've never cooked before, has come out tasting great. At the end of the day that's all that matters, right? I'm an ex-gasser and learning to grill over charcoal has been fun, and the experience of charcoal grilling itself is just more fun to me. Takes a little longer to get going than a gas grill, but to me this it is well worth the additional 10 - 15 minute wait.

I will say that at first I had trouble distinguishing it from the Original Premium. I had previously budgeted to buy a more much expensive grill but ended up returning that, opting for something simpler. This was therefore well within my price range, so I just went for the most expensive of the three available kettles available at the store thinking I would do some research later and figure out exactly what I was paying for.

Unfortunately the retailer I purchased this from had all the grills up on a shelf, locked down, so I couldn't actually look at them side by side. But from what I've seen in videos, the Master-Touch stands a little taller and sturdier. Combine that with the tuck away lid holder, and I can imagine it is easily worth the price difference above the Original Premium. 

Now, the other features I am pretty so-so on. The included Char Baskets are nice, but there is little instruction on how you should use them. Also made me feel a little like I was supposed to use them rather than like they were an upgrade. Not sure I would purchase those if they were separately advertised to me. Same thing with the Warming Rack that is included, except I actually use the baskets. Most often it feels like the rack is just in the way, and I have to take it off, tuck it away while actually grilling, and then put it back on when done so I don't have stuff laying around everywhere. I may just not have found the right use for it yet.

The GBS, truthfully, is not something I'm too excited about. I went ahead and purchased the sear grate (have yet to use it) just because I could. But a lot of times the middle insert is just another thing I have to manage when getting the grill set up. Now I've heard the GBS stainless grate is sturdier and thicker, so perhaps this will be made up for over time, or maybe it provides an advantage I'm not aware of. But right now I'm not too keen on other GBS components. May just be more of a personal preference.

All that aside, when talking value of included upgrades and features, the Master-Touch is a fantastic deal. Add everything up over the price of the Original Premium and you definitely get your money's worth. Now if what you want is something barebones and basic, I would suggest the Original Premium, though to be fair I have not used that one. I LOVE my grill, and I would grill on it every night if I could. I would definitely recommend this product to anyone looking to get into charcoal grilling.

title: Great grill!
text:
I've owned several Weber grills and still do.  I recently had to retire my original Weber premium grill (3rd I've owned) as the ash cleaner/catcher assembly had finally given up and the great warranty Weber offers had long expired. They had replaced it once, but that was 4 years ago.

Lot's of great things about this grill and a couple of things that are workable.

Ash management:
I love the new and improved ash catcher.  The design prevents putting too much pressure on the aluminum support ring that "hung" from the bottom via tabs inserted above the legs.  The newer design makes it easy to pinch and remove for cleaning and super simple to line up and replace when done.  Just a slight tilt to slide it into the stop/pivot point and then level it out and latch it in.  Easy.  The previous design had a slot on each side that you had to bend down to visually line up and then even raise into the slots and twist to lock it in. 
 As the grill was used more and more, this mechanism would wear down.  The support ring or ash catcher bucket would become slightly out of round making it difficult to remove and replace.  The ash sweeper required some regular cleaning of the grill bowl to ensure build up wouldn't impede it's motion.  Easy enough with some warm water, simple green, a scrap piece of wood to chisel the carbon build up and some double out steel wool to shine it back up.  

The ride:
Love the new height and the smooth rolling wheels!  The material on the wheels is a bit softer than the old ones and rolls smoothly and quietly out of the garage to grill up some tasty food.

Lid:
Handle with a heat shield and heat protected vent tab are awesome.  The temp probe is a nice add too.  What I don't like often is that the lid holder limits access to the grill surface. Two cases where this is a pain:  1) Lighting charcoal requires that I move chimney as far to the side as I can opposite of the open lid or take the lid off to center the chimney.  2) Access to food can be a bit limited with the lid blocking the way.  Again, these are easy to work around.  Just worth mentioning.

Cooking grate:
Sounded cool to have a center section that could be swapped out with different options.  In reality, it's a pain in that when removing the grate to load the grill with coals, the center section will fall out if you aren't careful.  I can't hang my grate by the grill handle any longer as I start coals.  I'm just going to end up getting a new 22" grate without the center section thing.

text:
I've had this grill since early summer (2+ months) and have had several occasions to use it for basic grilling of burgers, hot dogs, chicken legs and steaks and have been quite happy with the performance for these ordinary tasks. So far I haven't tried any serious barbeque or roast cooking although I did purchase the Weber iGrill thermometer system at time of original purchase. Unfortunately, the thermometer instructions did not address installation on this model grill even though it is supposed to accept it. The grills referenced in the install guide have mount points that are not present on the legs of this grill for the battery unit and I haven't used it yet for this reason. Hopefully Weber has some more updated info on their website to help address this model.

Another small gripe is that the aluminum drip tray holder is a basic stamped metal item that was shipped with extremely sharp edges! I know this from learning "the hard way" and having to visit an urgent care center after trying to install it to staunch the bleeding. After a few months of use (with the supplied replaceable aluminum insert) I carefully removed the tray holder and found the removable insert stuck inside the holder by grease that had accumulated between the tray and the holder. I decided to thoroughly clean the holder and ran it under hot water in the sink and then used a steel wool cleaning pad to shine it. After cleaning with the pad I continued rubbing the pad against the rough edges and found it smoothed them out very easily and made it much safer to handle. This raises the question of why Weber didn't bother taking the simple step of doing this in the factory prior to shipping it. I guess it may take someone filing a lawsuit to make this happen.

I do like the grill and find the iron grill plates to be a convenient size to clean in my kitchen sink after use. Hopefully I can get the digital thermometer connected properly and will try some slow-cooked barbeques and roasts before the end of the season.

title: True Story...
text:
I got my first used Weber LPG grill in the summer of 1997. A friend had called and asked if I would help him roll his grill out to the road for trash pickup (he had purchased a new stainless steel grill from a warehouse store). I told him that I would help him get his Weber grill to my deck and he could help me get my grill out to the road for trash.
I kept that grill, a used Silver B until the spring of 2018. I replaced the works twice in those 21 years, and she was starting to show her age. As a Father’s day gift, my wife ordered one of those shiny BIG money stainless steel grills and surprised me with it. When I finished assembling it, my neighbor came by and asked it he could take the old one for scrap. I said sure you can. As he rolled it away, he asked if it still worked, to which I replied “it works great. I cooked on it last night”. The next time I was on his deck, that old Silver B was there; he scrapped his grill and kept mine. 
Long story short, that BIG money stainless steel grill turned out to be the most worthless object that has ever been in my possession. After giving it an honest try for about a year, I called the same guy back to come and get it for scrap. In it’s place is a new Weber Spirit II grill. The same great engineering with some awesome updates makes this grill a pleasure to assemble and an even greater pleasure to use!

title: Easy clean
text:
I am super happy with this grill. Meat and veggies have turned out very well.  I grilled chicken breasts on low and then indirect heat, and they were the completely cooked but incredibly juicy.  I am also impressed with the drip covers over the burners. They have a very steep angle compared to other grills, so drippings don't stick to them nearly so much. 
 HOWEVER... what stands out is the ease of cleaning.  I have had other grills, and charred gunk just builds up on the bottom.  It had to be cleaned once in a while, and it was a pain.  This Spirit E-310? I just wipe out the drip pan (fantastic idea!) and slide out the lower tray to clean it.  It is night and day from cleaning other grills.  
      To be honest I was a bit concerned about the size.  For a similar price I could have bought a bigger grill with maybe an added feature.  Glad I chose this one.  The three burners with the upper rack has been plenty, and if I need to it is no problem to grill the veggies first rather than at the same time. I'm not sure if the 2 burner size would have worked, but the three burner size has been fine.  For the same or maybe less I would have had a grill that would have lasted me a few years. Because of the quality of the design, the quality of construction, and the ease of cleaning I do not know if I will ever need to buy another grill. 
      Just so that you know this is a real review by a real person I'll toss in one thing I would like to change about the grill, and it is not the size.  My one issue has been the opening for the propane tank on the bottom of the grill.  It is a bit too big, so that then the tank is in place it sits on the ground rather than resting in the grill.  This makes it a bit hard to move, and I move it each time I grill.  I found this provides an anchor, making the grill less likely to be blown around in a strong wind.  If I put the tank on the bottom ledge with the door open the grill rolls easily, but you should keep this in mind if you buy it. 
    So... I would highly recommend this grill, and that is saying something.  I have been pleased with other grills, but never highly recommend them.  I am this one.

title: Not perfect but awfully close
text:
My trusty old Ducane of 8 glorious years finally met its maker a few months back.  Sadly, Weber decided to put this sub-brand out to pasture and acquiring a new one was impossible.  Price unfortunately was an issue, and so sticking with a 4 burner setup wasn't an option if I wanted to stay in the Weber family.  I was admittedly hesitant to step down to a smaller size grill, but since it's really not all that often I need the square footage anyway I decided to pull the trigger on the Spirit E-310.  

I opted for the original Spirit rather than the II for one huge reason: the enclosed storage space underneath.  To me, an open cart is obnoxious - I just don't want to stare at my propane tank & would prefer other items i want to store be out of sight.  So this in my opinion was worth paying more than the newer version.  The fact that it also has 4 casters vs the II which only has 2 and needs to be lifted to roll was another nicety I preferred.

Setup was a breeze thanks to the easy to follow instructions and nicely organized hardware bags Weber provides.  For any confusing steps, a quick YouTube search will land you some helpful video walkthroughs that clear up your questions in a snap.

So why 4 stars and not 5?  Two minor but palatable issues.  First, the warmup time is abysmal.  Granted it had 4 burners but my Ducane shot up to 600 degrees in under 5 minutes making a nice hot sear easy and automatic.  This puppy will get to the 500 or so mark no problem but the wait time is a tad longer.  As long as you're not in a rush to get done out there, you'll be ok.  Second complaint - hot spots.  Despite the claims from corporate, they are in fact a thing on this grill, and it's because of the burner layout.  Youll notice that the three burner tubes are connected on a T that runs additional flame on the back end of the grill.  So naturally, this increased heat source leads to uneven cooking status between what's in the back and what's up front - plan & layout your food accordingly.

These minor nuisances to once side I'm loving what this grill has to offer thus far and look forward to many more years of good use.

title: Continued Improvement, With Small Flaws
text: I last bought a Weber grill about 15 years ago and I’ve been cycling through products by different manufacturers for the last decade. This Weber Spirit reminded me of what I’ve been missing. It’s as solidly constructed as my first Weber, perhaps even more so. It gives me strong, even heat and it’s a pleasure to operate. I also appreciate the subtle evolutionary changes that have taken place over time. The grill and burner design is better than before and I like the improved ergonomic design and accessibility of the drain dish underneath. One thing that did take me off guard, though (and almost caused me to damage my brand new grill) is the innovative design of the lighter switch. My grill came pre-assembled from Home Depot and I treated the switch like I did with practically every other barbecue I’ve ever owned. In most other barbecues, the button rotates or pulls off to expose a battery bellow. I pulled and tugged on that cover to inspect the battery as I hard as I dared without breaking it. No luck. Then I crawled underneath and traced the wires to the other side of the barbecue, and found the battery under a screw down cover there. That’s different. I think Weber would do well to pit a little sticker next to the striker button to prevent newbies like me from doing damage on their brand new purchase. On other thing: who ever was painting the cover of this of this barbecue at the factory missed a spot. It was a small, out of the way area, which is probably why it was missed in manufacturing, but still annoying. I fixed it myself, though, with heat resistant enamel paint.

Improvements:

2. The side rack is designed to lift grill for moving because I have no front wheels. But, the side rack comes off easily if you hit any bumps such as grass which makes it VERY frustrating. I move it each use from covered porch to grass area to ensure I don’t warp vinyl.
3. Back side of grill cooks hotter than front side. I think this is due to a horizontal burner running the length of backside but not in front side. I think the design intent was this way because of the warming wrack located at back of grill.
I pay attention to small details (perfectionist as my wife calls it) and so far I am happy with grill. Only time can tell :)

title: The grill I wanted
text:
This is my second Weber grill. My 10-year-old, 2-burner model finally gave up the ghost, but I had such good results with it that I wanted another one, just with three burners this time. Weber grills are simply the best.

Mine was already assembled and ready to go at Lowe's, but I spent some time making sure everything was screwed in correctly and tightly. No missing parts, and the grill fired up the first time. It heats to just above 550 degrees in aout 10 minutes with the burners on full blast; for searing steaks this is a must. But it handles low-and-slow cooking well, too, and I'm happy with its performance so far in all respects.

I purchased the (overpriced, but excellent) grill cover for it, as I want to keep it looking nice and protect it from the elements. I also plunked down for the iGrill probe that attaches to a magnetized pad on the grill and promises to mind your internal temperatures for you through a Bluetooth connection to your phone. That works okay, but it's not a game-changed for me, since I rarely stray too far from the grill while it's in use anyway.

The grates are cast-iron and you will need a good, soft-bristle brush to keep them clean, which you know already. But they release food beautifully if you apply a little cooking oil to them first, as you also should know to do.

Be good to your grill and it will be good to you. Buy a Weber, and it will be great to you.

title: Excellent Grill
text: Grill is excellent - cooks well.  The cast iron grates and all the materials are high quality like everything Weber makes. There are two zones for heat, but the back of the grill is like a third zone because there's another burner along the back and anything you place toward the back cooks/sears faster than the front. The tank mount is a neat contraption, but I'm not sure the tank scale-gauge is really accurate.  Get yourself a tank gauge if you really want to know what's left in the tank,  One shortcoming I discovered was that this particular grill, having the underside of the BBQ open and the grease tray exposed, allows for critters to find and get to the grease tray and even into the BBQ itself - which happened to me. If you have a model with doors under the grill, likely not an issue, but this grill is open on the bottom and the grease tray is vulnerable. Even when covered up, you may have to find a way to deter critters from getting under the grill and exploiting this weakness.  Would be better if there was a critter-proof cage around it or something. But for this price point, the grill is excellent and looks quite durable.

I eventually went with the Master Touch and haven’t looked back since. Let me just say we had 4 very happy campers while eating.  It was so good, I think I’ll break it out tonight for some fun times.  All in all, I think I put too much time into my decision. title: Excellent Grill
text:
This is the second Weber grill I have owned.  Not bad considering that time frame spans over 20 years.  The first Weber grill I bought was set up to work with natural gas.  I loved that grill but when I recently moved to a part of the country that had no natural gas service I had to leave it with the house we sold.  During the time I owned that Weber grill I only replaced the grates and flavor bars as it was very well made and reliable.  If I could have converted it from natural gas to propane I would have moved it with me.  
So I recently bought the Spirit II E-310 Grill.  I got the one with the red cover because I wanted something colorful.  It really is a nice bright red.  I decided to buy it through Home Depot as they had the best price.  It was delivered to my house and I decided to assemble it myself.  The assembly instructions were easy to follow and all of the parts were present.  I just took the assembly step by step and it went together without any problems.  When I unpacked the grill I noticed a dent in the cover.  Given how well the grill was packed it must have happened during shipping with UPS.  I went online and registered my grill and in the process of doing that I notified Weber that the cover was dented.  As soon as I did that they took the information and started the process of shipping me a new cover.  Now that is outstanding customer service. No long drawn out process to get the replacement cover sent.  They even followed up with me to confirm I had received it.  
I bought this grill because it provided three burners and was reasonably priced.  In other words it had the features I needed at an affordable price.  This grill allows terrific temperature control.  I can control the temp and cooking speed by adjusting all three burners separately or turn one or more burners off completely.  This is why I own a Weber grill.  The grill is so easy to use and provides consistent high quality results.  The two shelves are perfect for holding items as I grill and the utensils hang from the one shelf keeping them in easy reach.  The electric igniter works great as well.  The results I get from this grill are excellent and exactly as I have come to expect from Weber.
