title: Easy Smoked Turkey
text: I needed a smoker on short notice after turkey plans for our company / employee Thanksgiving luncheon went sideways (Bojangles cancelled turkey sales).  Without much knowledge of smoking a turkey, I knew that the kettle grill was basically idiot proof & decided I could figure it out.  I picked up everything I needed at Lowe’s, including an iGrill thermometer that works with my iPhone.  After watching a couple short videos on the Weber app & phoning a pro smoker friend (who basically confirmed what the app said), we smoked two perfect turkeys in a little over two hours and had the best Thanksgiving lunch ever!  The thermometer / timer made it very easy & removed the guesswork.  There is an art to using the kettle  grill and managing the air flow & temperature,  but it’s simple enough to figure out with the Weber app & a couple YouTube videos.  We bought the chimney charcoal starter which works like magic, and a few other handling tools  from Lowe’s, but this was the easiest straight out of the box grilling event I ever attempted, and I won’t lie - I was a little worried before I started.  (We since cooked a beef tenderloin on it with excellent results as well.)  I’ve used other Weber kettle grills before & they are perhaps the best way to grill chicken, steaks, fish, or anything else that needs a little charcoal smoke flavor without a huge investment.  Love Weber charcoal smoke!

title: Wow..what a great grill
text:
I am a pitmaster, always relied upon wood smokers and charcoal grills.  I never found a gas grill worth foolin' with.  And then I purchased my Weber.  Great grill.  consistent heat throughout the grilling surface.  I was drawn to the 10 year Warranty.  Previous experiences with propane grills left me replacing burners, flame tamers, and eventually tossing the whole thing after about a years use.  Due to rust and component failures.

The Weber holds up well, is easy to clean.  I like the aluminum pan inserts for the grease tray drain.  I also like the removable basin below the burners for easy clean up.  Being able to get your drippings, cooked sauces residue, and all the food particles and seasonings that fall from the food during the cooking process, out of the base of the grill regularly helps you keep your grill clean and makes it last longer.  The more you leave that stuff in there, the more moisture builds up to rust and rot components .   So I do like the easy clean. 
Another feature that is a good reference is the propane tank hanger with the "scale" that indicates approx amount of gas in the tank.  It gives you a really good idea of how much cook time you have on that tank.  I like the cabinet door that allows you to store my optional smoker box, for wood chips.  And the way the cabinet holds all the utensils I want to store.  On the sides are several clips to hand your tools for cooking and I use them all.

It's a great package... the 10 year warranty was the clincher for me.  We'll see if this is the brand I stick with from now on.  I already had the Weber Kettle grill for charcoal....and if I'm in the mood to fuss with ashes, and coals, etc.  I will roll that out.  I've had it for years and it still cooks good as new too.

title: Great small grill
text:
Got this grill as a Christmas present a few weeks ago after my cheaper grill rusted out in less than a year. I learned my lesson, and here’s my advice: don’t expect that $250 4 burner grill from Home Depot to last you that long. Also don’t expect much customer service either. Do yourself a favor and go for a reputable company that’s bold enough to give you a ten year warranty on all parts. 

Let’s start with what’s good: It’s well-made. From the moment I picked up the box and realized how heavy this small two-burner grill is, I knew it was because it’s good quality. Assembly was a breeze, even with the funky 3D instructions from the app. Anyone comfortable with a screw driver and a hammer can put this together. A cordless drill/bit driver will make everything so much faster and easier. After you put it together just step back and look at it, it’s actually quite nice for an entry-level gas grill. It will not be that nice and shiny ever again so enjoy the moment. 

So how does it grill? Accurate burner control and even heat throughout the grilling surface are just about the two most important aspects of any grill. And this grill shines in both aspects. The rear of the grill is the hottest, and that’s expected since it has a connecting burner that goes across to feed the right side burner. That’s the spot you want to use if you want those nice grill marks on that steak. The burner regulators have 180 degrees of range, that’s important, especially if you come from a cheaper grill that has only 90 degrees from low to high. You’ll feel like a grill master from the first time you use it. Another very important aspect is flare-up control, nothing can ruin what you’re cooking more than uncontrolled flare-ups. I put it to its ultimate test when I covered just about every square inch of that grill with bacon-wrapped mushrooms. I was waiting for it, the moment when I had to turn off the grill because it’s practically catching on fire. That moment never came. It just cooked very controlled with very minimal flare-ups, and the result was very juicy mushrooms with crispy bacon on the outside. It was quite the hit when I entertained for new year’s Eve. 

The only bad thing I can think of is that it doesn’t get as hot as I would like. 10 minutes with both burners on high and the lid down, will barely get the grill to 550 degrees F. But it will get hot enough to make grill marks on a steak, you just have to be patient. Also it’s nice that one of the side shelves collapses, but it would be even nicer if both collapsed. Also the Price at around $375 is a bit steep, even for this quality. 

Overall I’ll recommend this grill to just about anyone. It’s affordable, and it performs great.

I'm mostly happy with the function of the grill.  The heat is plentiful, well controlled and even. It works well with a smoke box too. title: Disappointed in Design
text:
I’ve been meaning to write a review of this grill for a long time.  I bought the Spirit II E-310 in spring/summer of 2019, as a replacement for a 10-year-old Spirit model which I had absolutely loved.  The quality of my old grill was well worth the price.   I have to say that I’m extremely disappointed in the design of this new grill.  It is extremely difficult to move around.  There’s just no easy way to get a grip on it.  There are wheels on only one side of the grill (as opposed to 4 wheels on my previous model), and they are on the opposite side of a flimsy collapsible side table. The obvious method of moving the grill would be to lift it by the table (as opposed to a sturdy handle on my previous model); but the table is just too flimsy.  So I end up collapsing the table, and trying to pick it up by gripping the legs.  Very awkward.  And then today, one of the plastic wheels fell off as I was trying to move the grill. I expected much more of a grill offered at this price point.  I miss my old grill. 

Also, I've discovered that the Weber brand grill cover that I bought is not weather-proof.  This winter, we in the Northeast have had numerous snow storms that end with rain.  After each of these storms, I’ve found the grill cover frozen to the grill.  So it’s a process to get the grill cover off, and then I need to bring it inside and dry it out before putting it back on the grill.  

All in all, I do like cooking on the grill, but find other aspects of using the grill frustrating.  If I were to purchase a grill again, I’d widen my search.

title: Damaged In the Box, Quality Downhill
text:
I bought another Weber from The Home Depot in September 2019 after a great experience I had with a Spirit I 310 Natural Gas bought in 2016. I needed a BBQ for my summer property and I really wanted another Spirit I identical to the other model I have but it has been replaced by the Spirit II. 

This Spirit II has been a big letdown. The lid was dented in the box right from the factory, as seen in the picture below. The box was not damaged externally. As a result, a new BBQ looks like junk sitting on the deck. Then the fasteners and bracket provided/shown to mount the propane gas line to the bulkhead can't be mated - the captive nut that shows as part of the bracket doesn't exist and there was no supplementary nut provided that would otherwise perform that task. The third issue with this BBQ is that it heats unevenly. I'm not sure if it's because it's a propane model or not, but my Spirit I has excellent, even heat. This one hot spots in the center and leaves the sides and corners cool. 

All in all, I'm very unhappy with my Spirit II 310. Weber quality seemingly has gone downhill after just a few years. I would suggest looking elsewhere for your BBQ needs, as it appears I am not the only one to have purchased a factory damaged machine. I see there are other reviews showing damaged and missing hardware. 

Disappointed in Halifax.

text:
Just used this grill yesterday for the first time and found it to be excellent. The grill is top notch and the customer service is world class. I'm no expert and have a lot to learn but I can already see that the included accessories give you a lot of flexibility. The included charcoal baskets make it possible to use less (or more) charcoal depending on the size of the cook, and want kind of grilling or smoking you want to do. You can place both baskets in the center of the grill or place one on each side of the grill. The included optional grill grate has a removable center piece that allows you to focus the grilling or searing in the center of the grill and you can easily add more charcoal to the baskets if needed. You could also separate the two included charcoal baskets and put one on each side of the grill for smoking. With this configuration you can cook in the center portion of the grill and then sear over one or both of the charcoal baskets on the edge of the grill. The grill grate has hinged grates on each side that you can lift up to add more charcoal if necessary. I haven't used this feature yet but it's very obvious how convenient it will be. The thermometer in the lid of the grill is very handy to show you the overall internal temperature of the grill itself, but I'll still use a meat thermometer for the precise meat temps. The lid thermometer will be good for seasoning cast iron pieces. Haven't yet used the included warming rack that sits on top of the grill grate. This looks to be better for bigger jobs. There is LOTS of room inside this grill. I chose this grill because it sits a little higher than the other grills and for extra accessories that came with it. This grill has just about everything you need for grilling or smoking except for maybe a meat thermometer. I ordered a Slow-N-Sear package from another vendor, as well as a Vortex product. I won't be using either of these products anytime soon because this grill, as delivered, seems to have everything I already need. This grill is a superb product as-is. Now having said all this, I'm thinking about ordering the Weber Jumbo Joe for everyday grilling. It's just the wife and I most of the time and the Master-Touch is best for more than two people.  EXTREMELY happy with this grill. 
Oh, and one more thing - Weber Customer Service. These people are the best. I installed the triangle assembly upside down when I put the grill together. Totally my fault. This is the part that braces the three legs of the grill. To fix this I needed to remove the wheels and reinstall the triangle right-side up. The only problem is the little hub caps that hold each wheel in place can't be reused. The Weber Customer Service person was friendly, efficient and sent me a new set of hub caps at no charge and no questions asked.

I've only used it a few times since I got it last month, but can already say this easily the best grill I've ever had. 
First, assembly. The directions overall were easy to read, which made putting it together pretty easy as well.  There are a couple pieces where you need to pay attention to the details, and one piece where the holes didn't line up perfectly and I had to muscle it a little, but overall, not difficult.
Second, design. The tables are solid, even with the ability to lower one of them. The angle in the legs with the wheels makes it very easy to maneuver due to the weight distribution. The shelf underneath has a backstop that helps break the wind as well, so items placed there stay there. The grease trap - super easy to remove and clean!  
Also, the version I got comes with a weight-based gas gauge so I can tell roughly how much propane is left in the tank. I haven't gotten through one tank yet, so I can't tell how well it work yet, but so far, to be honest, I'm a little skeptical. The red marks seem visible at both the quarter and 3 quarter spaces at the same time, and it's not terribly smooth in its movement.  So we'll see.
Finally, the cooking.  I love having the ceramic coated grates!  The reversible grates allowing for both heartier and more delicate meats is wonderful! The burners are appropriately sized so it comes to temperature well.
Overall, I am loving this so far and expect to use it very often as we continue through spring and into summer!

text:
I really like the hinge sides, lets me add coals or wood chips.
What I'd really like would be an 18 -20" extinsion to make this a smoker also. Wouldn't be all that hard.

title: Excellent Grill
text: I have had this grill for a few weeks now and have no real complaints. The grill is an excellent size, burners fire up immediately and produce consistent and strong heat. The propane guage is very helpful for anticipating when a tank change will be needed.

title: Assemble grill
text: Assembly took two people and a little over 3 hours. Instructions were very clear and step by step. Grill takes longer than expected to heat up but performs very well when cooking. I plan and hope to use this grill for many years.

title: Spirit II E310 review
text: Love the grill and the only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is the mobility.  While moving the grill isn't hard, it could be a lot easier with a handle of some type on the side.

title: Great Grill
text: Great fit for full time RVing. Would get one again.

title: Highly Recommend Weber
text: This is my first Weber and love the grill the quality is awesome and cooking has been easy. Weber owner for life now!!!

title: RUST
text: Have had my grill a couple years and last year the grates and flavor bars had starting rusting.  I store my grill in the shed during the winter.  This year figured I would replace the flavor bars and grates.  Not a $50 and $90 for them.  I should have just stuck with my cheap grill and replaced it every 3 years - would have been cheaper.  Also, this grill has always run too hot. On low will heat up to over 300.

title: Nice newer grill some features need improvements
text: I like the new grill, and I especially like the solid handles and heat shield.  Ash pan seems nice as well.  I am fond of the lid holder, but wish they would have still included the internal hook on the lid because sometime you just want to hang it on the side of the grill rather than have it high up as a shield.  I like the hole in the center of the grate for loading charcoal, but there is no way to hang on to it when removing it, and no place to put it when removing it.  It would be useful to either have a tool for removal, or a hanger on it to hang it on the edge of the grill

title: best grill I've ever owned
text:
i purchased my first weber about 17 years ago loved it all these years never had to replace the burners. Sure i had to replace the grates, the igniter and the thermostat but as far as quality is concerned you cant beat a weber . 
the frame was starting to rust and I figured it was time to buy a new one hoping this one lasts as long as my original one

title: great grill
text: this is a great grill have had other brands nothing can compare .

title: Weber Rocks!!!
text: Really love my new Weber.  The quality was evident as I assembled it.  It works very well and is a perfect size for my needs.

title: Perfect for two.
text: Nice little grill. Easy to use. Small propane tank a little hard to hook up because of small space.

title: Fantastic upgrade from a 10+ year old Weber!
text: I had a two burner for over 10+ years... less than 20, and am loving the three burner. It is so quick to turn on (gas tank first) and a quick knob push and turn for grill itself and then CLICK to ignite! Up and running! Love it! Going to be a GOOD ten to twenty years I hope!

title: Spirit II Yes Yes
text: Works very well for a variety of meats. A couple of design opportunities,  1) have the fixed in the up position tray on the left side since that side is the primary grilling side, and to avoid having to raise the tray and have it slip off the screws when you move the grill. 2) have the gas line connector on the inside of the grill to keep it out of the way

title: Great grill
text: Great grill. Easy to operate kudos to ACE hardware for setup and delivery

title: Bday Gift
text: I bought the grill as a bday gift for my husband and he loves it. Almost every time he uses it he tells me how much he likes it.

title: New Weber S-310
text: It’s good, but nowhere nearly as good as my 1995 Genesis which lasted 24+ years. This one has very cheap plastic wheels. We’ll see how it holds up over time. I like the new ignighter

title: New Weber customer
text: Grill cooks evenly and the temp so far has been able to be adjusted pretty good although I haven't had the need to cook at lower temps so I don't know how low the heat goes with the burner on low and the lid closed. I purchased the Cart/Stand with this and glad I did but the cart/stand is a little wobbly especially when brushing the grate after use. My real interest will be in how long this lasts. I take care of my grills and if I don't have to replace any parts for 5+ years, I will be really impressed! I have only had 1 other grill that lasted and it was a Coleman. I ponied up the extra $$ for this Weber so I expect this to last for years!

title: Weber Portable Grill
text: Excellent small BBQ. Easy to assemble and to transport. Sturdy. Cooks very evenly.

title: Exceptional quality and great grilling!
text: My first Weber and she works like a charm, easy to use, clean and cook.  I love the quality of the grill and wished I had purchased sooner!  A must for all grilled!

title: Great compact Bar-bie
text: Great compact barbie that can grill everything we need, for 2 people to 20!

title: Strong and long lasting
text: Lasts forever and withstands any weather. It has been on my Florida rooftop terrace for 3 years and has no rust or damage.

title: Master-Touch
text: I smoked some beef short ribs on the grill for about 8 hours between 225f and 250f.  The grill maintained that temperature without having to babysit it.  Awesome grill!!

title: Excellent cooking machine
text: Great cooker. Gets hot fast and cooks very evenly across grill. You will not be disappointed with this purchase.

title: No Uneven cooking.  Balanced heat all around.
text: No hot or cold spots which is huge these days with gas barbecues. I had a $2500 unit for quite some time and I had to constantly move meat around to get an even cook.  With the Spirit II not to worry.  I did not have to move anything!  Just turned them over and leave them in place!  Nice design and easy to clean.  I was able to remove all the burners and baffles in five minutes and thoroughly clean the unit.  Piece of cake.  Just love it!  Great job Weber!!

title: Need help from customer service

title: Love it!

We have jerry rigged with bungee cords until we can get a new grill. Knobs and other parts have already had to be replaced. That we didn't mind so much. We have had much cheaper grills last much longer than this one. The grill itself cooks well, it's a shame it's not higher quality to justify the proce of a new one,

title: Got to Have it

title: Love this grill

title: You will love it.

title: Great grill but not if you move it around a lot
text: Well built solid grill. Cooks everything perfectly, easy to control the heat. The only thing I don't like is that it not easy to move due to no type of handles on the side. As you have to lift the end without wheels, you have to lower the side table first as it will fall when you try to move the grill even a few feet. Design could be improved for moving around but other than that it's a very nice grill.

title: New Weber Grill
text: We really are enjoying our new grill. Only used it 3 times and all is well.  We had our last Weber Grill for 22 years and decided to replace it. The old one was still working just fine.  Spring comes slowly to Minnesota and we are waiting for the grilling season to begin.

title: Great little  BBQ
text: Heats-up quickly, it was easy to sear  the fish I was cooking.  The greats cleaned up nicely.

title: Quality
text: Picked up my new Weber Spirit II E-210 grill yesterday.  Assemble was easy with by following the instructions, and the quality of the parts was evident from the very beginning.  Almost everything was powder coated, so there were very few sharp edges, so no cuts putting together.  It lights easy, and heats quickly.  The screws and small parts were packed in number coded bags, which were referred to in the instructions.  The grill parts were not marked, so it took some effort to find the right part amongst the packing, and it's well packed, lots of stuff for recycling.  Looking forward to many years of grilling.

title: Weber 22” Master Touch
text: Using a 22” Weber is required in day to day life! There is no other grill that can compete!

title: Awesome Grill
text: Awesome Grill.  I've been using the cheap grills for years and finally purchased a Weber.  Love it!

title: The Essential BBQ
text: This upgraded classic is a must-have for any BBQ enthusiast.  The set up is convenient and effective whether you're cooking burgers and hot dogs or slow cooking a roast. There are plenty of accessories to compliment whatever uses you have in mind for this reliable stand-by.

title: Great so far
text: It was time to replace our old Weber after nearly 20 years.  I hope this one goes that long.  So far, so good.  It starts on one push and cooks evenly.  I've only used it a few times but we all like it.  And, it's a Weber...the best grill made.

title: Customer Service is not helpful
text: I purchased this grill because I could use the small propane tanks.  I am 76 years old and no longer able to lift heavy propane tanks.  The grill does a great job.  The size is perfect for just myself and sometimes a few friends.  I gave a low rating because of the customer service.  I disconnected an almost full tank for the winter.  I had used it twice.  I was unable to reattach it to use the remaining fuel.  After requesting help with the problem, a very disrespectful service rep, told me that if the tank went on once it should go back on again.  This has not proved to be true with several different tanks from different manufactures.  It is difficult and awkward to install the propane tank and the tank should NOT be removed unless it is empty.  Removing seems to cross thread the connector so that a previously partially used tank cannot be reinstalled.

title: Grill is too Hot.
text: The grill burns very Hot. Between 400 degrees on low and 650 degrees on high.

title: The end of a long dream
text: I always wanted one. Finally I took the plunge and do not regret it at all. I bought a couple of accesories and could not be happier

title: Perfect size grill for a couple
text:
I have not had a chance to use my new Weber grill because it has been so cold, windy and rainy in Columbus, Ohio! 

I did buy the grill unassembled and started assembling the in the garage on nice afternoons. I was impressed on the packaging of the product, the engineering of the pieces and clarity of the directions! I also downloaded the BILT app. 

This was a nice project for me while staying home. I am 67 years old and just realized my dexterity is not what it was back in my younger years, so it took me more than 1.30 hours to complete. 

I added several accessories and purchased the Weber's Way to Grill book. Best grilling book I have ever come across!

Looking forward to better weather and a chance to grill out on my new gas grill. I also own two Weber charcoal kettle grills that I have used for many years!

title: Recommended!

title: Great Grill with 100% of Cooking Surface Usable

The heavy ceramic covered grates are also easy to clean between uses. The spring-loaded tank "gauge" is a good heads up of approximately how much propane is left in the tank. The burners are hot enough that I seldom use them on high. AWESOME GRILL!!

title: Very pleased

title: How it cooks
text: It cooks way better than any other grill I had. You can control what your cooking a lot more compared to the other grills I owned.

title: Years Since Owning Weber & Glad to Have Returned!
text: This is one of your basic two burner grills. This is the first time I have a purchased a Weber product in several years, due primarily to the prices being the highest in the field. I am very pleased with this purchase and plan on keeping this grill for many years. It is very efficient and I had only one incident where it seemed to be running low on fuel, due to the temperature not getting as high as soon as normal. After turning it off and back on a couple of times, it started performing better. The only suggestion I have is to make the drip grease and water residue pans a little deeper. Even cooking for two people and a relatively small meal, with one side, the pan rsidue pan fills up close to the top, where it is hard to remove without partially spilling.

title: Great grill
text: Really like this grill. Its good/solid quality, heats up fast and holds its temperature well. I knew I wanted a 3 burner and had decided long ago that my next grill was going to be a Weber. Weber grills are fairly expensive, but as with everything, you get what you pay for. Highly recommend.

title: Perfect grill.

title: Temperature won't even reach 400 degrees
text:
I just bought my new Weber Sprit II and is taking about 20 - 30 minutes to reach 350 degrees and longer to reach 400 degrees but won't go over that. All the reviews and videos I watch advertised that it can reach 500 degrees in 15 minutes. 

Another thing if you finally reach over 350 degrees and open de lit you would have to wait again another 15 - 20 minutes to reach temperatures over 350 degrees.

I don't have any gas leaks and this is a new grill! I think I would have to return it, I'm very disappointed. The only reason I give it 3 starts is because the quality and look are really good.

title: Poor Heat Control
text:
For a backround comparison I am an experienced griller.  I have owned many grills. I currently own. Rec Tec BFG, Weber Q1200, Large @@@@@ This new spirit has terrible temperature control and very poor grease drainage.  My unit either wants to spike to 600 degrees no matter where you have the gas.  I have tried multiple burner configurations and dial settings with no luck in keeping a desired temperature.  This grill with the poor grease drainage has flare ups more often then any other gas grill I have ever used.  I have much better results cooking on my Weber Q series grill. I will be getting rid of this grill as it performs so poorly.   

This grill was a replacement for a much older Weber 2 burner that performed rather well but due to its age looked terrible. I am very disappointed in this new grill.

title: premium charcoal grill 22 inch
text:
this replaces (augments?-i can't part with it!) my 15 year old unit. I really enjoy cooking on it,  especially using it as a smoker for ribs and pulled pork. I bought a second lower grate and sometimes place it on top of the first with rock spacers to raise the coals closer to the cooking grate if I'm searing a few steaks or pork chops without the lid.  Today I'm cooking 2 pork butts side by side. one on the new grill and the other on the 'broken in' unit. 
   My only nit-pick is the wheels are useless on my back lawn.  I find it easier to carry the grill.   I LOVE cooking on it.

title: Great, Affordable Gas Grill
text: I LOVE this grill. Well made, easy to use, even looks great. It's help keeping me entertained (and my family fed) during our self-isolation. I also like the app with its grill guide for different types of foods and recipes. Weber is the best.

title: Right size for 2-4 people
text: I've has multiple larger grills over the years. I like the size of this one that cooks enough for 2-4 people without wasting natural gas to heat up a larger grill. Love it.

title: Missing tray

title: Above Expectations
text: The grill has performed above my expectations. The temperature has been accurate and easy to control. Using the Weber App I have been able to cook a wide variety of items at the correct temperature and time which has produced delicious results. I like the disposable drip tray. It is easy to reach and replace. The initial assembly was straight forward and the grill arrived in excellent condition. It took me about an hour to assemble, but I followed the instructions and took my time. I am very happy that I replaced my old gas grill with this one.

title: Not a better charcoal grill in the world.
text: I have always owned a Weber grill of some kind, but the Master Touch is the best. All the advanced features to make grilling and smoking a pleasure.  I only wish I could afford the accessories for the center of the grill. Being able to make stir fry on a grill... are you kidding me.  Love my new grill and I know I will get endless hours of great fun making new and delicious recipes.  Everyone should own a Weber charcoal grill in there life time.

title: Buy something else
text: I have had our Spirit (two burner tube) grill for less than three years.  The triangular "flavorizors" have completely rusted through.  The ignition button has completely failed, the  gas tubes distribute propane unevenly and need to be replaced.  I have been a life long Weber man but I am wondering if a change is in the air.  Almost $500 down the drain.  Exercise caution when buying this grill or get comfortable replacing it within 3 years.

title: Weber Q1200 Gas Grill
text: Light and easy to move around, yet grill itself is very sturdy.  Grill heats up fast and heat is dispensed evenly which makes for all pieces on the grill cooked properly.

title: Loading the Tank
text: I wanted a grill that was totally enclosed on all sides.  This makes it very hard to load a full tank of gas.  I struggled to slide the tank inside and scratched the surface of the floor.  This unit should have a slide in the bottom to assist in loading the tank.  I placed a piece of plywood with soft felt strips so I could slide the tank in position.  I know that it couldn't go into the hole for the tankl.  When the tank becomes half full, I will remove the board and place the tank in the proper position.

title: Second time around

The open design will hopefully prevent the moisture buildup that causes the rust. The grilling surface is great and the temperature is uniform. I also added the igrill temperature probe kit. Looking forward to many great grilling experiences.

title: Great customer experience

title: Get this grill!

title: Grill

title: Great little grill!

Easily the highest-quality small grill I've owned.  Looking forward to many steaks and burgers in the years to come.

title: Ehh so far

title: Quality has gone down hill
text:
I was given this grill as a gift and was so happy because I have always wanted a weber grill but couldn't justify spending that kind of money. I was highly disappointed when putting it together. I remember for years when I went to go look at them the lids were super heavy and the knobs were metal and rubber, now plastic and the lid is light weight junk. So it broke my heart to have to tell my mother in law that I wanted to return her gift. But there is no world where the cheap junk is worth what she paid for it. I'm sorry weber but way to let your game start slipping. If you are going to save money on materials then pass the savings on to us. Quit selling junk
and charging quality prices.

title: thumbs up
text: Best small grill I've ever owned.  Always had a Weber charcoal grill and now I'll never have anything but Weber for gas either.

title: Probable good buy, but....
text: I had previously owned a copper Genesis, for approximately six years... Great grill, but the hood disintegrated over time and pieces of metal were falling into our food on the grill - so time for a new one... the Genesis was bigger than we really needed, so I decided to go with the Spirit E-310. Bought it assembled from HD. Couldn't justify spending $800 again for Genesis - but maybe I should have... the Spirit is much lighter and clearly more cheaply made.... the stainless (if they are stainless) side tables scratch very easily already. There's no enclosed cabinet, and I wanted the GS ignition, but you couldn't get that with the enclosed cabinet Spirit, and couldn't justify the additional price. Lights easily every time.... glad to have the 10 year warranty now, but we'll see what it really covers in time. Have tried other non-Weber grills in the past, and they are just not worth it - despite the cheaper cost... only time will tell with this one... sorry that they seemed to stop making them in different colors...definitely seems like Weber tried to shave as much money as they could from materials to build this one... oh well..

title: So worth it!
text: So far, so Good! I wish I have bought this earlier. The size is ideal for a small family like ours. It heats fast and therefore saves us gas.

text: The grill itself is fine, it appears to be of good quality. The customer care service leaves a whole lot to be desired. It can't be reinstalled into its position so the table can't swing up and down. After registering the grill I called the Customer Care number. After holding on for a while a person answered. Now this is when the whole Corona thing had gotten started and maybe all the customer service people had stayed home and they just had someone there to answer the phone, I don't know, but I soon started wondering if I had the right number. He made light of the pivot stud popping out of the table and really didn't know much about what I was talking about. He became frustrated and hung up on me. title: I love it, but could use some improvement.
text:
I do like this grill. It seems expensive at first, and I admit that after feeling the quality of the stand I normally wouldn't pay this much for it... but, after using it as much as I have it is awesome. After looking at other grills, I just don't think that they have the same exterior coating that these grills do. It matters. For instance... mine , unfortunately, fell on the ground and the pavement didnt even scrape the serface. It is a thick, cured coating that other imitation grills do not have. It makes it worth the money. Duribility and functionality is the key Weber.

The ash sweeper is the best for not having to maintain the grill that often. All of the ash goes into the ash pot as promised and makes for the easiest clean-up of any grill/smoker. 

I installed a digital/wifi temp gage (for an additional $50) with temp probes. I would recommend this as when smoking, I have the lid spun around so that the exhaust damper is opposite my slow and sear... I would recommend the slow and sear by the way. 

I do love my wobbly weber and will be selling my pellet grill as a result.

title: Some of the best features aren't even mentioned
text:
Bought this to replace a gas grill I've had since 1995 (seriously). Before that my parents had a Weber kettle charcoal grill. I bought it at a store, so I was able to see the display model in person before buying it. I got the Mocha color (perhaps that chain's exclusive color as I don't see it listed on the Weber site). I went slow putting it together...took about 2-2 1/2 hours. The instructions are quite well done. The metal frame pieces are a bit flimsy (had to bend a few corners back in place while assembling), but the frame is more structurally sound once together. Overall I'm pleased with the assembly part. 

Like I mentioned this is my first new grill since 1995, so perhaps some of the features I found great are now industry standards. First up the cooking grate, which isn't one big piece but actually 2 pieces side by side. In all the pictures you see the grates with somewhat wide bars. But, you can flip them over and the other side has a narrower bar on top (the bars are shaped like a triangle so wide on one side, narrow on the other). The manual mentions this, but it's not seen in website photos. So, you could have a grate with more surface area on one side of the grill and flip the other grate to have more space between the bars on the other side. 

The other great feature deals with the gas tank. The tank hangs on the side, below the right shelf, and is very easy to install and replace. Hang the tank on the hook and then clamp down the guard (so no, the tank can't accidentally fall off while rolling the grill across the patio). But, the hook is also an indicator for the amount of gas still in the tank, which is measured by the weight of the tank. This is a great feature. So far I think it's pretty accurate...will see how it is as I use up tank and replace it. Again, this is mentioned in the manual but not shown on the website. 

Last, the left shelf folds down. This is nice for storage, and would be helpful for people using the grill in smaller spaces. These are just some of the features I found to be nice that weren't really highlighted.

Now, I did just find a 2 minute Weber YouTube video that mentions some of these features. Search Weber's videos for "Spirit II Features & Benefits" on YouTube and hopefully you'll find it. 

So cooking, how does it do? Like I said this replaced a grill I've used since 1995 which was barely working (couldn't even control temperature settings), so anything would be better than that one was. The separate temperature controls for the two burners are great. I like the thermometer on the lid. The starter has worked well so far (and does require a AA battery, which is included). I did not buy the iGrill for it, but perhaps in the future just to try it...I don't know why you'd need the iGrill unless you're lazy checking your food or you haven't ever grilled before and don't know what you're doing. I'm looking forward to using this grill more. I like the 10 year warranty on all parts as well (be sure to register your grill after purchase). I just laugh after all these years I'm back to a Weber grill.

text:
Purchased a 22" charcoal kettle about a month ago. Revolutionary. Absolutely game changing. My family's culinary delights are reaching unprecedented new levels. I've grilled chops, chicken filets, salmon, steelhead trout, corn on the cob, potatoes, several veggies, even s'mores for dessert. When I bought this, I had essentially no experience grilling. It seems that this grill is very forgiving. I have yet to try anything that has completely failed. It's terrific for newbies (and, I gather, for seasoned grill masters as well). A Weber Kettle + a few minutes watching a YouTube video on whatever you want to grill and you're off to the races.

My only minor complaint is that the rotating vent on the lid does not have a handle. It gets very hot, which makes it difficult to turn the vent to reduce airflow while grilling. I have seen some people online proposing modifications to accommodate this but it seems like something Weber could address directly.

Nevertheless, this grill is terrific. 22" seems like a reasonable size for a small family. I can easily fit a grill basket and 3–4 chops. If I were grilling for more than about 4 people I'd consider getting a larger one, especially if I wanted to keep grilling side dishes in the basket.

title: New Weber Spirit II E-210 Grill
text:
Love it so far.  Gets plenty hot to cook in just a few minutes.

I've purchased $200 grills that lasted 2 years, $100 grills that lasted 1-2 years, I've replaced burners on those cheap grills to get another 1-2 years.  

It was time again to replace the whole unit.  I have several friends that brag about their Weber grills.  So I decided to try one out.  At 2 times the cost of a cheap grill, I certainly expect this to last much longer.

Love it so far.  It was pre-assembled by my local Aubuchon Hardware and the build quality and quality of materials is certainly better than the average grill. 

Only problem so far was the ignitor would not work the other day, replaced the battery and still nothing.  Ended up being a loose wire connection, that just needed to be pushed all the way in.

2 burner warm up quickly and has plenty of space for my family of 5 (3 teenage boys).

Bring on Summer!

title: Care and complaints
text:
Over time this grill has been my mainstay. I’ve owned three. By and large Weber has made incremental and effective modifications in the design over time.   Two complaints. The mechanism that sweeps the spent ash into the collecting bin will over time rust and fuse into place and cease to work. In addition Weber has removed the handle on the back making it more difficult to move over uneven surfaces. 

Be sure to buy and use the cover and Weber’s effective spray grill cleaner.  Any buildup of fat deposits will after a time become moldy. Reduce it by cleaning the grill surface after every one or two uses.

title: Amazing grill - no more sacrificed meat
text: The Copper 22" Original Kettle Premium is my first Weber. I've been burning meat over fire for more than three decades, and after having this kettle for a few weeks, I realize a lot of good meat and money was sacrificed to inferior grills. I love the copper finish. It was a bit flashy for me and I would have bought black if the store had it in stock, but I'm glad they didn't.  The copper looks great during an Arizona sunset. The 22" is a perfect size for my family; typically just two but occasionally six people. Anything bigger would be a waste of space in the yard and on the grilling grate. I like the upgrades that come with the Premium. I'm not sure how accurate the thermometer is or exactly what it's measuring, but I love having it as it helps dial in the temperature. The enclosed ash catcher is great because even though I clean my grill the morning after, when the wind kicks up I don't have to worry about a mess all over the patio. I like the hinged grate, there's nothing wrong with it and being able to add fuel is super easy, but when it's grilling days are done, that'll be an upgrade. And speaking of upgrades, I love all the Weber accessories and after market goods that are available for the kettle. So I love this grill because of all those things, but it wouldn't be worth bragging about if the food coming off it isn't amazing. With the exception of one meal, everything has been fantastic. I made my first beer can chicken and it was so good I couldn't believe I made it. I also burned some quality Brisket burgers because I didn't manage my fire. That's probably the most important thing to learn about using these grills - fire and heat management. Take the time to learn the different techniques and how you can manipulate your kettle grill to suite your needs. If you can master that, with this kettle and all the accessories, you can make incredible meals you'll love and you'll love sharing. Now if you're convinced a Weber is right for you, don't be afraid of the price tag and don't get talked into buying something you don't need and won't use. Get the right grill for you, use it, love it. And download the Weber app as well as the BILT app for assembly - seriously, get the BILT app and you'll have the grill put together in no time.

title: Ok grill, but please read...
text:
I purchased my grill in March 2020 and it is now May 2020; I had it roughly 2 months and grill out 2-3x a month. I gave it 2 stars because it is a simple and stylish grill that was packaged well, but not a good fit if you're cooking for 3 or more in a family/group. The grill area is an oval shape so the main usable grilling area is 12.5" x 15", small.  There are only 3 of us, 1 adult and 2 children, and we can not fit 3 medium sized 8-10oz tenderloins, onions and/or asparagus, and camping potatoes in foil on the grill at the same time, which means something has to cook first then sits cooling while the rest finishes up cooking. Not ideal.

Other issues I came across was the location of the the regulator connection, it is right under the handle grip making it tricky to grip the grill securely to move it.  I also found it very difficult to install the LP cylinder, they do not go on easily; I have to turn the grill upside down to get the perfect angle to install. My biggest disappointment though was the coating on the porcelain-enameled cast iron cooking grates because it is already flaking off on one of the two cooking grates. I soak the cooking grates in warm soapy water just as the Cleaning instruction recommend and used only a wash cloth to remove cooked on remains and air dry. (If your past the warranty new grates are $65-$85 depending on your grill size) 

The small size I can adjust to, but this is a basic table top grill that is over $200, no one should have to struggle with moving their grill; the cylinder or deal with a rusty cooking grate in this short of time.

title: Not amazing but will get the job done.....mostly
text:
First off, buying anything anymore made in the USA little loan in my state of Illinois is a huge plus. Assembly was way easier than most grills I have owned or seen. Although the legs are a bit tight and if you don't have a lot of grip or upper strength it may be a challenge for you putting them in. Everything else was a cake walk and took me about as much time getting everything out of box as it did putting it together. There is a good amount of grilling area and the grill grate with it's swing open sides and pull out center are convenient. Also they don't really hinder the use of a turner which was a concern for me so great job Weber.

Now for the cons. If you go to brush your grill with any effort, don't expect it to be rock solid. The legs are thinner gauge aluminum than i think they should be and this thing twists like no other grill I have owned. I don't think it will break anytime soon but metal fatigue my be an issue later on. Also if you have had an acorn or some insulated grill of some sort this will chew thru charcoal to get the heat you want for searing or even 300-400 range. Also the lid keeper could be built better to allow it to rest straight up instead of angled in towards the grilling area. Another thing, make sure you realize that you check the height over before you buy. From what I've seen they are on the shorter side. Your back will thank you. 
 

All in all I'm pleased. If you are a hamburger or hot dog person just trying to feed yourself or a crowd it will do you well. For someone that likes high heat. Have stock in lump charcoal.

The real satisfaction from this Weber is the kettle. This is where you really get your bang for your buck. text: This has been the best grill I have owned, with my last one being a $400+ Kenmore. title: Quick to temperature, even cooking
text: I have owned four Weber grills over the years (one charcoal, one natural gas, and two propane).  I have found all to be consistently durable.  My recent purchase of the E-310 replaced a Genesis grill.  The E-310 heats quickly and provides uniform heat across the surface of the grill.  The grills are cast iron, and although they don't appear as thick as my old grill, they provide a consistent and even grill marking on the food.    The lid on the E-310 is not as heavy as my previous Genesis, but it seems to hold the heat allowing for an even grilling temperature, thus even cooking.  One side table folds down, which may be beneficial to someone desiring a smaller footprint for storage or use. The mounted temperature gauge is useful, but a point and read thermometer to check the temperature of the grills for searing temperature may be helpful.     After much research and comparison, the E-310 is living up to the excellent reviews and ratings it has garnered.

title: WEBER Q-1200 – MAKING THE BEST EVEN BETTER
text:
Other than using disposable propane cylinders as a fuel source, small portable gas grills are more frequently referred to as “blow-torch cookers” to describe their hot and harsh cooking quality because their portability demands a compact design that leaves inadequate space between the gas burner and cooking grate for the bulky heat-diffusing rack (filled with ceramic briquettes) that gives larger grills a more steady temperature control, a more indirect and even distribution of heat to the cooking grate, and more flavor enriching smoke produced by the meat drippings hitting the hot briquettes.  However, after combining all of the 5-Star areas of a Weber Q-1200 compact grill with a removable *Heat Diffuser of my own design (*perhaps a future aftermarket accessory), its only 3-Star rating (cooking quality) rose to the 5-Star level to make it a truly and totally 5-Star compact/portable grill that’s ready to go toe-to-toe with those huge porch-dinosaurs in the flavor and cooking quality departments.    

MY RATINGS IN A NUTSHELL:

PROS:    All 5-Star Rated
1. Construction Quality  (good materials / quality fabrication as with all Weber products)
2. Size and Portability   (perfect for cooking six patties or small steaks / easy to carry and store)
3. Ease of Use   (very useful fold-out side trays / accurate control of burner’s flame height) 
4. Ease of Cleaning    (two-section enameled cooking grates easy to remove, clean and reinstall)
5. Design  (football-shape promotes circular convection flow to more evenly distribute internal heat) 
6. Replacement Parts Availability   (all components are available and owner replaceable)

CONS:  3-Star Rated
1.  Cooking Quality  (still much better than 1-2 star quality of other compact/portable gas grills)

**Cooking Quality w/ *Heat Diffuser = 5-Stars   (slower/controlled cooking, good smoke, juicy results)
 
Weber engineers did an outstanding job of designing a heavy, cast iron, enameled, 2-section cooking grate that quickly distributes and retains burner heat throughout the grate’s entire area much better than the skinny stainless steel or wire grates that come with most other compact grills.  Other great design features are the solid area in the cooking grates over the burner route to protect the item being cooked from direct exposure to burner flame along with parallel drip rails on the bottom to channel the drip path past both sides of the burner to help protect it from fouling and cogging of its flame orifices.  However, while cooking quality of the Q-1200 is better than my two previous compact grills (each quickly became garage sale items), there is good logic in guessing that direct-heating from the close-proximity burner produces an excessive cooking grate temperature that could easily be 150-200 degrees hotter than what is indicated by the hood thermometer and usually too hot for comfortable and controlled cooking even at low burner levels.  

Whether I pre-heated the grill at the middle or low temperature setting, it would quickly char very black and deep grate marks (that my wife found un-tasty) on hamburger patties just a couple of seconds after tossing them on the grate, and did the same to the other side after quickly flipping them over (leaving large chunks of charred meat stuck to the grate in the process).  As indicated by the included cooking chart, the patties would cook in about 8 minutes, but the exceptionally hot grate temperature required my constant attention and flipping them every few seconds.  Additionally, there wasn’t a lot of smoke produced, and the patties were a bit dry because most of the quickly expelled juices dribbled into the collection pan below.  Obviously, the greatest caveat of a fast cooking time on a very hot surface is the very narrow timeframe that lies between rare, medium and charred – especially with patties or cuts of meat less than 3/4” thick.

Being a retired major-city fire chief, radio communications engineer and lifelong tinker, I wasn’t about to let one minor detail spoil an otherwise perfect 5-Star product without giving it my best tinker-shot for a good resolution.  After measuring burner flame height at different settings and the distance between burner and bottom of cooking grate, I cobbled together a simple but extremely effective “heat diffuser” from a small piece of stainless steel scrap bummed from a nearby metal fabricating company.  The diffuser is quickly installed or removed, is not attached to any part of the grill, does not contact any part of the burner or cooking grates, does not interfere with burner flame or change its perfect two-tone light blue color (but it does make burner flame considerably more stable in gusty wind conditions), does not block or restrict proper air/heat circulation, and does not create any condition that could possibly extinguish burner flame and/or create a dangerous propane buildup if burner flame was extinguished by any other cause.  

What my new Heat Diffuser DOES do is bring the Q-1200’s cooking grate temperature down to a level more relative to large grills equipped with a heat diffuser rack laden with ceramic briquettes to leave only brown (not charred black) grate marks on meat being cooked, produces just as much cooking smoke as large grills by drippings falling onto heat diffuser (which also protects burner from contamination), greatly stabilizes burner flame during gusty wind conditions, makes the cooking grates much easier to clean without charred deposits, and cooks about 25% slower than most cooking times on the cooking chart - which gives more accurate control of rare-to-well done timing that leaves the meat much juicier, with more smoky flavor.  

Since my *Heat Diffuser makes such a radical improvement in cooking quality and is quickly removable (should anyone desire taking a step back to blow-torch cooking), I have initiated the process to obtain a “patent pending” classification because I am sure the huge popularity and high quality of the Q-series grills combined with the vast numbers already sold will instantly create a great sales potential for such a versatile and effective aftermarket accessory that I will soon begin publicizing via other reviews and on social media.  Obviously, I cannot submit pictures of my Heat Diffuser due to pending patent protection; however, only the superior design and construction quality of Weber Q-Series grills make possible such a relatively simple method of greatly improving its cooking quality.

title: My steaks wouldn’t sear until I did this...
text: I am new to grilling and using a Weber. For my first several attempts, nothing seared. Nothing at all. It was frustrating! I could get a better sear or on the stove then on my Weber. After trying multiple attempts, I finally did some research and figured out the problem. My propane gas tank was on bypass mode. After closing the gas gauge, waiting a minute or so and then opening the gas and lighting my Weber Grill, my steaks finally seared! I have no idea why my grill was in this mode, but if you are having trouble with your heat, check the propane tank! If your grill is not smoking like crazy while you are cooking at the highest heat with the lid down, than you are likely in bypass mode. It’s not you, the meat or the grill grates. At full capacity, the heat gets so high that my infrared thermometer can’t even detect the heat. That’s when you know you are using the heat to its capacity and not in bypass mode.

I purchased the weber igrill 3, and its useful but it has too many bugs, I would stay away from that and just get a reputable aftermarket one. I also wished it was a bit more portable to be able to put it in my truck. The grates are sturdy and leave great grill marks. I make sure to clean the outside when its completely cooled with degreaser to amke sure the side tables and handle stays clean and ready to go for the next use. title: I like everything about this grill except the GBS
text:
This is a great grill.  I upgraded from a basic 22" kettle because I was tired of the ash storm everytime I cleaned out the bottom of the grill.  The ash catcher is as good as I'd hoped and is going to cut down on the dusty mess all over my deck.  The added height of this grill is also nice, it's maybe 2 inches taller than a standard kettle.  The insulated handles for the lid and the lid vent are nice because they could get so hot on my old one.  The addition of a thermometer is a game changer.  Really nice to have.  There's one thing I do not like and it's the Gourmet Barbecue System grate.  It's heavy!  Heavier than the standard hinged grate, and definitely heavier than the basic unhinged one.  It's hinged on the sides which is nice but the center is a separate piece that is not secured in any way.  If you are accustomed to hanging your grate on the handle or side of grill while you light the coals you're going to have problems.  The center will fall right out.  And if you actually use your grill frequently the the center is going to get very black and very gunky and touching it with bare hands is going to be a mess.  Setting it down on something is going to make a mess.  Anything you do with this center piece is going to make a mess.  And even if it doesn't you're going to have to try and fit this thing in the center of the rest of the grate potentially over the hottest section of your fire.  
If they really wanted us to buy in on the Gourmet Barbecue System they should've included 1 or 2 of the inserts to demonstrate the benefits of the system with this $250 grill.  Instead they've given you a grate with a hole in the middle with no added benefits unless you want to plunk down between $45 and $65 a piece for the inserts.  In the end I bought myself a new standard hinged grate and will be happy with that.  
Oh and if you're assembling this thing please open the plastic bag that contains the lid handle.  The handle is the last thing you put on if you follow the directions but the wrench you need to do all the nuts in earlier steps is also in this bag.  Bad decision Weber.

title: Not the Weber Quality I was expecting
text:
This grill was bought at the end of the 2019 grilling season, after much research, for the Weber quality that I have experienced in the past with my Kettle Charcoal BBQ, and for the heat efficiency that Weber bbqs are also known for.  Additionally I liked the available colour options.  

When I received the BBQ, I inspected the packaging closely, and found no shipping damage.  This is significant since I didn't plan to assemble the BBQ until the 2020 grilling season, and the BBQ would remain in the box throughout the winter months. 

Therefore, I was extremely surprised to find what appeared to be production defects and other damage. 

1. The most significant was the damage to the grilling box.  The grilling box was cracked at the front edges, in nearly identical ways on both the front left and right side corners.  

2. The front edge of the lid, on the right side and BEHIND the lid handle was flared out, and the paint and enamel was severely chipped and cracked.  

3. There were dents on the supports, and the flanges of the leg parts were bent, making assembly difficult

4. One of the supporting screw receptors for the right-most burner dial was broken off

I am amazed that a product with obvious defects would be packaged so carefully in the box.  There was no damage to the exterior packaging, and none to the internal cardboard protection packaging (which is some of the strongest that I've ever seen).  That fact, and also the oddly protected locations of some of the biggest points of damage (behind the handle, at the front edges of the grill box) indicate that this grill was either not produced to standard, or was damaged prior to shipping. 

I am honestly surprised at what I have here, and more so at the volume of other reviews that appear to indicate similar experiences by others purchasers of this product.  

Winning reviews is one thing, but if a product cannot perform as reviewed, or as intended, or requires lengthy customer service intervention just to get to the point that you thought you were at when you purchased, then value is being lost.  Quality control matters.

title: Great grill, worth the price
text:
While the initial sticker shock for the grill may not immediately have you racing to put it in your cart, I can reassure you it's worth it.  Having friends and family who have over the years been burned (not literally) by cheaper grills only lasting 2-3 years, I didn't want the same outcome.  I knew I'd have to spend some money to get the appropriate quality for a grill that quite frankly gets used everyday.  And if I do end up having issues, I can rest easy knowing it's backed by a manufacturer 10 year warranty - something that certainly makes it easier to sleep at night.  Having used this grill for a few weeks now, I love it. Just make sure to do your research and take care of this BEFORE even using it.  The grates need 'seasoned' before first use, and using grill spray (anti-stick) is highly recommended since you are on bare cast iron, not your typical coated grates.  While this can be a pain, I assure you with proper use, it's much more efficient and if properly cared for will have a lifespan much longer than coated grates.  
My only gripe with this grill is the igniter seems to be finicky (as is the story with any grill, right?).  It has lit every single time, however sometimes it will take longer - at times up to 10 seconds.  I would think at this price point I'd get immediate ignition every single time.  However, this is definitely not a big enough issue to not make this worthy of your backyard.

text: I've been a Weber Kettle charcoal griller for over 25 years.  I recently purchased the Spirit E-210 gas grill.  Thankfully I purchased it assembled so I didn't have to deal with putting it together.  I took the removable contents out and my teenage son and I could easily carry the grill up 2 flights of stairs to my townhouse balcony.  I strongly recommend purchasing the perforated box that holds the wood chips.  I always use Mesquite chips when grilling and the flavor is very close to what I get with charcoal.  I will use my charcoal grill for special occasions like grilling a turkey or rib roast, but for every day use the Spirit E-210 is my go-to.  The price was right ($375 assembled) and the size is perfect for my townhouse balcony.  The biggest factor in the purchase was the 10 year warranty.  You can't beat that!!  I also like the ability to easily control the grilling temperature, and the grill surface is large enough that I can do most things on the indirect setting which helps cook things thoroughly without excess char.  The only thing it lacks is the side burner for sauces etc. but since I'm used to cooking with the charcoal kettle, that does not really pose a problem for me.  The models that had the side burner were 2-3 times the cost of this unit.  No question a 5 star rating on this model.

title: Good value, quality product
text:
When I received the grill, unfortunately one of the key parts was bent (and unusable), but Weber's customer service was really easy to work with and they sent me the replacement part pretty quickly. 

Once I received the part, I was surprised and how easy the grill was to assemble. I did it solo in under an hour (from start of step 1 to the final testing of it). Removing all the pieces from the box and dealing with the packaging probably took an additional 20-30 minutes. 

The grill itself has worked really well. The grates are wide enough that smaller things (like the inside rings of a sliced onion) don't easily fall through. The cooking surface is also shielded on three sides, so food does not roll off easily. So far (4 uses) the grill does not get up to super high heats with the lid closed, but does get up to 450-500 degrees if left closed. The grill has worked well with a 14"x11" plancha and gets/keeps the cast iron well heated. The side tables have been pretty sturdy so far, showing no signs of bending when I put meats and cutting boards on them. And the clip that holds the propane tank seems to be working really well--it's nice to see the tank getting lower and to have a consistent and quality seal between the tank and the tubing.

Overall, I'm really happy with the grill. I thought it was a touch pricey when I bought it, but there's value in what you're paying for. Would recommend this grill (or the two burner) to anyone who asks.

text:
The deep ocean blue color is beautiful, and the grill holds charcoal as I would expect. The included grate it turns out, is really a pain to deal with as the center insert constantly moves around (really annoying when cleaning). I'd prefer a heavy grate with larger hinged areas for adding charcoal (I read the premium kettle grade is lighter).  I also found the warming rack to be of dubious value as it blocks the hinges and is mostly just in the way... I'm not using it. Perhaps it will be valuable for some later use.
 
When I was flattening the shipping box there were a couple large paint chips on the bottom. Inspecting the (already assembled) grill, it looked like the paint had come off from the area outside when the legs attach. This made sense to me, as I had to use oil and a lot of (twisting) force to get the legs inserted (metal shave off the legs in the process) - I looked to me like there was excess paint buildup inside the leg holes so it makes sense it was excessive on the outside causing it to flake.

In all, I'd say I like it, but with reservations. I'm hopeful the paint issue will not cause further problems. I might recommend the lower-cost model instead to someone making a purchase.

text:
I have had lots of grills in the past - both large and small.  All of my big grills always, rusted, rotted, etc, do 5 years ago I finally spent more $$$ on a Weber Genesis 330 grill....it has been fabulous and still in perfect shape.

I needed an additional grill for occasional, portable use.  Since I loved the quality of my Genesis, looking at the Weber Q1200 and Q2200 was a no brainer.  I ended up selecting the Q1200 because it was a little smaller.  I also purchased the griddle, cart and bought an 11lb propane bottle and an LP tank connector.

When I received it, I thought it was going to be too small.  My first use was a small company picnic gathering.  The Q1200 was PERFECT!!!!  I put 24 hotdogs on the grill all the way out to all of the edges.  The heat distribution is perfectly even, no hot spots or cold spots.  ALL 24 hotdogs cooked at an identical speed and all were finished at the exact same time.

Since then, I now use it as my main grill at home and prefer it over my larger Weber Genesis 330.  I am usually only cooking for 2-6 people.  Because it cooks so evenly, you can use the ENTIRE grate surface and I can easily get 10 hamburger patties or 6 steaks or 2 London Broils on the grill.  All have cooked perfectly.

Because the grates are small, cleanup is a breeze.  I simply take them inside, clean them in the kitchen sink and put them in the dishwasher.  I haven’t tried the griddle yet, but I will on my next camping trip and am confident that it will work flawlessly for fixing breakfast.

Absolutely love it - no regrets or complaints!!!

I liked cooking on it so much that I decided to buy a new grill for my permanent residence in Michigan. I wanted a Weber because of the reputation and high customer satisfaction including my own. I must say I was rather shocked at how much pricier the Weber grills are compared to other grills. I could have bought a much larger grill in just about any other grill with many more bells and whistles for less money than this little grill. Since I'm a single person, I thought this would be plenty big enough for me. Well, for the most part it is big enough for just me, but if I have two or three guests, I quickly run out of grilling space to grill steaks and veggies at the same time. So I'd say its a great grill, but unsure if it was worth sacrificing the grilling space just so I could get a Weber.

title: Amazing! Best Cooking Implement on the Market!!
text:
This is by far the best purchase I’ve made during the 2020 quarantine. And probably in the last 10 years. For the last 15 years I’ve been cooking on a Weber Smokey Joe. We realized that it’s just too tiny for a family of four. But still love my SJ. I absolutely love this kettle grill! And I especially love the color. I even think the extra $30 for the Spring Green was worth it. I love all the extra features, the char baskets, the gourmet barbecue system grill, the lid bail, the top vent grip, everything is just great. My wife and daughter really love the green color, it makes them smile when they see it on the back patio. So far I’ve done a couple top sirloins, some hotdogs and a six pound bone in pork shoulder that came out absolutely sublime. In fact that pork shoulder is probably the best thing I’ve ever cooked in my life. We’ve been eating pulled pork for the last three days and it’s still just amazing! I cooked that bad boy for eight hours and I could not believe how easy it was to control the temperature by just using the top and bottom vents. I followed the instructions on the Weber website using 72 briquettes (36 in each basket) and 16 lit briquettes. I used two Weber lighter cubes to get the briquettes started in my Weber charcoal chimney. I then used the two char baskets on either side using the modified minion method with eight lit briquettes in each one. On top of those I put two medium sized chunks of oak and to my amazement, for eight hours I did not have to add any briquettes for the entire cook. It maintained temp at 250F give or take for eight hours. Unbelievable!!! I thought long and hard about getting a pellet grill but I feel like the design, the functionality, the aesthetic, the back to basic nature of the Weber kettle grill is just perfect. I feel like I’m actually becoming a better cook (was never really a good cook in the first place) just by having this grill. I wish I could convey in this review how excited I am about my Weber Master Touch in Spring Green. If you’re reading this review it means that you’re seriously considering purchasing one... I would say don’t hesitate, go ahead and pull the trigger. You won’t be disappointed.

*one complaint... One of the holes for the lid bail was drilled too high and didn’t allow the plastic spindle to spin freely or the lid to sit down completely. I had to file that hole down a little bit to drop the lid bail down a quarter inch. Very minor, but still a QC issue that should be looked into.

By the way… I’m using a ThermoPro TP20S wireless meat thermometer. Which I also highly recommend.

text:
Bought this grill after a cheaper grill gave out after 3 or 4 years. Spent a little more for this grill based on the warranty, strong reviews, and salesperson talking up their customer service. Hard to regulate the temperature--even at lowest heat setting it has a hard time keeping under 400 degrees.  After 1 year of relatively light use the hose and regulator assembly began leaking.  While I assume the warranty should take care of it I've been unable to get ahold of Weber to talk to them which is the most disappointing aspect of the entire purchase as I was told their service was great.  I called and after getting the IVR message that hold times were long I chose the option for them to call me back when an agent freed up.  Waited all night without a call.  Assuming the customer service line was closed I then decided to email to inform them of both my grill issue and the customer service issue and we're at 3 and a half days with no response other than the automated email stating they received my email and would get back to me.  In the review process they ask that we not write about customer service problems but contact them instead; however, often when someone decides on a purchase their deciding based on the service and integrity of the company as much as the product.  I don't know that it makes sense to not take that into consideration in the review.  

In short, there's nothing necessarily wrong with the product but if going to have some of the same issues you have with a lesser priced grill and not receive good service/support you might as well save the money and buy the lesser grill.

title: Pay attention!!!!!
text: We have had Weber grills in the past, and chose to invest almost $500 in our newest grill. I would like to point something out, and maybe save someone else the embarrassment of going thru what we did.    The grill was assembled by the retailer. When we did the set up tests, we could not get the temp to go above 410 degrees. We called the customer service number, and a very helpful person talked us thru multiple steps, then determined we probably needed a new hose/regular set, which the company promptly sent. We replaced that, and still had problems with the temp not going high enough. We were waiting for a return call from customer service, when we figured out the problem.  The knobs to control the heat seem counter-intuitive to me. When they are turned all the way on, they are actually at "low" heat. Turning them just a very small amount turns them on "high". Once we realized that, the grill heated up quickly to 600 degrees. This was totally our fault- not any problem with the grill. The front of the grill has markings that indicate high-medium-low, and the manual also shows that. The problem was on our end- assuming that turning the knobs all the way would be "high", and partially turning them would be "low".  So, heads up! Save yourself the frustration and embarrassment we went thru!

title: Best grill I have ever owned.
text:
I've been a charcoal grill man my entire life, but recently with my grill (a 7 year old Charbroil) wearing out and charcoal shooting up to 8 dollars a bag I wanted to make the switch to gas.

After looking at many different sizes and models it came down to the Weber Spirit II E-210.

I must admit I was worried going into it as it did seem to be an awful lot of money for a small grill. Rest assured it's worth every single penny.

The overall quality of every piece is far superior to other models I looked at. It's also much bigger than you think it is. No, it's not going to grill for a party of 20 in one go, but it's more than enough for our family of four and no doubt could handle a party of 10 to 12 with relative ease.

The temperature control is what is so amazing about it. I've waited to write this review until I had at least 12 cookouts on it.

You'll be used to where your temperature ranges are by the time you get 4 or 5 cookouts under your belt. On mine, the second to the lowest setting on both knobs gives you a perfect 300 degrees for slower cooking. Up one mark takes it to 325. The half way marker is a perfect 400 degrees.

I'm sure that may very from grill to grill just a bit, but fact is once you get the temperature where you want it, just look where your knobs are set. It will be that way every single time you use it. It makes it very, very easy to have the same results every time.

The grills are also great. I, oddly, follow the directions and there's no stick at all on them. They're fantastic! I actually use a plastic spatula so I don't scratch the ceramic coating off.

I've cooked burgers, chicken, pork chops, ribs and steaks and never had anything stick.

It heats up quickly too thanks to its smaller size so you don't waste so much gas like you do on a larger model. In 10 to 12 minutes you're at 400 degrees no problem.

It's just a really, really well made and well engineered grill.

The only thing I'm yet to really try on it is off heat slow cooking, but I'll cross that bridge when I get to it.

If you're on the fence about buying this grill wondering if it'll be enough and if it's worth it, climb on down on this side and buy it. You'll be very glad you did.

title: Weber’s Spirit II is a solid GO!
text: This is my second Weber LP gas grill. Assembly took a little over an hour, and the instructions were clear. Weber has taken some excellent steps in protecting the burners on the Spirit II compared to their older models. The crossover tube is now protected from grease drippings with welded shields on it that are positioned between the flavorizer bars. The burners themselves run front to back, instead of side to side as my previous grill did. I do see that configuration as a minor annoyance, as when grilling over direct heat, I used to be able to use just one burners for 7 hamburger patties, where now I have to use both burners, resulting in a bit of heavier gas consumption.  This brings me to my next point. The Spirit II is not a big grill. It made sense for me though, in that I am not feeding a full family, nor throwing parties. I did invest in the optional iGrill 3 (with the lowercase ‘i’, I can only wonder if Apple was involved in the creation of it) accessory, and I hope you will too. Installation was a snap, although this amazing complement to your Weber setup will add $100 to your total cost. That’s worth it, at least to me. My only complaint about the iGrill 3 system is that it doesn’t tell you when to flip your steaks. True grillmasters may not care, but there are those of us that do. We want perfection, Weber, so please upgrade your app. Having been a Weber owner for 30 years, I can clearly see that the company has taken great strides in improvements in build quality and overall ease of use. Whether you are a grilling newbie, or a seasoned pro, the Spirit II will not disappoint.

The problem is, I was never the griller; my husband was. I had no idea how where to start, but I was determined to figure it out.  I began my research.  I shopped and compared and read reviews...I really did my homework. If I was going to do this, I wanted a user-friendly quality grill that I could really enjoy that was not too big or too small.  Along came the Weber Spirit II E-210 gas grill. Absolutely everything about it is perfect for me. Assembly was easy with a well-explained assembly manual, as was the start up process. I did it all by myself. I registered my grill which is more like joining a family; the Weber family.  I read about care, I was provided recipes, and mostly I felt like I had someone to contact with questions if needed.  I have not had any questions. Weber makes it so easy; you are virtually guaranteed success. I grill on my Spirit II multiple times a week.  I use their tools and grill accessories and have even expanded my menu. Clean up is a breeze; I use the Weber grill spray when cooking and cleaner after. If a 64 year old widow with no grilling experience can do this, anyone can. To be honest, my family is shocked. Family members with plenty of grilling experience are now trading in old grills for Weber grills.  I really wish I could better explain what a positive experience this has been.
