text: This isn't my first gas grill, but it is my first Weber.  And what a difference.  I puchased this 2 burner Spitit II grill from my local garden store where they offered free assmmbly and delivery. The grill is just the right size for my needs. I like the built in gage that will let me know when the LP gas is running low and needs to be replaced. No more guessing if I have enough gas to get through a meal. I am impressed by how thick sturdy the cooking grates are, much better than the old rusted grill I am replacing.  But what I really love is that I didn't just get a grill, I got the Weber company's support and knowlegde of how to actually cook properly on a gas grill. For years all I ever had was a charchoal grill where you just waited for the coals to get hot and then you put the food on the grate and that was that. Even with my old gas grill I never thought to do anything different.  But then I read some of the grilling tips on the Weber sight when I regisered my grill, and I learned about direct and indirect heat, and setting the temperature for the right foods, and using something other than just aluminum foil to keep food from falling through the grates. So I have now learned, thanks to Weber.com, to use a cast iron skillet to cook my fish, and how to do ribs in foil in one hour, and cook veggies properly. As a result I am using the grill much more often and enjoying the pleasures of eating on my deck and look forward to trying many more of the recipes on Weber.com

Assembly was easy and once completed grill seems sturdy and solid. It took me about 2.5 cooks to get the hang (develop the muscle memory) of having the lid off of the grill with the interior hook but now that I have it works flawlessly.  Grill space is more than ample. Ash cleaning system is simple, elegant and effective - I love it!.

The only relatively minor complaint I have is that the hooks on the front handle to hold tools seem a bit close to the kettle itself.  Tongs, spatulas and whatnot can tend to get somewhat uncomfortably hot when running hotter fires in the kettle (steaks etc.) Not a huge issue, doesn't make me love my kettle any less but it might me nice to have a heat shield on the front handle like the one on the top of the lid to combat this.

I have requested a new regulator twice.  Once on the website where we registered the grill and I emailed them too.  I never heard anything back. The only suggestion I would make is the design of weighted pressure gauge system.  There are little nubs which hold the tank out away from side of the unit, but they are too short.  The rim of the tank sits on the wheel axle.  This creates an inaccurate measurement.  The numbs also catch in the label of the tank...causing further issues.

I'm still giving the grill a 5-star rating.  It heats well with only minor hot/cold spots.  Far superior to any previous grill. title: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill - Great Investment
text:
I have purchased different grills, for less money, and have been dissatisfied with the short life, inaccurate cooking temperatures and the deficient heating elements.  
I have purchased other Weber Grills and been very satisfied with the workmanship and the quality of the grills, but at times, the cost was prohibitive. When necessary, I replaced the inner elements; the Weber site makes ordering parts very easy and the support has always given me backup if I encountered problems.  When the ceramic grates were introduced, exclusively thru Home Depot, I couldn't wait to see how they preformed and I was not dissapointed.  We relocated to Florida and did not bring our old bar-be-que, so when we decided we really missed outdoor cooking, we bought the Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill and have not been disappointed!  The price was excellent (it was on sale at Home Depot and they delivered it, completely assembled) and it is more compact (great for our space), looks nice and has great features.  I'm still learning new ways after 50 years of grilling and I still check the Weber site for new cooking hints and different maintenance tips, but overall, I have been very pleased with this model and definitely would recommend it.  The recipes offered on the Weber are easy to follow and quite tasty, too.

title: Dynamic Dining Adventures
text: I watched a few online videos before unboxing the grill and completing the assembly. From start to finish, it took about 30 to 45 minutes. The Weber Master-Touch 22" grill was my first charcoal grill, and from the first cook of smoked jerked chicken wings to my last cook of sixteen lbs of pork picnic, the Weber Master-Touch Charcoal 22" grill is a pleasure to use. The charcoal baskets help keep the coals in order and match perfectly with the hinged GBS cooking grate. The Gourmet BBQ System has many different add-ons. I'm considering the waffle iron. The Master-Touch holds ample fuel to cook for six to eight hours comfortably. The most helpful feature of the grill is the large ash basket. I grill on my patio, and there is no mess when finished. The Master-Touch 22" cleans up nicely too. I wasn't sure if I would use the added warming rack system that came with the grill, but it is ideal for warming rolls and keeping the vegies hot while the burgers and dogs are getting happy. I enjoy the aroma of charcoal and apple, hickory, or mesquite. As much as I've used my gas grill, the Master-Touch adds a whole new dynamic to the dining adventure. I expect to have many years of enjoyment from this grill. It's well built, and all the parts were well packaged and in the box. Nothing was damaged, and the lid and bowl were both round and fit perfectly. As I'm writing this review, I'm thinking of my next grilling event; fish or tri-tips? So many choices.

I ordered a new Master-Touch 22" Weber and in a few days it arrived while my 7 year old grandson was visiting. We pulled the parts out and to my surprise he started to organize the components to help me put it together.  It went together so easily I think my grandson could have completed it on his own!

title: Happily grilling once more!
text:
This excellent grill was surprise gifted me, by my daughters, on my birthday I have been without a grill for 5 long years.

After unboxing, then using the online app, assembly took about an hour and fifteen minutes. It heats up incredibly fast...550f in less than 15 minutes. Cooking on it is a pleasure. Some practice with temperature control will allow keeping temperatures as low as about 215f (as read on the built in thermometer.) My experience with grils is that is an approximate reading, as the actual reading is usually maybe 15-20f cooler. I haven't noticed any particularly cooler spots on the grill, though overall, at least for me, the rear 2/erds of the grill seem a wee bit hotter.

The starter works as advertised. BTW, I would heartily recommend a full 20# tank, not the tanks sold at the big box stores. Mine is from U-Hall, has a gauge on it which visually lets you know about how much propane remains. They are $35, plus filling. No more than the ones sold at the other places. 

It's a Weber, and works like one, from build quality to features. I have yet to use the smart bluetooth thermometer hookup as yet. That will be a Christmas present to myself!!

I heartily recommend the Spirit 2 E-300 as an all around fine grill.

title: Great Grill - Assembly Is A Pain
text:
This is not my first Webber gas grill. My previous ones lasted 10+ years each.

The good:
(1) The grill lights easily. The newer ignition module that takes an AA battery keeps clicking as long as you hold down the button. With the older piezo igniter you had to push repeatedly if it didn’t catch the first time.
(2) The (cast iron it looks like, with a surface treatment of some kind) grill surface seems to be more “spatula friendly” in that it is flatter on top. Time will tell if it is as durable as the old “continuous cleaning” stamped steel grill surface.
(3) The grilling surface seems large enough for all but large gatherings - read the description, it gives the grill area.
(4) The quality seems to be what I expect from Webber.

Needs Improvement:
(1) Assembly is a real pain. In order to fit into a smaller box, there were more smaller pieces of the frame parts which meant it seemed like there were nearly twice as many pieces in the box to assemble than my old Webber Genesis Silver had been. While the instructions are clear enough, you have to pay a lot of attention to which way certain parts are oriented as there are subtle differences in symmetry between left and right parts for example - And I am a retired engineer! It takes two people to assemble this, by the way. It would be difficult for one person to do all the steps.
(2) While I like the continuous re-strike ignition of the newer battery operated ignition module verses the older piezo igniter, I have a concern with battery life in an outdoor appliance like this. It uses a single AA battery. At least it’s easy enough to change. And by the way, the battery that came with it was dead because it had been packed bare inside a plastic bag of metal screws and hardware that obviously shorted out the original battery in transit.

All in all, once assembled the grill is easy to use and seems to be of good quality. But assembly is a real pain.

title: Tried and true.  Why mess with success?!
text:
We decided it was time to bid farewell to our TWENTY ONE year old Weber grill this week - and after looking at many other brands and models, we ultimately decided to replace it with the new version (Spirit II E-310) of the same model (Spirit II 700 series). Why mess with success??

My late husband and I bought our Spirit 700 series to cook on while we were renovating our kitchen in 1999 and I’ve cooked on it year-around ever since. I’ve replaced the grates, the ‘flavorizer bars,’ the regulator hose, and we’ve been using stick lighters for years (the ignition failed long ago) - but when the bottom rotted out, we knew its time had come. Webbie ended up ‘costing’ about $2 a month over 21 years. Not so bad.

We've cooked meals on the new grill every night since getting it, and it's every bit as wonderful as the old one, if not better!  I highly recommend Weber grills!!

title: Best Choice!
text:
I considered for a long time before I chose this grill. I wanted something compact (hence the fold-down side table) that wouldn't take up much space on my porch. I also wanted something that would last for "the rest of our lives", as my husband and I are "seniors".
A third feature is ease of lighting.
A bonus I hadn't counted on, but have been delighted to find is the even, consistent heating. And it heats FAST, also!

I have been assembling grills as a job for the last three years, and I've seen a lot of different brands and models. NONE of the other grills has the quality of materials as the Webers. This explains why they can offer the best warranty in the industry. (I suspect some brands are just hoping folks won't make good on their warranties, because you can tell they won't last.)
My only complaint is the plastic knobs for the burners. (another Weber grill has metal ones, so I don't know why ALL their models don't)

Ease of cleaning was another consideration, since I intend this grill to serve into my elder years. So far I've found if I clean each time I use it, (something motivated by the price our kids paid to get this for Father's Day), it is easy to clean. NO grill should be neglected and not cleaned, or it becomes very hard to clean. The grease tray is easy to reach and remove, and if I were so inclined, I could buy replacement tray liners, and just dispose of the liner each time, instead of emptying it.

If you are considering a grill, think about how this Weber will outlast 3 or 4 other grills, so it's worth the investment!

title: Great quality luxury purchase
text:
This grill is replacing a Charbroil that I bought on sale around 10 years ago. I'm pleased that it lasted 10 years before falling apart, so I was tempted to go the cheap route again. The problem, though, is even when it was working, it never cooked well. The meat had to be right over the burners or it would take a really long time to cook. So I decided to spend more on a Weber based on the reputation.

I bought this unassembled so I can fit it in my car to bring home. Even so, the box was too big for my trunk, so I needed to take the parts out of the box to fit. Once I managed to get it home, it was a breeze to assemble. I don't remember ever seeing assembly instructions that were so clear. It was actually an enjoyable experience. 

And it works just as I expected a Weber to. The ignition lights effortlessly, unlike the frustrating click buttons that I was used to. And there is a scale that shows how much propane is left in the tank, another useful perk. The whole thing seems more solid than any of my other grills ever did. I can tell this will last a long time. And the cooking...it is perfect. The cooking surface is small compared to other grills for sale, but the whole surface is heated evenly and therefore not wasted. So even though this is a little smaller than my Charbroil, I can cook a whole lot of more food at once. And with the thermometer and burner knobs that actually control the temperature, I can cook much better than I could with the Charbroil. 

The only problem was the price. It is very expensive, and a luxury purchase. If it is worth it depends on how much you use it.

title: Easy to assemble!
text:
For the past 25 years, we've been using a Weber Genesis gas grill.  It was great, but 25 years is 25 years.  If we got another, we'd have to find a place for it in our wills, so we went for a charcoal grill.

I was a bit concerned by the reviews that said this thing is hard to assemble, but I find myself to be in disagreement with them.  This grill was easy to assemble, though one does have to do a bit of coaxing and pushing and twisting and begging to get the wheeled legs into their receptacles.  Weber provides a small plastic wrench for tightening some of the nuts, and the only other tools you need are a hammer (better - a rubber mallet) and a screwdriver.

The grill works great.  Keeps the Weber briquettes going, and I like that you can lift up the hinged edges of the grate to add more, which is great for long sessions.

We've been barbecuing with CNG and LP for a long time.  Almost forgot the great taste of charcoal grilled steaks.

title: Versatile Grill and Smoker!
text:
I bought this grill because I wanted to experience the flavor of cooking over charcoal. What I got and discovered was so much more! Of course you can use this grill as a traditional charcoal grill but you can also use it as a smoker with no modifications required.
I found many YouTube videos of people using the Weber kettle to smoke all kinds of meats. All you need to do is set the charcoal to the side of the kettle for indirect cooking, add some wood for smoke and use the vents to control the temperature for low and slow smoking!
I've successfully smoked salmon, turkey, chicken, pulled pork, pork ribs, beef ribs, brisket. Even adding wood to give your traditional grilling some smoke flavor. One of the best steaks I've make was simply by using some hickory and the reverse sear method. I produced tender, perfectly cooked steaks with amazing smoke flavor that made me sigh with pleasure and satisfaction.

The kettle is well though out with the one touch cleaning system to remove ash. Sometimes is requires you to nudge the ash towards the cleaning wings but I have no complaints. 

This is my go-to grill for max flavor. I do have a Weber Genesys propane grill that I use when I can't wait for the charcoal to set up.

title: The Quality Is Worth The Price
text:
I have heard for years that Weber grills are well worth the extra cost, yet foolishly bought other brands that were on their way to becoming junk after one or two seasons.  Then it was a matter of paying more than I should have to replace rusted parts for several more years.  Fortunately, my neighbor told me about the quality and longevity of his Weber.  

This 2-burner Weber Spirit II is studier than any grill I have ever used, and I expect it will last a long time.  I also bought a Weber cover, and it is every bit as rugged, and seems likely to last for many years.  I guess time will tell, but there’s another matter I never considered much:  this Weber cooks better than any grill I’ve owned.  The cooking grates alone are better than I’d have imagined.  I just treat them like a good cast iron skillet and keep them well seasoned.  Is there REALLY a difference in the food?  You bet there is!  

My only regret is that I waited way too long to do this!  I wish I had just invested the extra bucks and bought a Weber years ago.  I’d have saved a lot of money in the long run.  

One other smart move I made was to buy the grill at our local Ace Hardware, who had a special deal where they assembled the grill for free, AND they assembled it properly.  I read way too many reviews where people bought grills from big box stores like Home Depot where they preassembled ( more like slapped together ) by people who were barely out of their teens and who couldn’t care less about the quality.  Then, the grills often sit out on the floor, if not outside, and get filthy.  If nothing else, get your grill in the box and assemble it yourself, if you can.  If you don’t believe me, go to your local home improvement store and inspect the grills chained together sitting outside.

Another Suggestion: get a container of disposable wipes for cleaning stainless steel.  There are several stainless steel surfaces on the grill, and stainless can be a pain to clean.  After reading all about using microfiber cloths and special cleaning products, I decided it was all too much bother.  I got the wipes at Walmart, and they come in a plastic container just like disinfectant wipes.  It’s easy to keep it in a box on my deck, use one or two wipes before I put the cover back on, then I don’t have to launder a microfiber rag.  The grill sparkles, it’s effortless, and fresh wipes are always at the ready.

Anyhow, for anyone looking at grills- save yourself the grief and quit wasting money- just buy a Weber.

The other features built in thermometer, propane gauge & large side folding shelf were a plus. I would have given it five (5) stars, but I found out it was made in "China". If at all possible I will not buy anything made in China if I can avoid it! I want USA made products only, including my vehicles.

title: Couldn`t be happier!
text:
Absolutely love the fool-proof ignitor !!!!!!!!!!!!
Steaks and burgers are seared better and taste better using the wide side up on the cast grates!
The convenient and included tank monitor lets you know when its time to refill, so you don`t run out of propane in the middle of grilling.

title: Great for burgers and dogs
text:
This is a great little grill for cooking up to eight burgers or lots of hot dogs at a time. I’ve also had success with salmon, pork chops, corn, and vegetables in a tray.

There are a few drawbacks, including it isn’t quite large enough use my standard veggie tray while cooking anything other than dogs/sausage. This is because the tray’s handles touch the curved top, and the only way it closes is when the tray is in the center, leaning little grill space around the perimeter for other items. Of course, this is meant to be a small portable grill, so it’s an acceptable compromise.

My main struggle is with controlling the heat for slower cooking. I think the challenge is the burners are close to the grill, so even on the lowest setting the grill surface is quite hot, leading to more charring unless I flip frequently. This has mainly been a problem when cooking skinless chicken with marinades.

All-in-all, it is a great little portable grill, but at home I prefer my Spirit II due to the larger cook surface, better lid geometry, and better control over the surface heat.

title: Don’t like the flare ups.......
text: Love Weber products and have owned Weber grills for decades. I purchased my Weber Spirit II to replace a larger version that lasted for 15 years. I downsized due to price and being an empty nester. The second time I grilled (hamburgers) I had several large-sized flare-ups during the grilling process. It scared me. I don’t recall having flare ups to this degree with my former Weber grills. I now clean/hand wash the flavor bars, drip pan and grates every time before grilling to diminish the flare ups. I also wipe down the interior sides and bottom of the grill with a soapy cloth to clean grease/marinade drippings. There isn’t an issue with chicken, yet I grilled steaks on two different occasions resulting in big flare ups. I realize the fat content of meat causes flare ups, yet never had problems grilling rib-eyes before. Because the flavor bars and depth of the grill is closer together/more compact, I think this is a contributing factor of the flare ups. I’ve also noticed the flavor grills the enamel has bubbled, pitted and in a few area has rust. Never an issue with my past Weber grills. I have concerns the flavor bars will have to be replaced sooner rather than later. The grill has a cover and kept cleaned so unsure why I’m already experiencing some problems with the grill. The only time I’ll grill burgers or steaks is when my son comes home as the large flare ups scare me. My son said “mom have a fire extinguisher close by if I’m not there.” I grew up in California with many fires so I have a healthy respect/minor phobia with fire.

title: Love the grill ~ but it is not easy to move around
text:
The first grill I purchased was Weber, and I still have the rotisserie from when I bought it over 15 years ago. That one died, and I was so happy to purchase a new Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill last month. I love the grill, the flip-down shelf, and the fact that the propane tank is located on the side which makes it easy to see the level of gas and is easy to remove. 

However, there is one major flaw which makes it very difficult to manuever/move the grill.  The wheels are located on the side with the stable shelf. There should be some kind of handles installed by the flip/down shelf to grab when moving the grill. When the shelf is in the down position, the edges are very sharp. It takes 2 people on either side of the grill to move it. 

Another disappointment are the plastic wheels.  The first time I used the grill, the wheels came off!  I found the cotter pin and called the location I purchased the grill to help me in putting it back together (which was not easy).  The Weber Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill is a very solid construction ~ except for the plastic wheels and no handles to grab in order to move the grill.

text: Love it! This grill is a dependable work-horse. We do A LOT of grilling. It's very easy to control the temperature and I have yet to find a "hot spot".  It cooks evenly -- we've cooked corn on the cob, pork steaks, chops, chicken, kebabs, you name it.  We are VERY satisfied with this grill and highly recommend it.  The only modification we made was to purchase an adapter that allowed us to hook up a standard sized propane tank to it.  We had the same model years ago that we loved that got stolen off of our patio.  For some idiotic reason we replaced it with a larger Kitchenaid model we bought at one of the big box stores.  What a mistake!  The Kitchenaid model had hot and cold spots and there was no controlling the temperature.  It was either 0 or 600 degrees.  Ridiculous considering the money we paid for it.  We got so fed up, we went back to this little baby and haven't looked back.  Thanks Weber!  And thanks for the excellent customer service as far as the shipping and packing (we purchased the grill on the Weber website).  A very positive experience, overall.

text:

text:

Cons: Although it is easy to clean, food tends to burn onto the grates and it is almost impossible to get rid of some of it. I think I’m a little OCD when it comes to it and others may not even notice, just my observation. 
My grill gets a deep clean every other use (grates, flavorizer bars, cook box, outside) and I noticed today that one of the flavorizer bars is damaged. The coating cracked and parts of it fell off (maybe a bad batch, nothing major, will talk to Weber CS about it).
It takes some time to get used to a 3 burner grill (for me who has never had one with more than 1 burner) and it’s a little challenging find the best spot on the grates (for heat, nice dear marks etc), but overall, the grill is awesome and it appears that the heat distribution is pretty even.
It took me 1 year to pull the trigger on a new grill but I’m glad all the research paid off, Weber makes some of the sturdiest and best built grills out there, it doesn’t wobble, not loose screws or attachments and a breeze to use and move.

title: My Weber Experience
text:
I bought my first Weber Kettle grill in 1985. There's a lot of imitators on the market but they've never compared in quality or in their ability to adapt to various methods of cooking. I've cooked pizza's, smoked chicken, pork butts, ribs and even prime rib along with the never ending list of fish, burgers, sausages, chops and of course steak. Controlling the temperature has never been a problem.

I've never bought a gas grill, though I have been given them as presents for Father's Day over the years. They'd usually last about two years before I'd have to start replacing parts. I'm not really sure how many I've taken to the curb on trash day but it was something that was repeated often. Always eyeing a Weber but receiving something else I'm thankful this year that has changed. I finally received a Weber gas grill to go along with my Weber Kettle and Smokey Mountain Smoker.... I couldn't be happier! Assembly was easy and didn't take very long. I'm not sure what I like best about the grill but the list is extensive. Some of the things I like (not in order) are the grates and how they give great sear marks, how easy it is to clean, that it comes up to temperature very quickly and at a glance (without lifting) I know how much gas is in the cylinder. The grill heats up amazingly fast and holds it's temperature very well! The quality of the components is top notch and let's not forget how well finished it is! I am extremely pleased with this grill and just like all my other Weber grills, I know it will last a long long time.

Right out of the box, it worked better than I had hoped.  I seasoned the grill by cooking high fat hamburgers on it a few times, then I put it to work smoking.  I added a gasket around the lid, just to help with heat retention.  I also went and purchased a digital thermometer with two probes.  One for grate temp and other for internal temp of meat.  Still getting used to how to dial in temp but I can't complain.  I used a 2X1 snake method to smoke an 11lbs brisket and the charcoal lasted well over 16 hours without refilling.  I was even able to use last coal to start another pile to cook baked potatoes to have with brisket.

BUY THIS GRILL!!  You will not be disappointed!

title: Some improvements and some shortcomings
text:
This is my 4th Weber kettle over the past 30 years.  They are my favorite grills.  I've used each one until it fell apart.  Here's my review of this one.

Pro's:

- This is my first kettle that has the bracket to hold the lid when the grill is open.  I like that much better than the hook that was inside the lid of my previous kettles.
- I like the handles and the handle on the lid vent much better.  My previous kettles had wood handles that rotted and nothing insulated on the lid vent, so I would have to open and close that with an oven mitt.
- I like the warming rack.  Never had one before.  It's really nice for getting food farther from the heat.
- I like the new shape of the cutouts in the one-touch cleaning system.  It provides more precise control over air intake into the grill, and thus the grill's internal temperature.

Cons:

- My #1 con is the new ash catcher design.  It's much harder to reattach after emptying, and there's enough of a gap that plenty of ashes fall out on the ground, even when the ash catcher is empty.  Epic fail as far as I'm concerned.
- The cooking grate, with the separate center section that can be taken out to use accessory cooking devices.  I have no interest in using other devices (I have all the accessories to do all that already), so this is nothing but an annoyance for me (the center grate falls out whenever I remove the grate - like to start a fire.  It also has a tendency to flip and fall through the grate when I'm cleaning the cooking grate with a brush).  I dislike this so much that I'm going to spend more to get a solid cooking grate.

Frankly, if I had it all to do again, I'd have bought another original kettle.

text: Got my grill SII-E210.  Put it together in about 2 hours this morning.  It was easy.  HOWEVER:  1.  Read and follow, exactly, precisely, the instructions.  Don't skip ahead, don't think you know how it goes together.  READ and FOLLOW the instructions EXACTLY and all will be well.  2.  The only real dangers are cross-threading one of the multitude of screws or breaking the weld on one of the nuts.  Take your time and get the screws started correctly and use a wrench to hold the nuts as you tighten.  3.  The instructions say to use a soft surface.  Do so.  I laid all the parts out on a rug in the garage and put the hardware in a Plano box (fishing lures box) labeled "A", "B" etc.  The leg pieces are screwed together from the end and side.  Start the end screws first and let them pull the side holes into alignment instead of trying to force and hold it.  The grill fit together correctly, all necessary parts and hardware were in the box, and nothing was damaged out of the box.  Basically an easy assembly - IF you read and follow the instruction. title: Good Grill.
text:
Whenever I hope to connect with the countless generations which came before me, forgotten and unknown - stretching into the past, I try to focus on whatever genuine pleasures we share. 

Pleasures before literacy. 

Pre-literate pleasure.  
Before any faint scent of epistemology could enter one's consciousness other than through a proximate contemporary. A history derived completely from the anecdotal.

What united us? 
What united our forbears, huddled together against the cold and certain death from predators, real and imagined, longing for safety.

What brought joy to those who genetically dwell in me, though separated by the millennia, pleasure?

Sex? Undoubtedly. 

A stomach filled with nourishment? Surely.

But fire. 


Now fire.

A hearth. A communal hearth.

Warmth.

Safety?

A sure way of warding off the superstitious and real threats of the night.

The smell of roasted meat (which drew the superior beings, known as dogs, to strike a selfish bargain with our species from which we have profited since its inception) giving our progenitors fits of ecstasy from the flame-kissed smells and tastes. 

Drawing together.



As I come home from work and ponder the complex nature of existence and my righteous and unrighteous complaints regarding modern life, I take warm comfort in communion with my ancestors.

I can't fix everything.

But I can grill a pretty fierce zucchini.

I may be elderly and unable to synthesize poison from natural ingredients and anneal it to a homemade dart in order to expel it from a blowgun into an unsuspecting eland and subsequently run it down over miles and drag it back home to the communal hearth, but I can delight my wife and family with a variety of evenly cooked meats on an autumn eve, toasting those that came before me with joy and fellowship across the years.

Thanks Weber.

title: Big grill performance in a compact form
text:
I have been using this grill almost daily now for the past two months and am thoroughly satisfied. You get your money's worth in terms of quality.
With its fold down sides it takes up a modest footprint in my small back yard and yet has sufficient grilling area to cook for eight or more with ease. It ignites with no hiccups and heats to 500F in less than 10 minutes. This burns off most of the debris from the previous use. Once I've taken my stainless steel bristle to it, I put on a heat-proof mitt and wipe down the grids with a paper towel soaked with a bit of cooking oil. I find this makes the grids effectively non-stick.
I've used it for various methods -- direct heat, indirect heat and as an alternative to a conventional oven and it has performed well in each scenario. I do find it helps to use a hard bristle tooth brush to clean the holes in the burners carefully and periodically. Depending on the kind of grilling I've been doing, I lift out the grids etc. so I can clean the sides and bottom with a plastic scraper. Too much fatty, sugary (BBQ sauce) build-up and the thing will flare alarmingly!
This is my first Weber and of the previous grills I've owned it is far and away the easiest to assemble. It really helps to read the instructions first! In all it took me just over an hour.
The built-in weigh-scale for the propane tank is very useful and pretty accurate. Besides, it's always prudent to keep a full tank on standby as a precaution.
I also bought the custom Weber cover for this grill and am hoping it will extend its life by reducing rust. We'll see in a few year's time.

It fits nicely on my upper deck which is just outside my kitchen. The convenient location means I use it often, about 3+ times a week. The two shelves fold down for a very small footprint. It comes up to temperature very quickly and achieves surprisingly high temps (500+) . Even with just two burners, it is easy to create direct and indirect heat zones to suit whatever you are grilling. We are a small family of three, and this grill is more than adequate for our needs. When we have company and need more capacity, I go downstairs to the larger lower deck, where I have a larger unit. I use the E-210 more than my other grills by far. title: Awesome alternative to charcoal grill!
text:
Super efficient and great alternative to traditional charcoal kettle grill. I have the large Weber charcoal grill and have been using it for years. I cook burgers, dogs, fish and shrimp direct and also use it for long low and slow cooks of ribs chicken and brisket.  Only issue is that it takes awhile for the grill to get ready and it’s not ideal for a quick on the go on last minute feed. We bought this gas grill as an alternative for times when we want something quick and delicious but do not have the time to go through all the steps a charcoal grill requires.  This grill gets nice and hot fast.  Yes you do not get the same high high heat as a charcoal grill or the all the smoky flavor but for foods that to me rely more on seasoning like a great burger or things without A lot of fat like a piece of swordfish this grill is perfect.  My only wish is that there was a way to flame kiss some
Of the food.  Hot dogs can tend to taste a little more fried than grilled as the fat does not render in the same way as it does over charcoal.  Still decisions but my preference is to have a lot of char. But many guests and family like it orher wise.  I say get this grill if you want quick and easy and dependable performance.  Much simpler and less to worry about than charcoal. You will love it.  I’m just a grill snob who cooks on charcoal when he can. Lol.

title: Perfect for Rving!
text: My wife and I just got back into camping.  We bought a travel trailer and I decided not to mess with charcoal while RVing any more because it's a mess.  So I bought another popular brand of portable gas grill first because it was cheaper than a Weber.  That turned out to be a mistake because the second time I went to use it the grates were rusted!!  I've owned several Weber products in the past and currently have a Performer Kettle, so I know they're quality grills.  So I decided to bite the bullet and buy the Weber Q1200.  Initially I looked at the Q1000 because of the lower price but I liked the wing tables on the Q1200.  I also liked that I could get it in my favorite color blue.  The Q2000 is nice too but with just my wife and I it was bigger than we need and takes up more storage room.  Now after using the Q1200 twice I love it.  The heat is nice and even and the food gets a nice smoky grilled flavor.  It's doesn't get too hot and never flares up.  Cleanup couldn't be easier.  The two cast porcelain enamel grate halves pop right out and can be soaked in a dish pan or RV sink for cleaning.   The interior is easy to get to and can be wiped out with a paper towel.  And there are foil liners for the drip pan that can just be tossed. I also like the wing tables as you can just set it on a picnic table and have a place to put cooking tools, etc. without setting them on the table.  In the end I'm glad I spent the extra money and got the weber.

Ce barbecue est plus dispendieux que les concurrents, on doit donc s’attendre à une bonne performance. La chaleur atteint 460 degrés en 11 minutes, 500 en 15,5 minutes, 520 en 20 minutes et 530 en 30 minutes et cela par temps CHAUD sans VENT ce qui est insatisfaisant. 550 degrés est impossible à atteindre dans un délai raisonnable! Pourtant il est dit EXPLICITEMENT dans les spécifications que ce barbecue devrait atteindre 500 degrés en 10 minutes.  (RÉF : PAGE 43 du GUIDE)  Et dès que l’on ouvre le couvercle pour y placer notre viande, il perd rapidement sa chaleur. Je dois pratiquement mettre les contrôles au maximum en permanence… Vous me direz que j’aurais dû acheter un plus puissant, (plus de 26 000BTU)c’est vrai mais je me suis fier à la documentation de WEBER.   Malheureusement je n’ai pas la chance de « bien saisir mes superbes marques de viande » pour faire le bonheur de mes invités comme le dit votre documentation. title: Solid grill, but rust?
text: First of all, what great packing. I've been in manufacturing for 40 years and I have never seen a product better packaged/protected in my career. Assembly was fairly easy, grill is sturdy and works great. No complaints with any of this. The only thing that keeps me from giving it 5 stars is what happened to the side trays after less than a month of use. When uncovering the grill to start cooking one day, i noticed what looked like bits of barbeque sauce on the side trays. I tried cleaning them but the spots would not go away and started looking more like rust than splatter. We contacted Weber to ask about this. They confirmed our warrantee information and decided to send us replacement trays without hesitation. Great customer service. Still don't know why this happened to the stainless steel trays that were not left exposed to the elements. Overall I am very happy with this grill. Works well in all respects.

title: Weber e-210 gas grill
text: Love almost everything about this grill. The assembly process is easy to understand and it goes together with a snap. The hardware package is nicely labeled and the instructions are easy to understand.  Now the fun part.   The pre heat is fast and efficient, the temperature rises fast for that quick clean of the grates to getting ready to grill.  The propane tank storage underneath with the fuel gauge is nice too plus there’s room to store your drip pans along with other incidentals that you might have. The drip pan replacement is nice also, it has easy access when you need to change your pan out and your not fumbling around trying to do so. The reversible grates  are excellent, to go from steaks and burgers to fish, chicken and veggies was a great idea.  and having a two piece grill, you can zone out your grill with no effort what so ever. You can use indirect heat and it hold temperature perfectly so your not wasting a lot of time with adjusting the flame. Replacing the propane tank is easy, but you need a little strength for the lift of the tank on to the fuel gauge hanger, but the tank lock is nice for securing the tank safely underneath. The folding side tables are nice for ease of storage if your not using it year round.  And now the bad.  The tool hangers would be better placed in the front of the side tables instead of the side, and the browning  rack could be a little bigger. Overall it’s a great value, and along with Weber’s awesome warranty and customer service you can’t go wrong with it.

title: Gives off that lava rock flavor without having it.
text: I first used the Weber Spirit Grill at a vacation rental cabin in Idaho. Loved it from the moment I first fired it up. It wasn't until I rented the same cabin the following year that I knew I had to get one for home. I noticed right off the bat I rarely encountered a flare up and if I did it was a minimal flame that never went into a full blown engulfing of the grill. I miss the old days of the lava rock which gave the meat such a wonderful smoke flavor but the Weber Spirit Grill channels the grease in such a way that  it threw off a lot of that missed flavor into the meat. It is so easy to regulate the temperature too. Who would have thought that you could actually do a little bit of baking on a gas fired grill? And last but not least, the grill stands up well. The grill at the cabin had been in use for 5 years (I found the receipt in the kitchen drawer) and it had not one spot of rust on it. The grates were perfect. Everything worked on it. Fired right up with one click of the igniter. Needless to say within that first week of being back home and using my old grill a couple times I was missing the Weber Spirit back at the cabin. I will still return to the cabin for the peace and quiet it affords me yearly but I have my own Weber Spirit Grill sitting out on the deck now and I'm loving every minute of using it.

text:
I had no plans for a new grill this summer but a storm last month decided to wreck my three burner Spirit 1 that was only a few years old.

The old grill was great but it was really overkill for my family. This one is definitely smaller than the three burner models, but for the three of us it's got plenty of room. My advice is to think realistically about what you're going to be cooking and how much space you need. There's really no need to buy a huge grill if you're just going to toss a few  steaks, hamburgers,  or a package of brats on there. For the three of us this has plenty of room.

The grill was fairly easy for two people to assemble. The Mrs. located the necessary items and I put them together. Naturally the first two parts in the instruction book were at the very bottom of everything in the box, but oh well. It went together in an afternoon.

I've used the grill at least three times a week since then and everything's turned out great. 

One thing I need to mention is the location of the propane tank. In the old Spirit grills, Weber tucked it away behind a door under the grill. It's now in the open hanging off the side over the wheels. Visually this may not be as pleasing but is a thousand times easier. Getting the tank under the grill and lifting it into place to hang on the scale hook was always a chore for me. It required three hands but there was only room for one. With the new setup it's much easier to grab the tank by both sides and set it down on the hook. If you don't like your tank being visible, Weber does sell a cover with their logo for $10.

I definitely recommend this grill.

text:
Our old CHAR BROIL finally gave it up after many years of good service.  But, even on its best days, it wasn't of the same quality as this WEBER.

The grill holds the temperature well, it will cook our burgers, sausages, chicken, and fish to perfection without having the outside be done and the inside essentially raw; or, of course, get the inside of the meat done while absolutely having to char the outside.

This is a sturdy and well-built grill, easy to clean with the appropriate WEBER brush (use the long-handled model for ease of use), and finding the correct temperature using the control knobs has been a snap.

The only feature I do not like is having to hang the propane tank on the attached hook.  It is a difficult hoist with a full tank and a tight fit.  We instead removed the hanger and placed a square metal plate over the hole in the bottom on which we could rest the tank.  It fits well this way, doesn't move about, and is far easier to remove and replace for oldsters like us.

A great grill, we recommend it highly.

title: Florida Grilling
text: First charcoal grill in over 20 years. Learning a lot in first few weeks of use. Some great, some good, some bad. We have made some great meals. Smoked pork butt, requires lots of interaction and attention, but turned out nice. Adding coals for extended indirect cooking through grate side access not the easiest. Beer can chicken was awesome with addition of a hickory wood block to coals. Hard to beat burgers and steaks on charcoal. Timing a little more challenging than on my gas grill. Master touch series Grill has removable cutout in center of grate. When removing grate to start charcoal with Weber chimney, must set grate on a flat surface or, center cut out will fall out and first time, rolled into pool. Speaking of chimney, tried two different chimneys and Weber model clearly better. Sturdier and easier to use than cheaper model. Mild buyers remorse that I did not get Weber grill cart combo. Is it correct that you can’t order the cart as an add on accessory? All in all it has made grilling more fun and more tasty, with just a bit of additional work and slightly less convenience than gas grill. Since we grill year round in Florida it will definitely get a workout and we will no doubt learn even more.

title: Decent grill with a few design shortcomings
text:
I wanted a smaller gas grill to replace my previous grill which had been a workhorse. There are good features and features that aren't so good on this Weber. 

GOOD: I received it in good condition - no missing parts or shipping damage. It was easy for one person to assembly (some people might need a helper for a few minutes, but it really wasn't bad). The assembly directions were clear. It looks nice. So far after a few months of use, the burners ignite on the first or second push of the igniter button. It gets up to temperature very quickly.

NOT SO GOOD: There are hangers on the outside ends of the shelves for grill tools. As you can see from my pictures, you can't hang grill tools if you use the Weber grill cover designed to go with this grill. (The grill cover also doesn't hang low enough when bunched up to cover the bottom shelf, allowing rain to get into the inside - but that's a different review). Flare-ups have been fairly common. The warming rack is very narrow - I used to cook asparagus on my old grill's rack, but the spears fall off this one, or are knocked off when I close the lid. In general, I'm just having to get used to slightly different grilling techniques due to the smaller size and more direct heat than the old grill.

BAD: As many reviewers have mentioned, it is ergonomically very difficult to hang a full propane tank on the "fuel remaining" indicator. If you have any back or arm injuries, I seriously recommend you don't try. It's a great concept and seems to be pretty accurate. I will probably not hang completely full tanks on it anymore - I will wait until some of the gas is gone and the tank is lighter. And it will still be difficult.

UNKNOWN: I have not done a thorough cleaning yet so I'm not sure how easily it will clean up. I'm skeptical that the exterior "stainless" steel will look good for very long.

title: I will never purchase directly from Weber again!
text:
I would give the grill 5 stars if it weren't for the issues I encountered assembling it and the poor customer service.

This grill was ordered for me as a gift on 9/2 and delivered 9/11 and there was $40 shipping charge When the grill arrived, there was no apparent damage to the package and no scratches or markings on the parts inside indicating any damage occurred during packaging or shipping.  My mother purchased the exact same grill from Amazon in May for the same price and free two-day shipping.  I had assembled the grill for her, so I knew it was not a simple task, but it was not extremely difficult either.  She really likes her grill, which is why the same one was purchase for me.

When I began assembling the grill, I noticed that one part of the frame could not be inserted to the base as one entire side was misshapen; again there were no scratches or markings on the piece to indicate it was damaged, so there was no way for me to know there was an issue until I began the assembly.  Since there are no indications of damage, I can only conclude that parts of the grill are defective.  I called Weber and was on hold for more than 30 minutes.  When I finally got thru to a representative (who was not at all friendly), I was told I would be sent an e-mail, which I was, and to respond with a photo of the defective part.  I responded within hours of receiving the e-mail and then after 3 days of assuming the part was being replaced, I received another e-mail stating that the photo couldn’t be opened.  I immediately re-sent the photo and received the replacement part a week later.  I went back to work to assemble the grill, only to find out that the part off the frame on the opposite side was also defective.  Again, since there are no scratches or markings on the part to indicate it’s been damaged, I didn’t know that there was an issue until I began to, once again, assemble the grill.  I had had the parts of the grill laid out on a blanket on my living room floor thinking it would be an hour or two process to assemble the grill seeing as I had done it before, not weeks!  If I could have easily removed the parts of the grill from the packaging without having to destroy the box, I would have sent the entire grill back and never purchased a Weber grill again.   I cannot express how disappointing and frustrating this has been.

title: This grill is BOSS for 2-4 people!
text:
First off, I grill meats only - no veggie experience.  Ribs, chicken and steak.  For ribs and chicken, I use a grill mat cut just a bit smaller than the grill surface - works great with this grill.  Really minimized flareups!  Steaks go right on grill; I usually do sirloins with lower fat content. This grill holds temperature really well.  On my covered patio I can grill even on cooler days (45F min).  For four or less people, this grill holds plenty of food.  Grill would probably bog down big-time if you overload the cooking surface. It does not have an upper warming/holding rack.  Only two burners, but they are adequate for the grill surface, and probably more economical on LP than three burners (if all on).
I've had this grill for 3-4 years, and only thing I've replaced (just recently) is the enamel flavorizer bars.  Got a set on Amazon for $20, fit perfectly.  Got a spare tank at Costco, so always have gas on hand.  Grill itself cleans easily with the removable drip tray.  Burners and grill box itself require minimal cleaning/upkeep.  I do keep the grill covered when not in use - rust and flareups are a grill's biggest enemies.  One big plus is the fold-down side trays; these really minimize the footprint for patio storage.  Summary - best grill I've owned.

The fold-down side shelves are a real plus for storage and should be standard on all Weber models, especially the three-burner version of the Spirit gas grill.  I opted instead for the two-burner grill because of the fold-down shelves.  This grill is well-built of sturdy materials and the caster style wheels make it easy to move about.  The only flaw I can point to is a design flaw involving the positioning of the LP gas bottle inside the enclosed compartment beneath the grill.  Installing the bottle onto the hook for the weight-based gauge is extremely difficult due to the weight of the full bottle (40 lbs) and the very tight space inside the cabinet.  There is almost no room to obtain leverage to lift the heavy bottle onto the hook.  This is a three-handed operation and there is no helpful guide in the owner's manual for dealing with this difficult installation.  I managed it in the end by placing a thin piece of plywood over the hole in the compartment floor as I maneuvered the bottle into place on the hook and then sliding the plywood piece out from under the bottle so that it would hang properly on the hook.  Not an easy installation!  Weber engineers, you need to fix this flaw!  Apart from that, I fully endorse this grill and expect to get years of good use out of it.

text:
Yes, at first glance, the Weber Grills are expensive.  And worth the cost.  The cooking control and flame control is just superb.  It is a convection oven when the lid is closed so cooking is very quick.

Even more importance for me as the durability of the Weber Grill.  Yes, I have purchased much cheaper LPG grills and their life time was very short, most often just 3 to 4 years as replacement parts, even from "name" manufactures, are just not available.  Those friends and neighbors that have Weber Grills have their grills remained usable for more than a decade; and, when spare spare are needed, Weber has them and they are in stock.  So cost of ownership is a winner.

The grease and sauce drainage system is the best I have looked at.  Easy to inspect, keep clean and replace the trap.

Temperature control is simple -- just keep track of the temperature gauge.

I put mine together myself.   Very clear instructions that uses a picture only instruction book plus a video that can take you thru each step.  The instruction booklet was so detailed that it was all I needed.  Took me 3 hours and I worked alone [which is not the Weber suggestion].

I am a proud new owner and I expect to be a proud "experienced" owner a decade from now after enjoying many fire-cooked meals.

title: Best grill we have ever owned
text: The Weber Spirit E-210 gas grill is the best grill we have owned.  I spent months online and in stores checking out the pros and cons of literally dozens of grills.  The grill that the Weber replaced lasted a reasonable time and functioned alright but was not made near as well as the Weber.  We have used the Weber several times and we are very pleased with everything about the grill.  We downsized from a 4-burner with a side burner in order to step up in quality.  The Weber side tables fold down and are sturdy.  The grill area is large enough for our family get-togethers.  The thermometer is accurate.  The electronic ignition helps start the flame on the first push.  The grill heats to 600 degrees in less than 15 minutes.  The grease pan access is open and easy to get to.  The propane tank is completely hidden in a sturdy cabinet and is far enough below the grill that I no longer burn my hands turning it off.  The built in propane gas gauge is a great idea and takes the guesswork out of knowing when to swap out tanks.  The handle does not get hot at all and is easy to lift and close.  The grill is easy to move, a nice feature we did not have with our previous grill because it was so unwieldy and heavy. Everything seems to have been well thought out and engineered to last.  The steel is far superior to other grills, even those costing more.  At this price point the quality, durability, and ease of use make the Weber a top choice.

EZ start, Even cooking, EZ cleanup.  The tank hanger/fuel level gauge is a nice feature no other grill has. The attention to detail extends to the vinyl washers used to prevent electro mechanical corrosion that occurs between different metals.  During my days assembling grills many people asked me what grill they should buy, my reply was always " if you want a grill that's well constructed and one that will last, buy a Weber".

text: Fabulous little grill!  The flavors coming off of this barbecue can't be beat by any other grill in my humble opinion.  Whenever I have time to grill using the old-fashioned coal method of grilling, I thoroughly enjoy myself.  I own both a Weber Gas grill and this guy here.  I use the gas grill for convenience and my kettle grill for a lazy Sunday afternoon on a Fall day, or sometimes even in the rain. I've owned two of these over the years, I much prefer this type that has a way to catch the ashes  as they fall, it makes for a very convenient cleanup/ash dump after they've cooled.  The pan style allows the wind to catch hot ash as it falls and blow it into your face as you make adjustments to the air intake on the bottom of this grill, this one won't do that.  The one negative to this model, is that there are times when you'd like to completely remove your lid, you can certainly hang it from the kettle, most of the time, but sometimes you just want it out of the way.  Make sure that you have a good place to set it that won't burn (not a wooden deck).  This grill is hot!  Always think about safety when there are little ones around.  I use a chimney to start the charcoal (lump charcoal is awesome!), but then don't forget to set that chimney on a non-burnable surface and hose it off to cool it down so that you don't walk into it and burn yourself on your legs.  I use a slotted wooden spoon to turn the top air intake and keep a barbecue cart close by to hold all my food and tools.  Don't let it's good price fool you (I paid in the ballpark of $150), it really does create wonderful flavors!  It was easy, actually really easy, to put together.  I gave my old one from 20 years ago (the one with the ash pan) to a friend, he still loves it.  I upgraded to the ash catch bowl model.

text:
We are generally pleased with our new Weber grill. 

Replacing the tank is one royal pain in the back. Because it must be hung on the tank bracket inside the cabinet, it requires two people to lift it onto the bracket. One where the cabinet opens and another reaching through from the back. This is the only way to be able to roll the unit around. If you don't hang it, then it rests on the ground inside the cabinet due to the hole that accommodates the tank. Another model allows the tank to be hung on the outside, but we don't like that option.

If the grill will be outside on a deck or lanai, we recommend getting the optional cover. Rain, etc. will leave water stains on the chrome side tables, the lid and the control panel. Mild liquid soap and warm water (as recommended) removes most of it. Perhaps a stainless steel cleaner will remove what is left.

Allow extra time to preheat the grill and for cooking. It seems to take a lot longer than the Ducane we replaced with the Weber. In fairness, the Ducane had four burners. (Ducane is now owned by Weber.)

title: Still the best small bbq around
text: We purchased an earlier version of this grill several years ago, and loved it. It is not cheap, but held up very well despite nearly daily useage. (Love that California Living!)  Because it is a Weber, it is possible to find replacement parts, and we did have to replace the flavor bars and some other items over the years. When we moved recently, we decided we did not have the space to pack/ship the BBQ and promised ourselves we would buy another once we were settled.  And, we did. First, we are extremely happy with the grill.  It is a perfect size for a small family, heats up fast, and cooks reliably.  The starter system has been upgraded since our original model, now with a battery and works even on cold/wet days (original was a striker type, and sometimes if it was really wet outside, it would require a lighter to start).  The grates are high quality cast iron, and has both a wide side and a narrow (we always use the wide side up) so if you are grilling say, asparagus, that helps.  It has a built in propane gas level gage as well, and the mounting system for the tank has also improved and is easier to get the tank mounted inside the base of the BBQ. The other improvement is a switch from a "cosmetic panel" in front to an actual door. Again, much easier to access the area under the grill with a nice hinged door.  Where the grill lost ground over the earlier model is that the original one came with a cast iron griddle that fit into the grate system.  I normally did not bother removing the grate to mount the cast iron pan into the grates, but used the round pan/griddle extensively (I saved the one I had and can now use on the new grill). This was perfect for grilling things like lamb chops and getting an amazing sear, and was my favorite way to cook a spatchcocked chicken.  The pan was a really nice perk, but the problem now with the grill grates is that there are little nubbie protrusions on the grates to keep them separated and spaced, but it leaves too wide a gap between the two grates. Kind of have to cook on one side or the other, or cook something pretty big so it doesn't go through the gap. I could dock my rating by one star for that, but I haven't seen any better grills out there, so can't really penalize the product for a past rendition being better.

title: Sturdy grill with great assembly instructions
text:
I splurged and bought this for myself because I've always wanted to own a Weber grill. So far, I have not been disappointed. 

Assembly was pretty easy...the instructions are probably the best I've ever seen for any sort of large appliance like this. There were a couple images in them that were wrong, but it was easy to figure out what they meant, so it didn't create a problem. My box was missing one of the screws that I needed, but Weber sent that to me pretty quickly.

The grill is very sturdy, and I expect it will last a long time. It reaches about 550 F within 10 minutes or so of turning it on.

In terms of grilling, I'm still learning about the hotspots and what temperature setting to use for various things. My main problem has been that even though I get the grill really hot and oil the grates before putting something on it, food seems to stick pretty easily. So far, I've made salmon, chicken and Cornish game hens with it, and they turned out pretty well, though it seemed as though I needed to cook things longer than I would've thought, so I guess I need to turn it up a bit higher than I would expect. 

The gas tank guage is probably one of the best features...it's nice not to have to worry about whether you have enough gas.

title: Very pleased
text: So, we bought this grill for camping trips in our little 19’ camper. We also purchased the portable cart to go with it. We just used it five out of six nights  on a camping trip last week. First, grill performance is standard top notch Weber. Best grilling at the campsite ever for us—filet mignon, seared tuna steaks, pork chops, NY strips, and shrimp tacos. Everything turned out wonderfully. Very steady temperature hold. It is a small grill so you can’t open the lid for very long without losing substantial heat so plan your cooking accordingly. The grill grates are conveniently the perfect size to soak in a standard small camper sink—I don’t know if this was intended, but it’s a wonderful feature that makes cleanup easy. The cart works well as a stand but leaving the grill attached to it for storage is very unwieldy. I recommend separating them for transport. Also, don’t forget to remove the propane bottle for transport. The on/off dial doesn’t lock in the off position so a rough road will turn on the dial and run out your propane. Also, the folding side shelves are a nice feature but I forgot twice to fold them out before lighting the grill. Both times I flipped them out before causing any damage but I have to imagine one day my absent-mindedness might result in two melted shelves. I need to fashion a warning sign for myself. Anyway, so far I love this little grill. The best part is that there is definitely a difference in how tasty the food is on a Weber grill. The styling is a nice bonus—it’s a cool looking little grill.

title: Great little grill that is not too little!!!
text: Great little grill that is not too little!!!  Unfortunately, I did have to call Weber as my new grill had a defective regulator as verified by Weber Tech when I called at 8PM the night I put it together.  The lady tech had me to test to verify the problem and promptly stated they would be sending me a new regulator pronto.  It came 3 days later, I installed same day and was grilling 7 large pork chops for company dinner that night.  The  grill will cook a large amount for a so called small grill.  It has a great heavy duty cast iron grill.  The grill should always be preheated to around 400 degrees.  I did purchase the 1/2 cast iron griddle separately as the grill is in two pieces.  Do not put two griddles in you may overheat grill.  Remove 1/2 and replace with the griddle and start griddling after you season the griddle in the oven with canola oil wipe down after each heating.  Then will be the time for bacon, eggs, hash browns, pancakes and anything else you may choose to griddle.  In the case of my grill, if yours does not heat up to 400 degrees in about 15 minutes, (maybe less) call the Weber tech and they can get you going, and in my case a new regulator was the answer.  From my reading, a faulty new regulator is not uncommon on any brand of grill.  The Weber service is good and evidently 24 hours.  Bought for RV grill, but will be using far more than that.

title: Well built.  Easy Assembly.  Great results!
text:
Bought the Spirit II E-310 to replace my 14 (or so) year old Weber Performer charcoal grill and after the first couple of grills, am left wondering why I hadn't made the switch years ago.  Loved my Performer (although it kinda morphed into a bit of a love-hate relationship when its gas charcoal lighting system  stopped working a couple years ago), but am certainly happy with my purchase decision.  The grill is solid, well designed, and above all else--works well!  Switching from charcoal to gas, I knew I would be giving up some of that smoky flavor, but now that my grates are starting to get a good season on them, the results have been awesome.

Quick note on assembly....as I unpacked the grill (and its many parts) from the box, I was thinking that I would be in for a pretty unpleasant experience, but the BILT app that you can download for step by step 3-D instructions made it a pretty stress free assembly.  Being able to zoom in on parts, joints, fasteners, etc, made assembly pretty simple.  Still took me an hour and a half or two (was taking my time not to over torque any fasteners or scratch any finishes), but everything came together easily and worked great from the start.

Overall, very happy with purchase and would definitely recommend!

I've had two of these now over the past decade and I do really like them. There are some significant design issues though. Most people complain that the grills don't get hot enough. The way they overcome this is by not putting vents on the lid and telling you to grill with the lid closed. This causes a different problem though. With no way to vent the heat, it is impossible to maintain a temperature below 475 degrees, way too hot for most grilling needs. So you either have to chose between it not getting hot enough with the lid open, or way too hot with the lid closed. They sent me a new regulator,  but that hasn't changed anything. 

The instructions say that it is normal to run too hot on first few usages, so they clearly know this is a problem and don't want you returning it. I think they presume that by writing that on there, they know you will keep it for a while in the hopes that it improves and then just never get around to returning it. A simple vent on the top of the lid that can be adjusted just like nearly every other grill sold has would solve this problem. So why haven't they added this yet? With that one little vent, this would be the perfect grill. 

The second design issue is the handle on the right side. You need two good handles for a heavy grill like, this but you can't actually use the handle on the right because the regulator is in the way. They've had these grills out for a while, no reason to not fix this by now. The third design issue I am a bit mixed on. The coated grills are nice in many ways and more durable than the cheap wire grills. But food sticks to it like crazy so it involves quite a bit of cleanup after each usage. 

So why am I still giving this four stars? I gave my last one to a friend who helped me move. I missed it for a couple of years and decided to spend 200 on this versus 40 for a cheaper portable grill. I just like the rugged look and feel to it. My last one was used at least weekly and stored on the back porch of a Colorado cabin. This is back home in Texas now, and I've got it installed outside on a homemade stand. For a single guy, this is a perfect size. It will grill for two quite easily while taking up a minimal space. I like that I can take it off the stand and toss it in the truck with a couple of one-pound bottles for visits with friends or hunting trips. I also like that I can plug it in with a basic 20 pound bottle on my home stand for daily use. But if I suddenly run out of propane, I could finish grilling with my camping bottles before I go and get a refill on the big bottle. 

Ultimately, I just like the thing. But I really, really wish they would fix these design faults. They would be so easy to fix and they've had plenty of time to do so. I'm tempted to find someone local who can just aftermarket install a top vent. That would make a huge difference.

title: Five-Year Reflections
text:
A lot of people get so excited about this grill that that they *have* to write about it after just a few days' use. This covers a somewhat longer timeline than that.

My experience with Weber grills practically goes back to childhood, but nearly all those were charcoal grills. When me and my wife finally over into a decent-sized house, one of the things on my mind was grilling, but I was all about cooking with gas, for a number of reasons, and the only name on my radar was Weber. The E-210 was the perfect size - neither too-much or too-little grill. As soon as we got it, and placed it on the back deck of the house, I went to town like never before, and the grill has consistently delivered the goods, year-round. (Appreciated the recent piece about winter grilling…I feel a little less like a weirdo now.) Have read some of the criticisms of the grill here, and have a few observations:

- I regard the Flavorizer bars as something of a semi-consumable: since I use the grill on the average of 3-4 days a week, I've clocked a *lot* of hors on the thing, and I'm frankly amazed the bars lasted as long as they did (four years). Just replaced them this past summer.

- Igniter: I can only speak for myself, but I have yet to replace even the battery on the original igniter…and this on a grill that stays outside year-round (and doesn't always get its cover put on as it should; my bad.)

In all, I can't imagine being without this grill. Everything I've always known tastes better when grilled is now absolutely scrumptious. Wife doesn't make fun of me when I go grilling in snow, because she knows she getting good eats as well. I'm sure there are other decent grills around, but I go with what I know here. Heartily recommended.

title: Good Grill, Poor Fuel Gage System.
text: On the upside, it is a quality grill, looks good, lights easily every time and allows very good control over the amount of heat it produces. On the down side, I totally dislike the fuel gage and LP tank mount. First, the mounting system doesn't allow for the curled metal most LP tanks have at the top to act as a handle. If  you rotate the tank to accommodate the mount, the regulator hose assembly is just barely long enough to attach to the gas tank. Second, the fuel gage system is nothing more than a spring system which to me makes the accuracy suspect and is likely to weaken over time. The short regulator hose prevents the addition of an in line pressure gage. My third (and final gripe about the fuel system is that the cutout underneath where the fuel tank sets is so big that the fuel tank drops all the way through to the ground if it is not hung on the fuel gage hook. Were it not for these three things, I would have given a five star review instead of three.

title: Underwhelmed
text:
When time to replace our beloved 28 year old (!!) Weber genesis, obvious choice: another Weber. But things have changed. 
Yes, went from a Genesis to Spirit solely on price/affordability. 
First, the burners now run left, middle, right, not front, middle, back. This changes the cooking game tremendously; from whole chicken roasting, to pizza on the grill. Both almost annoyingly impossible. 
Second, the entire metal cabinet is unnecessary. Replacing a full, heavy, awkward tank is very difficult to lift into the cabinet and hook into the hanger. The gas gauge is cool though.   
There is no longer a slide out bottom clean out tray...please bring that back!
Gone is a front foldable shelf that was ideal when cooking for a crowd. Weber designers reduced the profile of hooks to hang spatulas etc soo low, that a pair of tongs won’t remain in place without falling... and they are on the side, not the front of the shelf? Thankfully they moved knobs off the side shelf to the front, gaining real estate there is a score. 
Lastly, there is no longer a hole in the front of the grill to light it old school if *battery* ignition fails. Whyyy?
All in all, its a box that cooks food on my deck, that’s how disenfranchised we are. .. more than a bit of a let down after the long love affair we had with our old one.

Sometimes it does not go back past 400 degrees or it takes a long time to get there.  #2-  It is very easy to accidentially turn on the gas and leak propane when grabbing the carry handles. The right side handle is a little hard to grip due to other parts crowding it. That being said, it is a really good grill, it cooks superbly, and I would recommend it. The grill works with the small Coleman propane canister and lasted about 4-meals including pre-heating. These points are only brought up to let you be aware of them. When we bought the grill it did not come with a cover (which is new, our first weber grill came with one). However, when its very windy out (common where we live), I am always checking to see if the cover is still around - it has not blown off yet, but its come very very close. title: Worth the Price
text:
I shopped around a, lot comparing features and prices, before buying mine " in the box" at Home Depot (they had them fully assembled but I wanted one without smudges and handprints all over it- also easier to transport home in my pickup).

Assembly instructions were as clear and accurate as can be, plus they have a cool 3-D app (which I didn't need to use. All parts were included and parts for various steps were bagged separately ( keep them that way). All the bolt holes lind up perfectly and nuts were often already welded in place to simplify things.Of course, all materials were of a very high caliber. When all done, it was beautiful.

I am following Weber's recipes and instructions to a tee and they work. My propane E-310 Spirit II ignites immediately and the burner controls are very accurate. The tank scale gauge is much better than the pressure gauges I've used in the past, which were pretty useless.
I bought an iGrill 3 wireless wifi thermometer to attach to the unit (very scarce in stores) but I tested it first by pairing the transmitter (with probe inserted in it) with my Samsung a10e phone (with Weber app) then I left phone at bbq and walked around to test range. Unfortunately, they would lose pairing consistently- evidenced by red pairing light on transmitter going out and transmitter turning off- when I entered the kitchen door a mere 15' away, rendering it unuseable inside my frame/stucco house. I returned it and bought another brand with separate transmitter and receiver (not wifi) with a huge range.

So far, I have cooked burgers ( my wife says "best ever"), lamb chops and tritip roast and uncooked Italian sausage- all to perfection.
I find you can Google Weber recipes for almost anything and they work.
I love it!

title: Good looking and good working grill!
text:
This is actually our first gas grill and we're very happy with it. It is solidly built and we expect it to last for years. We've only had it for a little over a month, but have used it several times and it has worked well each time. 
I could have bought one pre-assembled, but I wanted to put it together myself not only to know how it was put together but also to know it was done right. I used a combination of the written instructions and the "Bilt" video and had not problems. I like the new "Bilt" videos as you can rotate the images in any direction to see what it should look like when done.
I also bought some accessories to go with it, including Weber's cover, rotisserie and light. The cover fits well with Velcro in several places to help keep it from blowing away when it is windy and the light is pretty cool in that it comes on when you lift the cover but can also be removed to use independently. I do have to say it is certainly on the pricey side. Haven't tried the rotisserie yet but plan to soon.
Back to the grill....
The wing tables are nice to have and include three hooks on each side for hanging tools. The stainless steel, however, does scratch easily but it's not really a problem.
I like the hanging tank gauge that quickly shows the amount of propane that is left. It's easy to see what the level is and easy to attach the tank.
The starter works quickly too. Turn on the gas, and as soon as the start button is pushed the fire is lit. Don't know how long the battery will last yet.
We've had Weber grills (charcoal) for several years now and they still work fine. I've used a Smokey Joe for camping and we still have our full sized kettle grill that has plenty of miles on it. This is partly why we chose another Weber.
While I can't testify to the longevity of this grill, I can say that we're happy with it so far.
