title: Stop shopping around and buy this grill!
text:
If you’re like me, I read reviews, watch review videos...a lot of them, whenever I’m making a big ticket purchase. After all, I’m trying to find a grill that will last me many grilling seasons, with a great warranty to back it up. 

So, my review adventure began and I shopped the local “blue” store and the local “orange” store. I saw the many levels of brands on display, both much more and slightly less expensive than this grill. I saw the dents, the dings, the rusted grills, the ones waaaay out of my price range...then, I saw this Weber. It was basic, but nice. It was aluminum, not steel. It was mid-priced, but not too expensive or too cheap.

Now, I’m in my late 40’s and I’ve been using charcoal for well over 30 years. I stepped outside of my comfort zone for a change and this Weber seemed to fit the bill. All the reviews spoke about good heat retention, long lasting, great warranty, quick heating (even for only being 3 burners) and no huge gaping slit on the back where the lid closes (see good heat retention). I mentioned the “basic” look, but I like it. Large wheels to help clear obstacles when moving it, unlike casters that get stuck on a piece of gravel. I like the open front since all the doors would hide is the propane tank and spider webs. The fold down tray is great for the small area in my garage for storage. Basic, but practical. 

So, a stop by the local big box “blue” store and I picked up my grill, a propane tank and home I went. I noted that unlike many competitors reviews, the Weber box was intact, not damaged and that relayed over to the interior as well. Not a single mark on my new grill, let alone huge dents and dings like so many reviews about other grills. 

After setup (which took at about an hour), I had the tank attached and ready to go.  I will also note that Weber has the build down to a science. The wires for the grill igniter don’t need additional cable ties as they are the perfect length and sit in a series of clips. There were no missing screws or profanity used during my entire build.  

I’ve only used the grill twice since my purchase, just three days ago, but both times I can attest to the quick heating and amazing heat retention of the unit. The grill lights immediately and reliably. The heat is even across the entire grilling area. The size is just right for my family of four and I see this lasting me a long long time. 

So, stop looking around and pick this unit up. It’s so versatile and well built, you’ll be glad you did.

title: Great for a family of 4+
text:
As an adult with a family of four, this is our first “real” grill that was more of an investment than a quick summer grilling solution. Great grill! Easy to assemble, like everything that one needs to assemble at home, use the correct screw driver head and use common sense when aligning and tightening it all down and it should go smoothly. I assembled this grill myself (33yr/M) in my living room while everyone was sleeping. When built, it’s quite sturdy. Or first meal on it was 3 1” NY strips and 1.25” porterhouse. We like well done beef in our household (sue me) and this grill performed flawlessly. Adequate and accurate even heating across the grilling grates that produced excellent hash marks. It holds heat well too. 16 minutes later we had steakhouse quality cuts grilled to perfection for 1/5 of the cost of going out. 

Worth every penny. The 3 burner model is a good size for a family of four plus a few guests. If you have lesser grilling needs, the 2 burner model would be a real nice consideration. Especially if it’s just one or two people with the occasional guest.

The Spirit line is indeed a basic grill. Side table and 2/3 burners. That’s it. But it’s such a nice grill. More “affordable” brands offer all the bells and whistles that much more expensive Weber’s offer but what you get is a season or two and things start to go out and you have to replace it. You may get less features with the Spirit’s, but what you get is quality. I look forward to using my Weber for years to come.

This grill is replacing a Weber Genesis Silver A that I have had for 20 years (outside). After such a great experience, a new Weber was the only way to go. The Spirit II....I love the well built base, the electronic igniter (has worked every time so far). Most of all, this grill holds a set temperature very well. I have done ribs on it already, and they came out great using indirect heat. The stainless side tables, front panel are nice touches, though they will need frequent cleaning.

The only thing to consider is size. I think it could cook for up to 8 with no problem, but for $100 more the E-310 gives you another burner and a slightly bigger cooking area. I don't need this, but it is worth consideration.

The only downside is that Weber used to offer the Spirit II series in 4 colors. I really wanted sapphire, but now you can only get black (mine) or stainless steel. 

I think that this is a great grill and am really happy to see that the E-210 matches or exceeds my old Silver A in so many ways.

title: Use a generic 'adaptor' hose for 20lb tank
text:
Great grill for my balcony! Perfect size for a single, couple or small family. Heats up quickly and easy to clean. I love it! 

Keep in mind the fuel connection is meant for small disposable propane tanks (it is a portable BBQ after all.) You can use a generic 'adaptor hose' from any hardware store if you want to use this BBQ with a 20lb tank. Just make sure it's got the 'adaptor' to convert from portable to the large tank. I got mine for $26.99CDN at Home Hardware. It doesn't have to be Weber's hose, since their hose seems to be getting really bad reviews because of the white ring breaking. 

BTW, Weber it really doesn't matter that you have a 2 year warranty on a faulty product. Perhaps it time to consider replacing your overpriced adaptor hose with one that doesn't break.

title: Wrong Wheel Frame
text:
On April 19, 2021, a Weber Spirit II gas grill was ordered.  It arrived on April 25th.  Assembly began immediately and it was soon discovered that the wheel frame (see photo) to which the wheels were to be attached was incorrect.  One of the bent “legs” could not be inserted therein.  A call was placed to Weber where I was informed that a replacement part would be sent to me.  It arrived four days later and assembly began again.  The part received worked fine.  However, two  tabs on one other of the smaller items were bent.  Fortunately, with a pair of pliers,  I was able to return it to its proper position and complete the assembly.  

To comment further, the Weber person with whom I was relating the problem to was very friendly and helpful.  Also, in that there was an enormous amount of tape (top, bottom, and sides) I wonder if perhaps  the grill  had been returned by someone because of the wrong part, and that it was re-shipped to me.  

The grill has been used one time.  It works fine, and I am satisfied with the results obtained.

title: Classic Weber charcoal grill with great updates
text:
I love my Weber charcoal grills, I had my last classic black 22" charcoal grill for 15+ years before relocating which was still great just replacing the grilling grates when needed. Used it year round in the NY area in sun, rain, snow, sleet weather. I would catch my neighbors peeking out their windows when I would grill particularly in the winter when the rough cold and snow would keep them inside but yes, I would be grilling!
So after moving I retired the ol' faithful "Man-a-Q" and decided it was time for a new one. Super happy when I came across the Master-Touch 22" in Ocean Blue by chance and picked it up. (the color sold me on the spot, more of a brighter blue and not dark blue) It is packaged with some nice accessories like the 2 charcoal basket holders for indirect cooking & the warming rack that circles half the outer circumference of the grill. Not to mention a new lid holder design that is superior to the old hanger on my previous Weber. Very nice options! Overall a true Weber classic charcoal grill with some modern great updates.
So why not 5 stars? I used my new Weber the day I brought it home (of course) to cook up some dinner. I went out after to clean everything up to notice a roughly 3" circle piece of the paint missing from the lid! (I made sure to inspect the grill previous since it came preassembled) Super disappointing since it sticks out like a sore thumb with the blue color, I take care of my grill so the only thing it could be is some kind of defect in the paint / color. Contacted Weber support the next day via website chat (provided pics, ect) and the Weber support agent was quick to back their product and put a order in for a new replacement lid on the spot! Only downside is its on backorder since the new color is in high demand but its only a aesthetic issue that irks me looking at it.

I've only owned charcoal grills and after a few different brands Weber has been the brand in my back yard or where ever I go. Some like propane which is a "instant-on" convenient grill but I find it the same as cooking in the oven, pellet is awesome but in inclement weather like rain you would not catch me plugging a grill in to an outlet. Weber Charcoal grills have always been the ol' reliable for year round grillin and look forward to using my new Weber for years!

This grill was easy to assemble and easy to use.  I like the holding system that doubles as a gauge for measuring the level of propane left in the tank.  A big plus is the even heating of the entire cooking surface and limited flare ups.
The only thing that is preventing me from giving 5 stars is the inability to set a low temperature setting; even with the dials turned all the way down, temp stays above 300 degrees.

title: Best and most capable grill under $500!
text: From a quick hot dog and burger grill, al the way to long slow smoking sessions of 2+ hours per pound of meat at 225*, this economical wonder never fails. The "new" side grate accesses allow for addition of new charcoal and wood chips to enhance the smoking experience. Couple this grill with a high quality remote digital multi-probe set, and you have all the keys to making the very best BBQ no matter the cost. For example, we recently cooked a 5 pound buffalo brisket that fell apart after being smoked for 8 hours. Shared the meat with friends, and none of them could stop remarking about the meat being flavorful, exact doneness, and delicious.  This is our third Weber in the past 30 years, and by far the best!

Everything has turned out great -- the new ignition is incredible plus it this grill just cooks things properly.  You can't bet on that with other brands.
I'm very satisfied with this grill.  The only way I would change my mind is if it didn't last -- but I don't expect that!
The grill we just gave away was bought in 1997 and it was still working, just needed some attention and it took up a lot more space.

text:
It's mostly great, and I'm proud of it.  However, it's very top heavy, and I'm afraid of it falling over every time I try to move it, which makes me drag the leg a lot.  The wheel and handle set up doesn't help with stairs.  I have a deck I store the grill on, and I have to lift the whole grill every time I want to use it, and put it away, which isn't easy on my back, and I've recently developed hip problems.  For example, I have a toter for recycling, and the handle is on the same side as the wheels.  It's much easier to learn it towards me, and roll it around, and with stairs I can pull it, and roll it over the steps, or ease it down without having to carry the full weight.  The toter is easier on 2 flights of stairs than the grill is for a few steps.

It just seems like a few design oversights, and perhaps slight adjustments could make handling, and moving the grill much easier and safer.

Also, perhaps it's user error, but even with all the vents fully open, it seems like the charcoal doesn't burn hot enough with the lid closed.  I keep clearing out as much ashe as I can, but when I put the lid on, after a little bit, it's almost out, like it's suffocating.  Maybe I need to clean the grill or something, cause the first time this wasn't an issue at all, I was amazed by how hot it got.  Like I said, maybe that's on me, and not the grills fault, cause I only use the cleaning system, and haven't done a thorough cleaning yet.

text:
I bought this grill about a year ago and have not been happy with it from day one.  I have owned Weber Kettle grills approximately 40 years.  (My entire adult life). I bought this one not because I needed it, my old standard grill that I have had for over 15 years still works fine but I just wanted to spoil myself with the additional accessories and the thermometer.  I have never had a grill with a thermometer before.  Always have had just the standard, basic 22”kettle.  Anyway, from the first time I used it I noticed the lid fits loose and just sits on the rim of the base.  There is no type of air tight seal at all.  Once the coals are hot the only way to turn down the heat is completely close both the top and bottom vents and even then it won’t go below approximately 375 degrees.  With both vents closed the coals should go out.  The lid is not damaged or “out of round” it just doesn’t fit right, it is almost like it’s about 1/2 inch too big, leaving a gap for air to come in.
  I used it again this past Memorial Day weekend to celebrate with family and friends and cooked a full rack of babyback ribs.  I have learned over the past year the only way I can manage to get the temperature low enough to cook “low and slow” is I have to completely close both vents and balance a cinder block on top of the lid to get it to fit tighter.
  So, after this past weekend I have had enough and decided to say something.  If you decide to buy one you better pick up a cinder block while you’re at it.

title: Should of bought one years ago.
text: Switched to a Weber Kettle after having many issues with my old propane grill and I should of made this switch a while ago. Not only is charcoal a much simpler grilling method, but the things that a Weber kettle can do out number a propane grill vastly. In the weeks of having my Kettle I have smoked tasty ribs, pulled pork, beer can chicken, and countless other tasty BBQ meals. Many of the above would have been hard on the propane grill mainly the smoked meats. Also with the Kettles sturdy construction and simple operation I don’t have to worry about parts breaking like on a propane grill. And lastly charcoal grilling may not be as quick as propane, but the charcoal taste makes up for it. If you are looking for a grill that does it all and you don’t want to pay the $$$ of a pellet grill I would 100% recommend getting a Weber Kettle. My only complaint of the grill would be the top air vent should have a handle to assist with opening it while hot, but this is nothing a BBQ glove can’t fix. There is also a large market and community revolving around kettle grills so you won’t be hard pressed to find grill modifications and how to videos. 3 additional components that I would recommend to get with your grill would be: a charcoal chimney for starting your charcoal, heavy duty metal tongs for shifting coals, and the Weber Charcoal baskets for better grilling by indirect heat. Even with these add one you are still south $100s of dollars of a pellet grill. 10/10 would recommend.

title: Weber Spirit E-310 Gas Grill
text:
This grill was a replacement for about a 10 year Spirit that we previously had and which had the burner tubes pararallel to the front of the grill.  This new Spirit has the burners perpendicular to the front which make it harder to cook with just one burner lit, harder to use the warming rack in the back and harder to use the rotissierrie.  When you lit just one burner with the "old" Spirit configuration all the heat was right in front of you  and there was no direct heat under the warming rack.  Now if you light one burner there is always direct heat under the warming rack so it is hard to use the whole thing.  Same thing with the rotissierre, which is centered on the grill.  With the old configuration I could light all three burners and then after the meat is seared turn off the center burner or the center and the rear and have only indirect heat on meat.  Now with only one burner on, there will always be a portion of the meat with direct heat and the other end will be less done.  Going to be VERY hard to achieve a consistent doneness on anything on the rotissierrie.

I grill 3-4 times per week and all in all this grill is a major disappointment.  By reorienting the burners you eliminate the flexibility of using indirect heat in more flexible ways.  This grill is poorly engineered, poorly executed and doesn't come close the finesse you can achieve with the old Spirit. The propane tank is difficult to hand inside the cabinet and you have to be on your hands and knees.  Its almost like they didn't really cook on this grill when it was tested.  You would have noticed at least a few of these issues.  Weber can feel free to contact me about these issues.

text:
It seems like a good enough product with one major drawback that I have not previously seen mentioned. Yes, the knobs are cheap plastic, but I am gentle with them and hope that when they break they are easily replaceable. The meter for the propane I have yet to weigh in on, but although it suggests the tank has been empty for about 3 weeks, I keep grilling and there is still propane, but its accuracy is called into question.
My worst surprise is the orientation of the lid. When you raise the lid as far as you are able to access the food (turn it, etc), the smoke that is released from under the hood is directed right into your face if you are standing, as I always have in the past and believe is natural, in front of the grill. Something about the shape of the lid and the degree you are able to open it causes this quite significant problem. Smoke into the eyes not a comfortable situation!
I am now trying to train myself always to be standing to the side of the grill when I open the lid to keep the smoke from searing my eyeballs. 
I'm wondering if anyone else has had this issue, and I am surprised it was not mentioned in any reviews I read.

title: Amazing value for a family grill
text:
Purchased 3 months ago and used it AT LEAST weekly since. The Spirit II makes grilling easy and fun, coming from someone who used to own a cheaply made 2-burner years ago, but has used other Webers in the past.

Assembly was not terribly complicated. I watched a video beforehand, and it was about an hour-long job for two people. It fired up perfectly right away, and we've had no problems since.

You probably won't find a better value in a grill. All components are made to last, and the warranty will back that up. I frequently cook for 3-4 people, and even made enough chicken to feed a group of 12 effortlessly. Caveat: If you plan on making 10 ribeyes at a time, this probably isn't the grill for you. It is, however, going to be great for the average user.

I knocked it one star for a very small amount of uneven heating, but I've seen much much worse. You also have to factor in the weather at the time of grilling, and acknowledge that fire is unpredictable. Again, it's only a one star knock because of the MSRP. If it were a $ 5k grill, I would expect perfectly equal heating all around haha.

Finally, the ability to make this grill your own is a huge plus. The Weber cover and utensils complement it well, but I would highly recommend downloading the Weber app. It seriously changed how I grill. Also, the iGrill 3 is a good investment if you frequently cook larger pieces of meat, especially on lower heat. 

All in all, I could only not recommend this grill to someone who plans on usually grilling for a large family of more than maybe 8 people, or someone who wants a grill that looks flashier. My honest opinion is don't pay more to keep up with the Joneses. Just buy this grill and get to cooking.

title: A very convenient and efficient grill
text:
This is the first grill I ever owned. I only cook for myself and for one or two visitors. The size is perfect for me. I originally wanted the two burner model but Home Depot accidently shipped this model and told me to keep it after I informed them of their error. The grill is very easy to operate. It heats up very quickly and I noticed during the preheat temperatures reach over 600 degrees (the maximum on the thermometer). The temperature remains consistent as long as you keep the lid down. I have been experimenting so far but my best results have been with direct heat: chicken breasts, salmon filets, pork chops and asparagus. I had mixed results with indirect heat because I need a better thermometer. I ordered a pizza stone because I think this grill will make great crispy crust pizza due to its high temperatures. 

The two wheel design works great for me. My backyard patio is made from pavers and the two weeks move easily over them. I think the original 4 castor design would be a little more problematic. The grill supposedly weighs over 100 pounds but I found no difficulty moving it.

The only negative characteristics are purely cosmetic. The metal surfaces on the grill front and side tables scratch very easily. I tried to polish it up using Dawn and a non-abrasive sponge and it left abrasions. I tried using Simple Green and a paper towel but it didn't polish the metal. The other problem is that the "hubcaps" seem to always pop out when I move the grill. I can't figure how to lock them in place.

text: We assembled the E-210 Spirit II Grill ourselves.  Easy, and a very sturdy grill.  Then had to try it out with a barbecued steak. We have a small Weber at home purchased 10 years ago that still cooks up a great barbecue. (4) The drip pan works far better than any other brand of grill.  In the past I had to fabricate drip pans for other grills...those never quite worked right.  Weber knows how to do it. (5) And best of all, the grill top itself cleans up easily.  After it cools, we take it to the kitchen sink, use a rough scrubbing sponge and soap, and in a minute have a clean grill top for the next barbecue. (6) Haven't really had a chance to use the thermometer except to know when the grill is ready.  But a nice touch...especially if a rotisserie is added.

So I finally decided to turn the valve on the tank way down so as not to have it fully open.  That seems to work better and helps control the heat.
Also, the cross members on the grill are raised higher that the up and down grill members.  This makes it difficult to turn anything that you are cooking with a spatula.  So I have turned the grill over for cooking anything that I may use a spatula with.  My other Webers that I have owned are not like this. title: Glad I Purchased the Weber Spirit II Propane Grill
text:
I thought hard about purchasing the Spirit II Weber grill.  It is far from the least expensive grill of its size and capabilities on the market.  Not having purchased a gas grill for many years I did some research before deciding.  Reading reviews and looking carefully at various grills.  It was clear that Weber stands out in quality and customer service.

Once I decided on the Spirit II, because it fit my needs best of the Weber line, I chose to assemble it myself.  This was remarkably easy.  I am elderly but reasonably handy and everything fit together perfectly.  I only needed a second person (my wife) for two minor steps where her help was mainly needed for safety.  I assembled the grill on my deck and there are small parts that can vanish through decking -- watch out!

With the grill assembled, propane canister purchased and all connections tested as advised in the manual (I didn't need the video assistance available but it was nice to have it if needed), it was time to fire it up.  Again, the starting process worked perfectly and the grill quickly heated to 550 F.

Now having used it for several weeks and numerous dinners, I can confidently say the purchase was an excellent choice and well worth the investment.  Combined with the iGrill Bluetooth thermometers, it makes grilling a breeze.  I haven't tried anything really hard but I can, at this point, confidently say that I'm enjoying my new grill and hope do so for a long time to come!

As we all know, it takes a couple uses to learn any new grill so the first few items cooked, although delicious, weren’t my best work. I’ve since dialed it in and have enjoyed smoked ribs, smoked chicken, roasted peppers, corn, onions, potatoes, burgers, dogs, and chicken. 

After the first use, I noticed a chip in the enamel on the lid and although I couldn’t be 100% sure if it came that way, I emailed service and about a week later a new kid arrived. So, that was pretty awesome. 

I only have two issues with this grill and the first is that I waited so long to return to charcoal grilling. The second is that the little ledges the cooking grate sits on are not perfectly level so I have a little wiggle in the grate. It does not have any affect on cooking, I’m just a little OCD, so….

All in all, this is a great grill with a large cooking surface and can sear steak at 559-600, smoke a pork butt at 225, and everything in between. Do yourself a flavor and go buy one immediately! (see what I did there?!?! Lol)

Great small charcoal grill for those who like the charcoal grilling method.  Being the grill is titled "premium" I would have liked to see it come with a charcoal box to segment the charcoal easier/ quicker.

Also the lid has a small "lip" on it for hanging it on the main bottom portion of the grill tub is a cheap and a nuisance at times.  I have seen some kettle charcoal grills that actually have a mounting mechanism that you can put the lid in for "holding" as you are tending to the grilling items on the grates.  This would be much easier.  Again as a "premium" I would have thought that feature would come with the grill I purchased.  

Finally, would like to have better temp control such as the ability to raise and lower the cooking grate.

title: Easily the best grill I've used
text: I had high expectations for this grill because of the Weber brand and because it has received very high reviews from sources I trust most (i.e. Wirecutter). It also wasn't cheap. My expectations have been far exceeded. This thing is solidly built and performs incredibly. I used the optional app-based setup instructions, which were really helpful. It ignites quickly, easily, and consistently, heats fast and evenly, and allows a great level of control over temperature. I really like the two-sided grill grates (one side thin for more delicate foods, one side wider) -- the wider side provides an excellent sear with minimal sticking.

title: Good temperature controls
text: It does flare up ( vs our old infrared grill). Plus side, it holds the temperature  close to spot on!  Use this grill at least 5 days a week!

title: Bad legs good grill
text:

I took it home and bent the metal back into place well enough so that the two legs fit in place and I was able to use some bolts I had to secure the two legs in place.

The grill works great..  My wife was especially surprised how much better this cooks than our previous grill.

title: Bring back the wheels
text: Assembly was fine, grill heats up fast and cooks well.  One complaint:  whereas I could easily roll my old Weber Silver on its four caster wheels, this one replaces two of the wheels with posts, so you have to lift the end to move it.  Instead of a handle to lift, it has a fold-out shelf.  If the shelf is collapsed (e.g., to make it easier to put on the cloth cover), you can't easily move the grill; if the shelf is extended, the act of using it as a handle puts stress on the folding joint. Better design would have been to put four wheels on the grill, just like the old ones.  Two caster wheels would cost a couple of bucks ... ?

text: The removable center piece to the grilling grate makes it harder to clean and gets in the way of scooping burgers with a scapula sometimes. The two tool hooks on the handle are actually awkwardly shaped (too wide) so most tools can't fit on there and I had to buy a separate kettle grill tool hanger. Just after two cooks, I've noticed the cover is scuffing from placing it on the cover holder.  All that being said, I do love the ash catcher pot. And I enjoy that the top vent handle is plastic so I can safely adjust the vent with my bare hands. But was it worth the price? I don't think so but others will disagree and I might change my mind if this grill lasts me over 10 years. Also, the triangle leg support came bent but customer service is very good and they sent me a replacement free of charge.

In the end I could not deny that the Weber grills were designed and built so much better than the competition. We have grilled  probably once a week since bringing our Weber home. The food has turned out amazing! We will always own the quality of Weber going forward.

title: I'm not really satisfied with this product
text: I'm surprised how little use of this grill it takes to go from full propane tank to not empty but unusable due to low tank pressure - and the tank-fullness scale absolutely does not work -- it sticks at any given point, and by agitating the tank on the hanger, you can get it to register full, empty, or anything in between, regardless of whether it's actually full or empty.  I have looked online to see how to convert it to natural gas, as running out to get more propane after every 2 or so meals is very inconvenient (and expensive).  It is also disappointing that it never gets hot enough to really sear a steak, though with a full propane tank, the steaks come out quite good.  Burgers are a different story - they either fail to cook properly on the outside (with the hood open) or they bake through like a meat loaf (with the hood closed).

title: Third Time Lucky
text:
After seven years and two tries at grilling with another well-known brand (no names, but it rhymes with 'mar foil') I finally took the plunge and spent the extra money on a Weber.

Oh. My. Goodness.

A couple of things I'd like to point out. First of all, our local Lowes has about 97 grills lined up outside for your consideration. There are several different brands out there on display...but no Webers. Those are all INSIDE where it's warm and dry. Now, why do you suppose that is? My theory is that they want to move the lesser product. Greater turnover, greater profit. Which is not a bad thing by any means, but having had two of those inferior grills (once again, no names, but it rhymes with harm oil) I can tell you plainly: if you get one of those based on price, you get what you pay for. Example: I can easily pick one of those things up with one hand, less the propane tank, of course. I'm sure they're NOT made of tin foil, but it sure does feel that way.

But the Weber! It's DIFFERENT.

Full disclosure: when I bought this behemoth in mid-June, I had the option of course to have it assembled and delivered. Had I taken that route, it might've been delivered by 4th of July. Maybe. As it happened, we were without a stove in our home at the time, so a cooker of some sort was pretty urgently needed. As such, I drove over to Lowes and picked it up in the box.

A big box.

A VERY big box. And heavy. About 120 pounds, if the specs are to be believed, and I do. And big? It just barely fit in the back of my little Nissan. But it did fit, and I did get it home, then I had to figure out how to get the darned thing OUT of my little Nissan! My sweetie and I are both older and arthritic, so this wasn't easy, but we did finally get it out of the back of the car and onto the ground. I didn't even try to carry it onto the veranda; instead, I opened the box and took it in piecemeal. Then I started the ever-dreaded assembly process.

But...surprise! It was easy. No swearing involved! The instructions are very well illustrated; just keep in mind that they apply to two different models of Spirit grills. If you remember this and read carefully you'll have no problems. There's even an app available that demonstrates things if you have issues, but I didn't have to take that route. Maybe two-three hours working slowly and deliberately and the job was done, and when finished my new Spirit II E-310 felt remarkably solid, unlike its tinfoil predecessors. It also felt heavy, but not at all bulky, and surprisingly maneuverable with its big plastic wheels. Just lift it from the left side and roll it around. 

Having accomplished this, it was time to mount the propane tank and fire it up for the first time. I love the fact that it's got a weight-based gauge on the side...it takes at least some of the guesswork out of the process. Just eyeball it and you'll know if you have enough fuel to finish your day's cooking tasks.

So. No more fooling around: turn on the gas, set the port side knob to ignite, and push the button, Max. 

POP! Off she goes. And boy howdy, does she go! I preheated the thing to 500 degrees in just a few minutes. I allowed it to burn off the manufacturing goo, then shut everything down for seasoning. A little olive oil cooking spray on the grates and away we went again. And in no time at all, it was burgers and hot dogs for everyone! YUMMERS!

Mind you, this is just our first go-round with Webbo (for everything must have a name, mustn't it?) but if it all goes as well as the first time, I imagine I will be enjoying this for a long time to come. After all, it comes with a ten year warranty, for heavens sake. Guess they mean for you to be using it for a while! I did invest in a cover, though it will be sitting on our screened-in veranda. Better safe than sorry. Besides, it looks...well, stealthily cool, under that black cloak.

Lesson learned: you really do get what you pay for. Spend a little bit more money on the front end and get yourself something that will last.

title: Spirit II E-310 is a winner
text: I've been a Weber charcoal kettle guy forever, but my wife wanted a gas grill, so we have the Spirit II E-310 now. We selected this grill for its simplicity of design and small size. We didn't want a large grill taking up a lot of space on our deck, and the 310 fits the bill perfectly. Great Weber quality of finish. We ordered this grill from Ace Hardware, who assembled, delivered and set up the grill for us. The guys from Twins Ace Hardware in Fairfax VA did a great job, and even walked us thru the operation of the grill. While I'm still learning how to balance the gas elements' heat (vs charcoal cooking), so far everything we've grilled has turned out very well. Cleaning the grill is easy. Overall I am very pleased with our E-310.

title: Good, but not great.
text:
Overall it's a very solidly-built grill, and heats up really fast to high temperatures. I like the folding side tray, which keeps it compact when covered, as well. There are a few cons, however:
1) The warming tray is somewhat loose and can easily be knocked out of place. It also makes it hard to reach the back of the main grill area.
2) While the grill heats up well, there are still some hot and cold spots. The front area, especially in the corners, does not heat up as well as the back and middle.
3) The "enameled cast iron" grill top is nice for cooking, but with 1 or 2 uses it's already showing lots of rust when cleaning with a weber grill brush. I dunno that I'd call this "enameled."

text: Grill seems to work great. Just used it for the first time today on the 4th of July. Giving it 3 stars because assembly was problematic. Got seven steps in and hit a roadblock. After navigating to a customer service rep over the phone, which led to no resolution, I had to spend a lot of time documenting the issue through photos and writing to send an email to Weber. They sent me a new part, but it took three weeks to get to me. With the new part on hand I proceeded to continue assembly. I got the job done, but encountered two or three other instances of parts not quite being shaped right to fit into each other. In these cases I had to manually bend the parts to fit correctly. There was clearly a quality control issue, at least with my grill.

One must lift the other end to move the grill. It's not a big deal but I wonder what shape they will be in in 5-10 years. Also the little hub caps keep being popped off by the  axle sliding back and forth. I had the opportunity to disassemble my old grill and was surprised to see that all the fasteners were bright and shiny because they were made of stainless steel. The fasteners for this grill seem to be made of some kind of plastic which should be corrosion resistant but I wonder if they are going to get brittle after a few years of seasonal changes. text:
This grill lasted 3.5 years, but only because I dragged it across the finish line for the last year+.
Admittedly, I grill a lot - about 6x per week. In the 3.5 years I had it, I replaced the flavorizer bars 4 or 5 times and it probably should have been twice that many. The temperature gauge stopped working about 2 years in. I got used to where the hot spots were and worked around them. The burners literally fell apart and had to be replaced which was NOT easy to do as the screws were warped from the heat. And then a few days ago, the metal supports holding up the pan under the burners broke and the pan fell out of the bottom rendering it basically unusable because the grill is on patio pavers and I can’t have all that grease falling onto them that the pan would normally catch.
All that said, I liked the grill. I decided to buy another Weber, just larger and with more BTU’s and thankfully, the new one doesn’t have a burner tube running along the back of the grill creating hot spots.
Given that I probably used it 1000 times or more, I feel like I got my money’s worth out of it and that’s why I’m not filing a warranty claim (just because you can doesn’t mean you should) as the warranty supposedly covers the major issues I described up to 5 years.
Would I have liked it to last longer? Of course. But I used it A LOT and can’t complain too awful much. It’s a solid little grill that will last most people a very long time.

title: Love it, but it comes with dents
text: We love to cook on the Weber grill.  Before purchasing, we did research and checked reviews.  We agree with most users that the grill is great. No hot spots so food is evenly cooked.  There were only 2 minor complaints, but not a reason to not purchase.  First, the box arrived in great condition.  However, when the parts were taken out, the base the wheels are on was dented.  We had to press it down in order for all the wheels to be touching the ground.  Also, the top of the cabinet door had a big dent it in it.  We could not straighten it out but it is not noticeable unless the door is open. These two incidents had to have happened on the manufacturing end and there are videos showing we are not the only ones to receive these dented items. For the price, I expected better.  Secondly, the propane tank scale is a great feature, but apparently all tanks aren't created equally.  All of our tanks have wider lips and cannot catch on the scale.  We remedied it by turning the tank around 45 degrees so that the back hole would catch on it.  It's pushing the limit on the hose, but it works.  Either a wider lip on the scale or a hose an inch longer would be better.  Still, we love the grill.

title: Awesome grill !
text:
Customer Service - 5 stars
Product - 4.5 Stars only because I expected the highest quality from Weber the first time itself because they have been in business for a long time. 

I received the ocean blue Weber Kettle Grill as a gift. The color is really beautiful and has a pleasing shine to it in the sun. The unit was packaged nicely and was without any visible imperfections except for something that looks like a dent or a bad paint job on the lid. I was willing to overlook that imperfection, however, the day after installing everything I noticed that the paint at the contact between the lid and it's top handle started chipping away. I suspect this may be either a bad paint job or a problem with the type of Ocean Blue paint. Anyways, customer service responded to my concern within a day and offered to send a new lid immediately. The new cover has no imperfections. I appreciate the Weber customer service team for resolving the issue very quickly.

I smoked wings and grilled burgers on the unit until now. I am still learning to control the temperature properly on the unit. Occasionally smoke leaks from under the lid at some points but that should go away with more usage. The cleanup is pretty easy except for the ash flying around but then that is expected with a charcoal grill :)

Overall I am satisfied with the product and look forward to cooking with it more.

I have had Weber grills for the last 20 years.  Moved to a new location and converted four neighbors over to Smokey Joes.  It was the flavor from indirect heat grilling that won them over.

I have grilled Thanksgiving turkeys on my Weber.  You cut the rib bone out and separate the thighs from the bird prior to cooking.  Set up coals for indirect on both sides of the kettle. title: Cooks very well, excellent design
text:
The good - and a lot of it: well placed, quality temp gauge & Weber name plate, very good quality high-temp enamel paint on top and properly painted in the factory for excellent adhesion, cast iron grates: excellent dual profile design and porcelain coating quality , reliable and easily serviceable electronic ignition that so far has lighted first time every time, excellent gas valve portioning, excellent quality stainless steel burner tubes and rear tracer lighting tube, wonderful carcass bottom angular design for guiding grease to well-placed, easy front access, adequate capacity grease pan, tank placement on right side makes easy tank access and frees inside for a nice shelf made of no rust, no rot plastic with slat surfaces that looks attractive. I can't report the durability of the plastic wheels and stationary leg feet. Check other long-term reviews to see if they don't split like other brand grill wheels & feet.

The Improvable: grates lack a front finger hole to lift grate for brushing grate bottoms, stick-on badge next to right burner knob and Spirit name plate both applied crooked that makes grill look cheap, propane tank holder fits most, but not all tanks. Reported reliability of the i-Grill 3 needs to improve before I buy one.

Tips: regardless of what Weber says about no-stick techniques I've found the best practice that works every time for me is to use the Weber no-stick spray lube: preheat grill at the heat setting to be used for that food item: Example: burgers: preheat, medium heat to 450°, get everything ready for quick access, lift top, spray a little squirt right where one burger is going and put it immediately on, squirt next, quickly put next burger on, repeat, repeat, repeat, close top as quickly as possible not to lose too much heat. Then stainless steel brush the tops of grates right after taking off food - let cool, lift grates and brush the bottoms to dislodge hanging pieces. If there is a big crusty blob of burnt grease on a flavorizer bar I knock it mostly off with the brush then, but I don't scrape the rest unnecessarily. Voila, ready for next grilling with a nice, clean shiny, pre-seasoned grate. 

I hope that helps. This Weber heats pretty darn evenly front to back and side to side for me - unlike my last two grills, making it much easier to get a batch of burgers or steaks at the same doneness. I use Bluetooth meat thermometers always- but not the Weber brand until reviews of reliability improve. This and the crooked badges are the 5th star deletion. If I could have given 4 1/2 stars I would have, because everything else is excellent!

title: Can't Get Much Better Than This
text:
At present I can only rate this grill based upon it's looks, features, design and build quality.

I bought this to replace a 20 year old Weber Genesis Silver A grill which was worn out and ugly even though the old boy was still cooking (the original ignitor was still working !) .

This grill is so nice and clean and pretty that I have not had the heart to begin getting it all
nasty dirty and grill funky from cooking on it. 

Meanwhile I have a 1970ish Weber Imperial Sequoia 22 1/2 " BBQ wagon that I will continue using until I figure out what to cook on the new grill for the first time break in.

There is no doubt in my mind that this is the best gas grill ever made by Weber or any other 'Common Man's'  LP gas grill out there which is available for purchase in big box stores.

At first I had buyers remorse because I was sad to let go of my old Silver A Genesis because of all the good meals made on it and I could have kept it going for a couple of
more years (that is how good Weber made it) I have no regrets now. I did cannibalize
the Silver A for parts before donating the remainder to the Boy Scouts metal recycle bin.

title: Grilling perfection.
text: Bought my Weber spirit and researching extensively , and seeing nothing but positive reviews. Have to say , best decision ever. The spirit gets good and hot for searing, the heavy grates are awesome and easy to clean. The quality is evident in the build . It's heavy and solid , unlike the flimsy grills I have had in the past. It also makes a great small smoker with a pellet tube . The thick body and lid really hold heat well.  All in all, I look forward to a long happy life with my Weber !!!

text: So far the grilling area works fine but I have issues with two of the design features. I move my grill from the garage to outside to use it and then return it to the garage. Also, the part that holds the propane tank should have a higher bracket: the propane tank has fallen off when I moved the grill. I do like having the folding shelf and the propane measure features. I just wish they were executed better for the price I paid.

title: Mostly satisfied with constructive criticism
text:
I love the added height, the built in thermometer, the cool touch air vent, and easy slide lid.  I am less fond of the grate with the removable center piece; it makes it difficult to scrape.  Furthermore, unlike the traditional grate, I need a table to hold it while the grill warms up; I cannot hang it on the rim of the bowl otherwise the center falls on the ground.  I will probably end up replacing it with the standard hinged grate which is frustrating considering the price point.  Also, the warming rack is superfluous; it ends up getting in the way more than anything.  The jury is still out for me regarding the coal holders for between the grates.  During standard cooking (burgers, sausages, etc...), I have gone back to dumping the coals on one side of the grill and leaving the other side empty.  I see the potential value for longer cooks/roasts but need to try them more to determine their usefulness.  However, having learned how to cook on a kettle grill by simply shoveling all the coals to one side, it might be difficult to adjust.  

In summary: the added height, cool touch air vent, sliding lid, and especially color (I found an Ocean Blue) make me satisfied with this grill.  The added features (grate with removable center, charcoal bins, and warming rack) seemed nice at the time, but upon using them they are less than functional and might even get thrown away; the grill grate is especially frustrating.

text:
I bought The Master Touch 22" charcoal BBQ from weber earlier this summer and I'll always be sold on Weber products.  I previously had the first generation charcoal Weber for nearly 15 years until I thought it was time for an upgrade.  

The main difference between the first generation vs this one:
- The ventilation is more easily controlled in the Master Touch
- The handles are safer to manipulate
- I like the cover rest handle rather than burning the patio floor.  It was convenient when my balcony was made of concrete but now that I have a composite deck, I can't rest the cover on the floor with my old BBQ.

The only thing I wish was available is a heavy duty cover for this model.  The only one available is a light cover and it only attaches from one corner.  With stronger winds, the top actually comes off from underneath on the other unattached side.

Overall, very pleased and I also use a natural starter with the chimney.  BBQs are very good!

title: No Match For A Wood-Pellet Oven
text:
When our 17-year-old Weber grill’s framework rusted out from sitting in the elements . . . we replaced it with a wood-pellet grill.   After only a few uses, both my wife & I realized we were unsatisfied in the way ‘grilled’ items came off the wood-fired ‘oven.    There was no way to have direct and indirect cooking surfaces . . . there were no char marks . . . nor could one not cook with a rotisserie on it.   We came to the realization the wood-pellet ‘oven’ was simply not a true ‘grill!’
The decision was made to sell the wood-fired ‘oven’ and replace it with another three-burner Weber grill.   The Spirit E-310 fit the bill . . . and the nice thing is this grill has the burners oriented front to back, rather than side to side as the old grill had been.  This allows for both direct and indirect cooking surfaces easier . . . and the controls are up front and good-sized to control the burners.
We are totally satisfied with our new Weber grill and counsel everyone considering going with the ‘hype’ of wood-pellet grills to think long and hard before giving up the results which come off a Weber grill instead of an outdoor oven!

title: Quality of Grill
text: Excellent little grill for the most part, which reflects Weber's consistency in excellent quality and overall design. The gas-control knob actually does regulate the flame very well to provide different cooking settings. I have had other Weber grills (gas and charcoal) and they were all good investments for the money. My current purchase of the Q1200 portable grill has, so far, been a very good experience, but there are a couple of minor aspects of the product's design that could use improvement.  First is my frustration in cleaning cast iron grates which constantly need attention to mitigate food residue and fat buildup.  Coating the cast iron grates with a ceramic enamel coating only improves the cleaning process minimally.  Polished stainless steel grates, which for me, has been easier to clean, should be offered at least as an upgrade option.  Second, the interior surface of the lower cook-box should be polished to a smoother finish in order to facilitate better drainage of food juices and debris to the little collection pan underneath. Even with the current design being well-executed, buildup on the wall surfaces is still a problem.  This clean-up issue has been experienced in my other grill (Weber 'Spirit II') as well, and may or may not be something Weber can reengineer economically.  But, ..at he end of the day, ..I'm still happy in my purchase.  Weber continues to be the leader in grilling products.  Thanks for listening.

title: Weber Customer Service to the Rescue...Wow
text:
Initially freaked out as during my burn-in after 25 minutes grill temp was at 225? Made no sense as I could see that all 3 burners were lit so I immediately called Weber. Explained the situation and the guy told me he hopefully has a cure. We shut off the grill valves and closed the propane bottle. After a few minutes he instructed me to open the propane bottle very very slowly which I did and guess what? The grill came to life like a flame thrower. 

Tech explained to me that the propane bottle regulator had gone into a protective mode as it falsely detected a problem. And further stated that had I not done the corrective measures quickly it may have never come back to life (would have replaced at no charge). Said this is a situation with new regulator guidelines. Upon further investigation there is even mention of this in the manual (but let's be honest, who reads a gas grill manual)? 

Now the better news...this grill gets to temp very fast and 600-650 for steaks is a few minutes away. I've only grilled 5 times as a new owner but after examination I think this grill will be serving me for a long time.

Thanks Weber for having a phone technician available. Great customer service.

title: Don't let its size fool you!
text:
We purchased this grill at the start of the 2021 grilling season to take with us on our day trip excursions.  This grill is lightweight, compact and extremely versatile - capable of EASILY cooking enough burgers and steak for 6-8 people in short order.  At one point during the summer we were using this grill everyday to cook lunch and dinner and on the odd occasion even breakfast using the optional griddle plate.  The Q1200 follows similar design language to previous Weber Q models however, there are some notable features in the Q1200 that make the tiny price premium over the standard Q1000 worth splurging on.  These features include sturdy thermoplastic side tables that fold into the grill for storage, a temperature gauge, increased dome height (great if you like cooking taller items like whole chickens), and lastly, a fully electronic ignition system that is fast, easy, and reliable to use.  

The grill's interior sports a porcelain enamel coated cast iron cooking grate that is strategically designed to shield the gas ports (to prevent clogging and flare ups) on the burner from the food drippings.  Heat is very even and can get hot enough to sear steaks without much effort.  The gas inlet port is integrated with the gas pressure regulator and is designed such that it can accommodate the standard 1lb propane camping cylinders or be used with larger home style BBQ tanks using the accessory gas hose.  

While this grill is typically marketed to ideally cook for 4 that in reality, this grill has EASILY cooked for 6-10 people.  The grill space is generous and the height of the domed lid allows you to push food right to the edge of the grill to maximize your cooking space.  I’ve cooked 5 large steaks, a whole chicken along and have made an entire 3 course breakfast for 6 using the accessory griddle plate.

Cleanup is a cinch as the grill's smooth curving design allows fat and grease to slide into a generously sized drip tray located centrally at the bottom of the grill.  The cooking grates, while mostly cleanable by simply burning it off can be easily removed in 2 small sections and soaked in a sink of warm soapy water.  

Weber not only created the perfect portable grill but they’ve escalated the Q name into another world by offering an entire ecosystem of Q series accessories.  The list of useful add-ons is extensive and allows a Q owner to scale their grill to suit their needs.  I’d argue this grill is so versatile that it can likely outperform (if not outright replace) lesser home BBQs.  

I have trusted the Weber name for the past 20 years and expect nothing but quality and perfection and the Weber Q1200 is no exception.  Its extremely well made and I would expect this thing to easily last me 20+ years.  Like all Weber products, you can buy replacement parts for their grills at VERY reasonable prices much of which, are still available for 30+ year old products.  

Look no further if you’re considering a compact grill.  Nothing in this size and price class can even compete with the Q series grill.  Competitors have tried numerous times to make a better product but end up copying elements of Weber’s design.  I guess copying and mimicking a Weber Grill is the greatest form of flattery after all :)

title: Weber Spirit II E-310 assembly and cooking review.
text:
Well I owned a Weber Silver 'A' and it was working fine. My wife decided I needed a new grill so she purchased a Spirit II E-310. 
I do like the extra burner though.
I did have issues assembling E-310 though. The tapped holes in the cast grill body had a burr on the trailing edge of the tapped hole and since I wasn't at my shop where I have all the tools I need to do repairs and fix manufacturing mistakes, I ran a drill bit through the threaded hole and then used an adjustable wrench on the screwdriver to seat the screw completely. Problem solved, you couldn't see the screw head because it was covered by the burned knob plate. 
The second issue was the cheap aluminum guard over the opening for the drip pan. I needed to modify it by bending and trimming to make it fit correctly. Again I think that may have been a casting issue, whatever it's done.
The last gripe I had was a marketing issue. For the life of me I don't know why they used a sticker on the right hand shelf instead of a piece of cardboard with the marketing information. There's that little curved arrow printed on the corner of the sticker letting you know where to start peeling it off. Yeah right, the sticker started to delaminate and now I have a partial sticker on the shelf that looks like stainless steel but attracts a magnet. I guess I need Goop and/or alcohol to remove what is left of it with out scratching it. We'll see.
As far as the grilling goes it's a Weber do I need to explain? If I need to you wouldn't understand. My Silver A was 22 years old and was working fine and lasted a hour on the side of the road with a free sign on it.
I gave it 5 stars because it's a Weber. If there was two categories one for cooking quality and another for fit and finish quality the cooking would have been 5 stars and fit and finish would get 1 because I was upset that I had to make stuff fit and peel a sticker off.

Weber customer service verified the grill came off their assembly line in July 2021 by the serial number included with the grill yet they would not honor the warranty. When I contacted the business I bought the grill from, the return shipping label they provided was to a Home Depot in GA. So even though I bought it on E-Bay, the grill apparently came from a Home Depot. So if you find a good deal on E-Bay for a brand new grill from Weber, beware...they will not honor their warranty. title: Great little camp grill
text:
So I bought my first Weber Genesis Grill this past Christmas to replace a 25-year old grill of a different manufacturer that I'd had since new.  It was reliable as a rock, had 3 rebuilds over the years but the poor thing was ready to fall apart.  The Genesis grill was a terrific upgrade and gave me an idea of the quality of the Weber brand.

We got a new travel trailer in January 2022 and we needed a reliable grill to take on our camping excursions.  Naturally, I started looking at a suitable Weber grill to fill that need.  After much looking at all of the various "portable" models I decided on the Q1200 since we didn't really need anything bigger since it's just the wife and myself.

The Q1200 is  a great little grill for our camping excursions.  It's neat and compact and it's almost like they designed it to fit in the storage compartment of our Arctic Fox 25W camper.

I did buy an aftermarket 8-foot braided stainless steel adapter hose to be able to use a 20# propane tank versus the 1# disposable canisters because of the ridiculous cost of the 1# canisters that are about 4X the cost of bulk propane.  The adapter hose still allows the use of the 1# canisters if that is what you have available without any modifications to the grill.

Ultimately, I might modify the grill to hook up directly to the camper's propane system, but that's down the road.  The grill itself works great for 2-3 people though it loses heat very fast when the lid is opened to flip the burgers, hotdogs, chicken or steaks.  You definitely have to cook with the lid closed.  From my experience, you'll get maybe 2-3 grill sessions out of a 1# canister so you'd better take several with you if that is your choice of fuel sources.  With the 20# tank it's not much of a concern as you can lift the tank and readily tell if you have enough fuel for a camping trip.  If it's low, fill the 20# tank up for $10-$12 @ $3/gallon.

Make sure you get spare aluminum pans to catch the drippings out of the bottom of the grill too.  They tend to blow away if it gets windy and they definitely are needed if you're cooking steaks or chicken as the meat tends to drip A LOT!

text: Overpriced grill that lacks quality material. I've owned this for a year now and have cooked throughout the seasons. This cooks well enough, and seems to keep a decently even temperature in the middle and rear. Though the front tends to cook cooler. My issues are with the quality of the exterior. The stainless components are an incredibly cheap form of "stainless." Unless you clean after each use with recommended cleaner and microfiber cloth it will stain and discolor. Which seems ridiculous for an outside grill. Which I also keep covered. There is much better quality stainless material available and for the price, this grill shouldn't be that delicate. The painted lid isn't much better. The "porcelain-enameled" cast iron grates are "meh," they require just as much upkeep and care as regular cast iron. My issue is with how thick the grates are, it just increases the surface area that is going to stick to your food. If they were about half the thickness they would probably be better. Overall, I expected better quality and less delicacy for the price and from Weber, though it does cook decently. For the next question on the form, "would you recommend this product to a friend?" Yes, but only if you buy it heavily discounted, it certainly isn't "quality" for the full MSRP.

title: Why?
text: Love Weber, love the 22” Kettle, but… why would you strip features that have always been associated with the kettle? I have been using the kettle for 40+ years and two features that I’ve always taken for granted are now gone or different. Why? #1-the handle has ALWAYS doubled as a grill tool hook. No bells and whistles necessary, just sized to accept the lioops at the end of my grill tools. Now that has been made impossible with the new grill handle and to get this feature you have to upgrade to the bells and whistles version that transforms the handle to have hooks… c’mon. That’s a basic grill feature and your monetizing of a basic need sours me on a company I have loved for decades (this is my 5th kettle and I have two gas grills as well). #2 the kettle lid has ALWAYS had a hook in the lid aligned with the lid handle in the N/S orientation, but for some unknown reason you now move the hook to the E/W orientation?! Why? I imagine it has to do with the lid catcher for the new bells and whistles version, but that’s a bad reason. Whoever decided that was a good idea should know their base.

text:
New grill and multiple issues, including with Lowe's. We finally got this new grill, our replacement after six years, and Lowe's cancelled delivery three times. The manager at the local Lowe's expedited a delivery and the grill arrived with 17 points of damage, which I documented with photos with my complaint. 
After getting the photos, the manager called me and said this kind of damage 
was typical" with Weber grills they dellvered. I told him that was unacceptable and I demanded a followup from Lowe's. Finally a different manager called and scheduled delivery of a new grill he handpicked before assembly. We had a Saturday morning delivery planned and the Lowe's delivery driver refused to deliver the grill. I got this information because I wanted an update on delivery. The manager did call back and he sent two of employees in a personal pickup to deliver the grill and pick up the damaged one. The replacement grill did arrive without noticeable damage.

I called the manager to thank him and he said finding a grill from Weber without damage, sometimes extensive, is difficult. In fact, he told me Lowe's had delivered a Weber grill and the entire top was "caved in" and Lowe's was trying "to make it right with the customer." If this is the kind of "quality control" that Weber has, your company has major problems.

When I attached the propane tank there was obvious leak at the pressure fitting, so I called Weber, explained the issue, and did receive a new hose and pressure fitting assembly. So far so good.

For a small grill, the Spirit II E-210 feels sturdy and substantial and should last for many years.  It's easy to put together if you go slowly and pay attention.  I'm a 70 year old woman and I figure if I can put this little grill together by myself, almost anyone else can.  I've been using the grill now for a few weeks and the flavor bars make a big difference in the taste of foods!  Cleanup is easy and fast.  I love my new grill!  

On another note, when I first hooked up the regulator hose to the propane tank, there was a leak.  I called Weber and forwarded the info they requested.  Two days later a new hose and regulator was delivered to my back door.  At this point I had to get help to change out the hose because the fittings were so tight it took more strength than I had.  Ultimately it took two people to separate the hose, but when that was done, the rest was simple.

title: Master-Touch Huge Disappointment
text:
I have been a Webber charcoal grill owner since 1985.  Owning 18" and 22" grills and a Webber Charcoal Smoker.  Unfortunately the new Master-Touch Grill 22" is so disappointing. Webber has gone away from the solid quality grills they used to manufacture to making a very cheap knock-off of their originals.  

- One of the best features was the "one touch" system to remove the ashes.  it is now very difficult to remove the ash bucket and it holds less than half the ashes it used to. 
- The Gourmet BBQ hinged grill grate is useless 90% of the time.  I get what you're trying to do and its good for the few times you need it but is should come w a standard grate too or make the Gormet System an add on
- The grill is ~ inches taller which makes it very unstable/tipsy.

I could go on but suffice to say its so disappointing from a great company.  I recommend shopping around.  The only thing they got right were some cool colors.  :-(

title: First one was good - this one seems even better
text: This is my second Spirit II grill. The first one was great but after 8 years of my neglect and the wet weather in Florida - it finally rusted beyond repair (although one burner still worked). Most of the rust was on the inside of the doors that contained the gas cylinder and around the small wheels underneath. This time I bought on with the ability to hang the gas on the outside and it has 2 larger wheels on one side instead of 4 small ones under the main grill - it seems less affected by the wet, humid weather.  Its also easier to hang the propane cylinder on the outside beneath the permanent  shelf on the right side. Note that only the shelf on the left side folds down. The grill starts up like a champ and with the two burners on high can reach 450° F in a few minutes. It has enough room on the cooking grills to cook enough "meat" for probably 8 hungry people.  So unless you think you will be barbecuing for the entire neighborhood - you can buy this two burner instead of the larger 3 burner.  Overall it's a great, well made gas grill that sells for a very reasonable price. It's also important to know that buying replacement parts and extra add-ons is easy to do either on line or at major home repair stores.

title: 3 burner that out performs my old 4 burner
text:
This is my first Weber grill ever.  I've always wanted one and I got this one as a Father's day gift.

I have to say that I REALLY love it.  The grill itself is solid and doesn't have that flimsy metal twisting feel when you open the lid.  All the knobs are tight and I am very impressed on how the ignition system is wired.  

The battery compartment is inside the cabinet rather than directly behind the ignition button (which is usually more exposed to elements).  I'm looking forward to seeing how this configuration works and if it will mean reliable grill starts for more than a 4 month stretch before it quits.

The heating is completely even across the total cooking surface; no hot or cool "spots" to worry about.  I also think that this little 3 burner grill is much hotter than the 4 burner grill it replaced.  I was able to crank out a LOAD of food during our 4th of July cookout, much more efficiently than if I were cooking with my old 4 burner.

I'm super impressed and am looking forward to many years of cooking and ownership.

text: The Weber Master-Touch is it. I also own a Weber Genesis Propane grill and I am proud of it. There are convenience and control realities with Propane grills that I enjoy. They serve their purpose. I also own a highly rated durable charcoal grill that is built with extreme longevity in mind. The problem with that charcoal grill is that it will not get hot enough for a spectacular sear on a steak. Way more than half the occasions I grill our meals Ribeye or Filet Mignon are the protein of choice, so a good sear is very important to me. Because my charcoal grill falls a bit short temperature wise I occasionally elect to use the propane grill for the high searing heat I can dial up with ease. I wanted a charcoal grill that could reach 450-500 degrees reliably and still have structural durability for at least a few years. There is a cooking celebrity chef who has a tv show and they feature grilled meals. That chef uses the Weber Master-Touch grill. The features of the grill and ease of use on the show made me decide that I wanted that specific model. I am glad that I got it. The tolerances of my unit after assembly are snug and temperature control is easy. With my old durable grill I have to glove up if I want to adjust airflow or I will burn myself. On the Weber there are handles and levers that enable airflow adjustment quickly without requiring protective gloves. I remain glad to own my old durable grill, but my new Weber Master-Touch has become the star of my grilling equipment.

title: Supplied gas regulater leaks easily
text:
Major issues with the gas regulator. The one supplied uses a cheap plastic retaining ring near the hose that if its put under any stress (even mild stress), it gives way and allows gas to escape out the side.  I obtained a replacement from Weber, which I thought was great at the time (maybe i was sold a faulty one), but after installing the replacement and placing the tank back on its hanger, i could hear gas escaping again anytime the hose was not situated perfectly strait where it connects to the gas tank.  Propane will escape just next to the black screw on connector that you use to tighten the regulator onto the propane tank.  This really seems like one of the places where you might not want to cut corners as having a gas leak in any circumstance could cause a fire / explosion.  

At this point it appears as though i will have to obtain a decent gas regulator from another source since the model supplied (made in China), leaks way to easily.  After a search online, I see others have complained about this same issue.  I can see a date on my replacement regulator (7/21) that may be its manufacture date.  

The grill works well for cooking, but can struggle to get to a suitable cooking temperature if the ambient outdoor temp falls below freezing, or has significant wind passing by.   Also if you attempt to move it, and lift it by the tray opposite the wheels to roll it, the tray can detach from the size of the grill, as its not sturdily secured with the hardware provided.  This grill can also blow over in the wind if you put a grill cover on it as the base is not heavy enough to hold it by itself (I now weight it down since that happend 1x and left a dent in the lid).

title: The Original Kettle: Great value and performance.
text:
Don't get all the fancy-dancy outdoor stoves. Do it right and get this.

Don fiddle with propane knobs, replace parts, call repair techs. Go with simple and best.

After 18 years of being dragged, beaten, melted and burned, it was time to replace my 22-inch black Weber Kettle. This time I went for the gold, or copper, in this case. The original kettle is the best grill on the market. I am a firm believer that cooking on gas or propane is grilling, but not barbequing. If you're using gas or propane, you may as well do it in the kitchen. I would have brought the wheelless, battered grill with me, but the movers would not allow it in the van.

I subjected my Weber to charred mesquite chunks and branches, oak blocks, and hickory for 18 years. It never saw briquettes. The grill held its own, and the new premium has stepped in to pick up where the old one left off. I am impressed and appreciate the redesigned ash catcher. The thermometer in the lid is an excellent addition. No more holding palms over the fire and counting, "one thousand, two thousand" for very hot, "three thousand, four thousand" for medium, and "five thousand, six thousand" for add more charcoal and wait.

I look forward to another 18 years of use, but this time, I'll ensure the bag of mesquite charcoal isn't too close to the grill to catch fire and melt the tires.

The printed directions were not as clear as they once were. I don't like fussing with my phone to assemble anything. The screen is too small. The use of petroglyphs to cover assembly in all languages needs better drawings or words. 

This is the fifth Weber in my life, and the wheels are the same pain in the neck and frustration to install as they were when I assembled my first Weber in 1972. Some things just haven't improved with age.

title: Standard propane bottles do not fit the Q1200
text:
The Q1200 grill has a known problem with the regulator. There are many complaints on Amazon reviews about this issue. It will not allow you to screw on a standard green 1 pound propane bottle because the bottle interferes with the rear wraparound handle. The 1 pound bottles are approved for use with this grill per the users manual, the website, and customer service, but they do not fit. So they sent me a replacement regulator which I installed. But since the regulator has not been redesigned, the 1 pound propane bottle still will not fit. 
Weber customer service has been terrible through this ordeal. They do not bother to read the emails, or look at the attached photos I send. They just repeatedly give you canned, off the wall, unrelated, canned answers. Totally useless. What good is their 5 year warranty?
If you ever intend to use this grill with the standard propane bottles, I would buy something else. If you intend to use it with a 20 pound tank and a hose, it should be OK.

title: Master touch is all you need. No more pellet grill
text:
This is a highly versatile charcoal bbq. It absolutely slays any meat you decide to grill/sear/smoke. This is my 4th Weber grill. (18in base kettle x7 years, 18in Smokey mountain x3 years, Weber Spirit II propane grill x1 year, 22in Master touch kettle) all have been very solid and serviceable. This smokes just as good as the Smokey Mountain and way better than the pellet grill I replaced with this kettle. Don’t be fooled by the pellet grills; charcoal and wood chunks create a far superior smokey flavor on your meat. Best tri-tip and pulled pork in my life came off this kettle. I only have two negatives. I wish the center grate for the Gourmet accessories stayed in place when I took the grill off as opposed to falling out every time I try to refill my charcoal on a new grill/smoke. Additionally I installed a secondary grill lid thermometer on the vent side of the lid so I can get a better reading of temperature where my meat is located (vent over meat) when I do indirect grilling/smoking.
The bottom line is Weber Has been making this style of grill for over 70 years now and the recipe really hasn’t changed too much because when you start off with something that’s near perfect, there’s not much more you can do to make it better. This really can do it all. Thanks Weber for making fantastic quality grills at an obtainable price point. When you hear charcoal grill, you think Weber kettle.

title: Quality Control Issues/Prompt Resolution
text:
There are quality control problems at Weber. First, they shipped a major component that made assembly impossible. Next, the regulator failed almost immediately and blocked the gas transmission to the grill. There's an indication of a design defect in the warning to open the source gas tank very slowly so the regulator doesn't lock up. That tells us that they've run into a lot of regulator problems and that they haven't engineered the mechanism right. Nothing should be that sensitive. (I have a degree in mechanical engineering, and worked in the field for a number of years, so I have some history of dealing with mechanical designing.) They know that the regulator is underdesigned, and they're trying to pass the issue onto the consumer. Presumably, in time, they'll redesign the regulator to work properly and not fail so easily.
       On the positive side, the customer support was largely very responsive. They replaced the incorrect part (It took 6 days to arrive), and they didn't dispute my recognition that the regulator was at fault for the grill not working. Again, they promptly replaced the regulator (taking 4 or 5 days). The only fault I found with customer support was that neither of the agents knew enough to say, "We're sorry that you're having a problem." That magic word, 'sorry,' helps a lot, and it's clear that the agents haven't been trained to acknowledge that their mistakes have inconvenienced a customer. The prompt resolutions certainly helped, as did the positive attitudes, but it never hurts to accept responsibility AND apologize for it.
