title: Excellent grill with a pretty good regulator
text:
I purchased the Q1200 after researching reliable and high performance portable grills for RV camping. I need high enough output to give a good sear, enough area to cook a couple of courses at a time for 2-4 people, and roomy enough to fit a small Dutch oven for baking, but compact and light enough for the portability needed in my Aliner Classic.  This meets all those needs and I highly recommend it.  I purchased the optional griddle half which increases its usefulness to breakfast (eggs, hashbrowns, bacon/sausages) and grilling vegetables without having to clean dishes, a definite bonus.  

I found two drawbacks in the Q1200 regulator.  The first is that it does not turn the flame down to a low enough setting (it generally won't go below 300 degrees on the built in thermometer) reducing the ability to simmer for long times or smoke meats on the go (with a pellet tube). For this reason I give the grill 4 stars and not 5.

The second, temporary but more serious, problem (well-handled by Weber) was a failure of the regulator entirely. I have a hose to run the grill off the main propane tank and eliminate green cans (cheaper, more reliable, and more ecologically friendly). This worked extremely well all summer over 18 nights, but on a fall camp out it would not light.  After unsuccessfully trying the "regulator reset" instructions found numerous places online I was certain the regulator was faulty and needed replacement.

Weber customer service is definite plus and I was helped at the call center by a terrific agent who made me confident I was going to get the correct part which Weber shipped without cost and I got within two days.  Clear and easy replacement instructions and about 15 minutes and we are off and ready to go again. 

In short this is a terrific and convenient powerhouse of a portable grill and if the regulator tuned it down to a lower level it would be perfect.

title: Kettle Premium adds to our family tradition
text:
The Original Kettle grill is my go to standard and holds a real place of honor in our home... This was the model my dad always had on our porch when I was growing up, always a Webber kettle, never propane.  After I graduated from college and started making a home with my now-wife, we invited him over to a cook-out for my stepson's 4th birthday.  We had a little tiny hibachi from the grocery store we were going to cook hotdogs on. My dad went out and bought us our first Webber as a gift. It meant a lot.   
We held on to that grill for 15 years! (And technically, it was still in working order for the most part). But this year, just before Thanksgiving, I decided it was time to treat myself to an upgrade.  I looked over all the options, but in the end, it was undeniable that the classic kettle grill serves me perfectly, and never complicates the goal and reason I like grilling- standing outside, cooking with fire and smoke, making delicious food that keeps your family close. 

We live in an urban row home, and this grill is ideal for the front porch. It does not take up much space, it's easy to move around, and (pretty) easy to clean. I never have to plug it into an outlet, and it does not require me to keep a tank of propane sitting around.  It's also completely understated- not to flashy or attractive to passers-by, and somewhat unassuming. But in performance, it punches above it's weight- grilling, searing, smoking, I can easily fire it up to grill a couple of sausages or cook a platter of hot dogs and burgers, sear up some chicken thighs or smoke 30 wings, and I've used it for our Thanksgiving turkey for the past 5 years.  
In buying the new model I was a little skeptical about the price jump to the "Premium" model, but after we've used it 4-5 times, I'm really glad we went with it.  The heat shield under the handle is a great improvement (on the last model I had for 15 years, the handle melted after we used some pretty big/dense lump of charcoal on time). I also really love the built-in thermometer. I love using my kettle grill as a smoker, and having the thermometer built-in is really handy.   But the biggest improvement is the ash catcher. Having this bin is excellent and really helps keep the ashes tidy and easy to remove and dispose of. I always hated emptying ashes from the old flat plan because they would inevitably spill and blow all over the porch; the new system is super convenient and works perfectly. 

I 100% commend Webber for keeping this classic piece of home cooking, and making the slight improvements they have.  Our son is now 19, and I'm looking forward to the day I can gift him his first kettle grill once he settles down.

title: Olympic Champion Performance
text:
I distinctly remember the day I purchased my Weber Original Kettle 22’ grill.  It was July 19, 1996 the opening day of the Atlanta 1996 Summer Olympics.  I lived in the Atlanta area at the time and the day was one of high expectations and excitement for us residents.  I purchased the Weber for a cookout celebration with friends and family to watch the opening ceremonies.  To say my Weber grill ended up being an Olympic Champion would be an understatement!

This utilitarian but impressive grill has performed exceptionally for 26 ½ years and has NEVER let me down. For the first 20 years I used the grill at least once a week with many times being twice a week.  More recently as my children grew and we became empty nesters our use went down to about once a month.  I am amazed to calculate an estimate of the total number of meals I have cooked on my Weber.  Once a week for 20 years plus once a month for 5 ½ is over 1,100 total!!  I am proud to report my Weber has served me well for somewhere between 500 & 1,100 barbeques per my estimates.  I don't know the exact total of times I have used this Weber but stats like this are Olympian Champion level performance. 

There has been little maintenance required for this exceptional performance.  I have replaced the upper grill once or twice and the bolts securing the vents to the kettle needed to be removed and replaced.  The unit has always been protected from rain with a cover or a roof so rust was never an issue.  

Eventually I will need to replace this grill as I am now seeing some corrosion in the metal near the lower part of the kettle where the heat is most intense.  Last week I was strolling the grill aisle of my local Big Box home store where I saw other charcoal grills priced @ the entry level of $499 up to $1,800+.  I can only laugh knowing I may have paid $65 for my Original Kettle 22” in 1996 and can get another one today for only $139 that will likely outlast me and any remaining grilling days I have left on this earth!  Considering that I am Sold…

RJ the GrandMaster

The large circular knobs mimic the iconic Wolf ovens with their little chunks of cherry red strip. The propane gas tank has an intelligently placed hook that holds it in place on the side and also gives an indicator of how much gas is left.  The grills are very nice and thick imparting excellent grill marks onto the food. I've used this several times and never fail to walk away with succulent, delicious tasting food for the family!  A definite winner and no-brainer for a top notch gas BBQ that will inspire you to fire up the grill more often.  I also decided to purchase the pricey grill cover that was made for this model, it is very easy to throw over (once completely cooled down of course) and has simple and effective velcro fasteners on the side to cinch in within seconds.  Worth the price.
After recently owning a now bankrupt company's electric/charcoal fusion BBQ, I am more than pleased with this Weber and will always come back to this brand.

title: Recent switch to charcoal from gas
text:
I have used gas grills for a number of years but recently down-sized and got a charcoal kettle based on very high reviews from a number of sources. These are very initial, novice impressions and I am happy to be schooled.

I really wanted to love this product, but now I'm wondering if I should have paid a third as much and got some non-descript brand from Walmart. 

Two surprisingly mediocre features in an otherwise bullet-proof product:

First, the warming rack is awkward and its placement is indeterminate and it can actually slip through the grates. This should not happen. Either make it securable to the stable grilling platform or don't have it.

Second, the central "cut-away" in the grilling surface can actually fall through which is puzzling. Why have a portion of the cooking surface that can be nudged or jostled to fall on the charcoal below? 

Third and again, I am a novice with charcoal, but the design seems to require A LOT of briquettes to maintain high heat. I filled a chimney with briquettes to an inch from the top and got them volcano hot in ten minutes. But once I spread them they quickly burned through and the heat rapidly dropped. No idea how this design gets even close to 500 F but again, that may be my mistake with the venting (I kept the bottom and top vents fully open). Would greatly appreciate any tips that don't involve two whole chimneys of charcoal or a giant pyramid with a pint of lighter fluid.

Best regards.

title: Unlike a certain other "Q"... This Q is for REAL!
text:
Perfect grill for empty-nesters, young couples, and the like. Just the right size for dinners for two! Much more efficient with propane than firing up the big grill and faster & less fuss than breaking out the charcoal. The Q is now my #1 grill and all the others are relegated to "special events". The design of the Q is very well thought out and all of the accessories, such as the cart, the 20lb tank hose, and even the grill cover work seamlessly together - Like they were actually designed to work as a system!
And yet, you can quickly ditch all the extras, grab one of the little 1lb propane tanks you get from the hardware store, and head out with a light, self-contained, set-up that's perfect for a picnic at the beach or tailgating - the Q is versatile! 
I was concerned prior to purchasing the Q that it might not have enough BTUs to get that perfect sear. Absolutely NOT an issue! I'm not sure if it's the burner design, the burner spacing, or whatever magic Weber's come up with but it cooks like it's BTU rating is 5X greater than stated!
Simply put, the Weber Q is awesome! I only wish I'd gotten one sooner.

text: This Spirit II E-310 is my third weber grill.   My prior two weber grills were spirits also.  My first I had for 16 yrs and second fir 15 yrs.  I didn't wanted a good reliable grill but something that wouldn't break the bank.  The installation was somewhat confusing looking at the schematics of the manual.  I recommend downloading the app.  Once I did that,  it went together know problems.  I should mention after the grill was built, it is very sturdy.  Make sure when turning the gas on that the lid is open and all burners are in the off position.  Then turn the first burner on and push the igniter button.  If not done in this order,  the safety feature will slow gas flow and the grill will not heat up past 200 degrees.  I made this mistake and have not done since.   It is a good safety feature.  The grill heats up to 500 degrees pretty quick.  The porcelain grates are awesome to cook on and the grill heats evenly.  No hot spots   I grill out 3-4 times a week in the summer and fall and must say the grill is actually the best of the webers I've owned.   The ease of placing anything from meat to vegetables on the grill and shutting the lid and letting the grill do the work is quite fun.  The eveness of the cooking and flavors have been fantastic.  I would recommend this grill to anyone in the market for a nice looking, sturdy reliable grill.   Worth every penny.

text: This is my third Weber grill and my first Weber tabletop model.  I recently purchased the Q1200 to replace a different brand as my new RV grill. I BBQed on three separate nights: salmon, ribeye and chicken thighs.  The unit operated as it should.  There was a learning curve to place the meat on the grill at the correct temperature as not to have the burner flame up and burn the meat.  The grates are heavy and retain the heat so from my experience, reducing the flame to low doesn't immediately lower the cooking temp.  The grill preheated to 500 degrees at highest setting and I had to lower the setting after placing the meat on the grill.  On my third use only preheated to 375, no flame up.  The cooking grill is in two haves and is easy to clean in the sink after use.  I prefer to have a temp gauge on my BBQs, one of the reasons I selected this model.  I am planning on cooking a whole chicken as a friend recommended.  He stated it possible due to the dome style hood design.  The folding side tables are handy but for my use there not really needed.  Overall, I would recommend this grill to cook for 1 to 4 persons.

title: You need this!!
text:
As someone who never cooks, I was worried I'd spend all this money on the Q1200 and cart and use it once. (My previous grill was a monster that I used 3 times in 20 years.) But I love it and am using it several times a week. In fact, I just made a Portobello mushroom cap "burger" on a toasted bun for lunch!  

The Q1200's just a super, compact and convenient grill that takes up little space on my deck. It feels lighter than I expected -- most of the weight is in the grates. The flip-out shelves are an awesome convenience. The grill temperature easily climbs to it's maximum -- you have to keep an eye on it. The grilling surface is large enough to easily handle a large cut up chicken, and cooks quickly.  (I've had an easier time cooking chicken to juicy perfection on this Q1200 than I do when using an oven, especially the large split breasts.)  Depending on what you're cooking, you could easily feed 6-8 people with this grill -- probably even more. 

Even though the cooking surface is smaller than a regular size grill, it's comprised of two separate grates, which makes them easy to handle and transport as they're heavy. (I often just use one side which minimizes the number of grates I have to clean.)  Of course, the split surface also provides the option to switch out one side for a griddle plate. (I bought the plate, but have yet to try it.)  It's also notable that the grill grates are broad with less space in between, which means you can throw some fairly small things on there without food falling through.

I initially used the small 1lb propane bottles as I wasn't sure how much I'd grill (I otherwise NEVER cook); but I've been using the Q1200 so much that I transitioned to a regular propane tank. It was very easy to set it up with the adapter hose and the propane tank. Fortunately, I was aware that using a tank can trigger a safety mechanism that prevents the grill from fully heating. There are helpful instructions on the Weber website on how to prevent that so I've had no issues. 

The Q1200's been pretty easy to clean, but I'm diligent about cleaning after every use. Burning everything off with high heat, and then using a grill brush is a FALLACY though. The Weber Grill Grate cleaner helps quite a bit with degreasing and the removal of charred buts. I also spray on liquid detergent and let the grates sit in the sink a few minutes. Again, it's wonderful having compact grates when it comes to cleaning.

I highly recommend getting the rolling cart designed for the Q series. It's lightweight but sufficiently stable, and puts the grill at the perfect height. (However, I have not tried transporting the grill and cart anywhere to test their mobility.)

Seriously, I can't recommend this enough

title: Horrendous Customer Service
text:
I grew up with Weber, specifically their charcoal line.  After purchasing a home, I knew I wanted to make this investment and commit to something that I knew would last a long time.  I did plenty of research before landing on the Spirit II E-310.  As a novice cook, one of the reasons I wanted this specific grill was because of its compatibility with the iGrill3 thermometer.  It is advertised EVERYWHERE that it works with the badge on the Spirit II line.  After assembling the grill, I was hit with an addendum stating the right table NO LONGER came with the badge.  How in the world is it appropriate to still advertise it as compatible but not include it in the actual grill?  I have tried every method of contacting Weber for clarification.  Via email, I received one response and it was automatically generated and included the instructions for installing the thermometer (assuming the badge was still on the grill!!!).  Via phone, customer service had zero idea the grill was shipping without the badge so they had no suggestions other than to use the thermometer and just place it on the table.  

Cherry on top, I have owned this grill for a little over a week and now the warming grate is constantly falling off.  You can tell it was produced with very little room for error and the slightest movement of the grill or high temp will cause it to fall off.  

As someone who grew up with this brand and trusted it with my first home grill, I will not be coming back.  I expected much more from Weber.

It was clearly engineered and built with the same attention to detail as its larger brethren. The drip pan and the drip tray are well designed to make everyday cleanup a cinch. Weber flavorizer bars are the standard for gas grilling with a minimum of flare ups. The stainless steel side tables are generously sized and can keep plates, thermometer and utensils close at hand. 

The only problem I’ve run into so far has been a raccoon who went in through the open back of the cabinet and managed to make a mess, absconding with the foil drip pan and its evidently tasty (to it) drippings. Removing the drip pan after cool down and storing it on top of the grates in between uses has since stymied the raccoon.

text: I have quite a lot of smokers and grills, so I believe I know about grills. Overall the grill itself works flawlessly. However, I think Weber should/could improve it without adding much in the way of costs. First, kudos to Weber for adding extra hardware because I needed it. Was short 2 screws. Only had one extra which I needed, the other I figured out a way to not need/use it. The grill gets hot quickly, but also does a great job of staying at 300-350 indirect heat too. Things Weber should improve: folding shelves. Making the shelves foldable would add probably all of 50 cents more to manufacture but would be a huge benefit. On my back patio I have a Workhorse Pits, a TMG smoker, Assassin cabinet smoker, Lone Star Grillz smoker, an Assassin charcoal grill, OK Joe Bronco, Blackstone griddle, Halo Pizza Oven, and an outdoor fryer, so moving things around to get this to fit was a challenge. Next issue is the igniter. This grill uses only one igniter on the left burner and the other burners light off of that burner. So if you want the middle burner on, you have to turn the left and middle burner on then turn the left burner off instead of just adding an igniter on all 3 burners. The last thing I’d like to see Weber add is a sacrificial piece of metal on the hood similar to the genesis. This grill does get hot and having that piece of metal would help maintain the enamel on the herd better. Otherwise, I could see the heat potentially affecting the enamel. Other than that, I’m glad to see Weber offer a more affordable grill than the Genesis or Summit but still make it feel premium when compared to most other brands. However, for the price, those 3 changes should be included.  Knowing that before purchasing, I still thought that this was the best grill for my needs. I would buy again.

title: These have always been great grills

Steaks BBQ'ed over charcoal always tastes better than "grilling them" over gas. It does take more time to prepare to cook but it's well worth the extra effort.
Use a charcoal chimney to light the charcoal as "Match Light" briquets will put "taste" in what you are cooking. If you want to take BBQing seriously as I do and be a purist use lump charcoal in lieu of briquets because briquets have additives in them to make their shape and hold together. Briquets burn longer and leave more ash while lump charcoal is pure, leaves less ash and burns hotter which is great for searing steaks. You may want to use briquets for a long cook. I keep both on hand!

title: The Ultimate Grilling Experience
text:
I recently purchased the Master-Touch Charcoal Grill 22" and I can confidently say that it has elevated my grilling game to new heights. This grill is a true gem, and I cannot recommend it highly enough for any grilling enthusiast.

First and foremost, the build quality of this grill is outstanding. The materials used are top-notch, ensuring durability and long-lasting performance. The grill is solidly constructed and exudes a sense of sturdiness. The attention to detail in its design is impressive, from the seamless assembly to the smooth operation of its components.

One of the standout features of the Master-Touch Charcoal Grill is its innovative One-Touch cleaning system. This mechanism allows for effortless ash removal, eliminating the need for messy and time-consuming cleanups. It's incredibly convenient and ensures that you spend more time enjoying your delicious food rather than worrying about maintenance.

The cooking experience on this grill is unparalleled. The 22" cooking grate provides ample space to cook for a large gathering of family and friends. The built-in lid thermometer is an excellent addition, ensuring accurate temperature monitoring without the need for guesswork.

Another feature I appreciate is the hinged cooking grate. It makes adding more charcoal during longer cooking sessions a breeze, eliminating the need to lift the entire grate and disrupt the cooking process. Additionally, the built-in lid holder is a thoughtful touch, providing a convenient place to rest the lid when checking or flipping your food.

Finally, the aesthetics of this grill are simply stunning. It boasts a sleek and timeless design that is sure to impress any guest. The variety of colour options allows you to choose one that matches your style and adds a touch of elegance to your outdoor cooking space.

text:
Let me start off with saying I’ve had other kettle grills other than Webers. Each one the paint would come off after several cooks. Grates would rust extremely fast. These were comparably priced and sized to the Weber.

 Now onto the good stuff! Webers grill grates are top notch quality. The ability to open the grates to add charcoal when cooking is a game changer. Kettle top holder feature is essential and could not do without it after using. This feature also makes cooking a lot of fun between searing to moving the cooked items to a cooler spot and tenting for internal temps to be reached.

Compared to my other kettles the temperature is more stable and easier to manage. If you never kettle grilled there’s lots of videos on YouTube that will get you into the groove of things. There’s a learning curve but it’s a-lot of fun progressing. Once you get it you will be cooking for the masses with lots of smiles. Charcoal is king and you will find out why, flavour town!

Very pleased to write this review and hope this encourages more people jump on the Weber kettle craze. There’s a reason it’s been around for years!

Oh almost forgot, get a charcoal chimney. This one product is a must for quick even charcoal lighting. 

As you advance check out Tuffy Stone and really let your taste buds explode with a Weber grill.

text: Bought the 22in Weber kettle since i needed a grill. I went back and forth on getting this or a barrel grill, even tossed around the idea of getting one of the dual grills with propane and charcoal from a different brand. Ultimately went with the kettle as i have had the dual, propane, and other versions of charcoal grills (barrel). I never had any complaints with the last weber kettle i had (still kicking myself for selling it the last time i moved). Might have been feeling a little nostalgic as my dad was in town and he taught me how to grill on a weber kettle when i was 9. The real driving force behind getting a grill at all was my son wanting his 8th grade promotion party to be a BBQ at the park with friends and family. He requested flanken style ribs, his favorite, among other things like burgers, hotdogs, carne asada etc.. the memories of family gathering and listening to the older men in the family tell stories while grilling and shouting for me to cover my ears when they thought i was to young to hear something they had to say came back. It was a great time, surrounded by friends and family telling stories and now being one of the older men telling kids to cover their ears as they watched me do my thing on the grill. Hahaha.. oh how time flies. I don't know for sure, but i think the kettles now hold heat a little better than the last one i had. Simple to use and a great grill to teach basics of grilling to your children (as previously stated, my dad showed me on a weber kettle back in the 90s and i taught 4 of my 5 kids on my last kettle.. the baby of the family will learn on this one). For sure the ash catcher is a great improvement over the old saucer pan thing i had on my last one. The hinged grill grate are pretty clutch too. The color of the grill is awesome too. I wanted a red one (thats what my dad had, and like i said.. i was probably feeling a bit nostalgic since he was in town..) but i saw the copper and since it was in stock and nobody near me had a red one i grabbed it, and i am glad i did.

title: New Weber E-210 Grill
text:
This grill was purchase to replace a 3.5 yr. old Weber gill that was toppled over on its front side by a sudden wind microburst, damaging  (bending) the shafts on the two burner controls.  While I could find no gas leaks, I was not comfortable with igniting it, and concluded I should by a new grill.  The new grill is more expensive model, and it has additional features that are mostly improvements    The two folding shelves work better than the single folding shelf on the old unit.  The new unit has four casters which improve its mobiity.  The new unit mounts the gas bottle on the inside, but lifting and positioning a full bottle to get it onto the hanger hook is very difficult.  I found that using a18" length of a 2x2 piece of wood helped, but I found no suggestions in the user manul to guide me.

Starting and cooking on the new grill is a pleasure, although the old grill was comparable.  On the negative side, the grill arrived with three damaged parts, two of which were bad enough to make their use impossible.  Weber did respond to my phone call by shipping replacement parts promptly.  The third part was bent slightly at the top, but it was still usable with no functional effect.  The shipping carton was in perfect condition, and the damage could not have happened in transit.  Some Chinese employee simply chose to pack obviously damaged parts in the carton.  I have observed over recent years that quality control and Chinese manufacturing can be an oxymoron.

title: *Almost* a perfect grill! 4/5
text:
Pros:
I love it! It's helped me fall in love with grilling again. Everything is straight forward to use and there is no shortage of info online to get you started. My food has come out better than ever!

Cons:
The legs attach via buttons you press in and then stick the leg in place and the button pops out and locks the leg. This is nice for quick disassembly if that is what your looking for but I would prefer if the legs bolted on.

Knit picks:
The grill rolls over EXTREMELY easy when moving it while fully assembled. To move this grill you grab the handle on the front, lift up, and roll your grill where you need it to go.

The back wheels act as a pivot point so if you lift the front leg off the ground more than an inch or two it rolls forward and falls over backward. So be careful of that!

Second knit pick is the legs are just thin aluminum. This isn't the most expensive grill, and the legs are no doubt strong enough to get the job done, but this isn't a cheap grill either, and it is a major name brand. I expected a little more out of the legs build quality and attachment style.

I highly recommend a using a wood grill scraper to remove any loose food on the grilling grates while cooking and a nylon grilling brush to clean the grilling grates once the grill cools down. Apply or spray a thin layer of cooking spray (olive oil) on the grilling grates after each time you cook to preserve the cooking grates and the keep the food from sticking on the grates. Also keep the grill covered to prolong the life of the grill.

I highly recommend this affordable Spirit grill!

title: to expensive for the quality, you pay for the name
text:
You pay for the name and the accessory world around it.
The quality of some parts is so ridiculously cheap that they should be embarrassed. The wheel caps, the screws to mount the lid handle, the plastic feet. This thing is so cost optimized that it screams cheap China product. The important parts like the grates and the kettle itself seem ok, otherwise they would get in trouble in the long run.
You also pay for its proven design, so yes, it works well, it's thought out well and you get phone customer service probably on every continent. 
But looking at the materials and build of this vs. a charcoal gravity feeder seen at your home retailer, the difference is absolutely shocking: I would guess nearly all of what you pay goes into Webers profit margin, and almost nothing into the material and build quality. For the other one with heavy cast iron grates, lot of materials, electronics, just the sheer weight, how the handles and lid feel, it's hard to believe they can make much profit for the offered price. 
It's good if a good company makes a good product for a good profit.

title: mediocre waste of money
text: If this is the standard for propane grills in 2023, I feel ripped off.  This grill is a WEAK, literally low-energy time waster.  If your gig is firing up some hot dogs and hamburgers [not too thick], you're good to go.  Not sure if you can toast the rolls, not enough heat.  I'm flabbergasted how this passes for a outdoor grill.  The heat source is too far away from the cooking surface, the "flavorizer bars"  are like a heat sheild.  Why would you cover the flame so thoroughly?  I have read and re-read the troubleshooting guides thinking I had tripped the safety mechanism.  Is 20 times too many to make sure?  I replaced the regulator, I have tried multiple propane sources.  And yet this grill is no match for my Air Fryer in term of performance.  Nothing like grilling a whole chicken for 90 minutes @ 400F and it comes out under cooked and soggy.  Good luck trying to sear something on this low energy dud of a grill.  Perhaps I have much higher expectations than most folk.  I want  a grill that is so robust that you have to tame the flame, not hope you can get your meal cooked.  Now I'm stuck with this monolith of mediocre engineering lurking on my deck and I hate it.

The issue was that the grill without the propane tank installed is top heavy and blew over in a strong wind when the grill was less than a week old. So I caution anyone to not set up the grill without installing the propane tank. The control panel was broken as a result of the fall and Weber grave me a credit after I replaced the control panel, which is above and beyond what was covered in the warranty. text: I think the grill components are good quality. That said I have some complaints.  Weber doesn’t offer you an easy way to move the grill. It has wheels but the only way to move it is to lift up a flimsy folding table on one end of the grill. Unless you grab it by the very end of that table and lift upward, putting pressure on the hinges, it will pop out of the pins and be a wobbly mess. I could see even getting injured because of this. I also do not find the porcelain grills to be very nonstick, and they stain very easily. The gas system design I also feel is lacking, because my old grill didn’t care which burner I turned on first, but this one you have to turn on the far left one first and light that, and then you can turn on the ones to the right of it. If you don’t know this, and try to light one of the other two first by mistake, you can have a dangerous buildup of gas which could explode when you light it.

title: 90s Throwback
text: The Weber Spirit E-310 reminds me of the 90s Weber Genesis in every positive way possible. It's a grill that inspires confidence in those less serious about grilling, but still provides the functionality demanded by a seasoned Pro. It's incredibly simple to use, clean, and maintain just like the Genesis of the 90s. The Spirit E-310 is also the perfect size; it offers great cooking real-estate and enough room to establish cooking zones, without being massive and heavy. If you need to move it, with no tank and the side tray folded it's a one-person-carry. While there are several more highly optioned variations of this generation Spirit, you can't go wrong with this one; it's the perfect grill to just go out, and cook. My only wish is that there were more fun color options like the 90s Genesis models (I know there are some but they're not readily available). I grew up helping my Dad grill on a Genesis 1000 that was a beautiful burnt orange color and would've loved something like that. @Weber maybe add paint to sample to the "build your own Weber" page? Actually, that's a positive thing because the meat doesn't get charred as easily as my other grill (although my husband likes it that way). I like that you can easily remove the tray under the burners to clean it.

title: Good for cooking, but plagued by poor quality.
text:
It cooks perfectly fine, but the build quality of this grill is abysmally low. In only a summer of ownership, I had the main drag handle fail on one side due to a poor weld. I contacted their support team about this and then a game was played where the support member I was speaking to tried to deny my warranty because the handle broke when I was moving it. I had to defend myself in an email and argue this was a manufacturing defect and after that I was given a replacement bowl.

The piece that failed was the spot weld where the main handle connects to the bowl. The paint flaked from normal cooking heat cycles and exposed the small spot weld to rust apart. 

I also discovered during the replacement of my bowl (my wife built this for me originally) the top bowl handle does not bolt and nut together, causing looseness that can't be repaired. It's a 1/4-20 thread with a stamped piece of metal meant to act like a nut pushed down into the threads. 1/4-20 nuts are so cheap it's ridiculous.

Overall my experience with this grill was great until I had a problem, now when I think of Weber I think of an American grill company that sold out and cheapened their product.

title: Turned me into a proper suburban dad
text:
I'm 67 years old and have never grilled anything besides hot dogs and hamburgers on a variety of big box store grills. Grilling was just a necessary chore so we could eat. Then my wife got me this gem.  
All of a sudden I WANT to grill. I've made several steaks (for the first time in my life) that came out perfect. She also got me Weber's Greatest Hits and Weber's Smoke cookbooks and frankly, I had no idea I could actually cook. I use the Weber chimney to get the coals started, and once I drop them the vents do a great job controlling the temperature. Keeping it clean is simple too, especially getting rid of the ashes.  
Whether you're a novice or a veteran griller, I guarantee you will be happy with this grill.

My only slightly negative comment about the Weber is the inability to get a good sear on some meats. text: I originally bought a cheaper portable propane grill, but it never got hot enough, it would dry out my meat and not sear it. After a ton of wasted food and frustration, I finally decided to splurge and buy the Weber Q1200.  It heats up fast and gives my food a perfect sear.  It makes grilling so easy!  I was nervous about the Q1200 not being big enough for our family of 5, but it’s perfect and fits nicely in our camper. (I originally ordered the Q2000 but it was way too big to transport so I sent it back and got the Q1200). text: I give this item a three star rating for a number of reasons.  First, I think three stars indicates that it meets my expectations and it does. While putting the grill together, I ran into a problem with step 4 in the manual.  I could not get the back panel holes to match up with the two side panels.  I called Weber.  The gentleman on the other end of the phone had a copy of the manual available to him and described the parts in the step as a "back panel, four screws, and four cylindrical disks".  Having some knowledge of terminology, I told him that the cylindrical disks were probably called "washers".  I feel that a person in a technical support position should know the term washers.  He ordered me a new back panel.  Two days later, while reorienting the parts left to install, I discovered that I was trying to install the back panel on the front of the grill and the back panel that was being shipped was not going to help. This was my mistake.   As I have accounts with both Fedex and UPS, I knew that back panel hadn't shipped so I called to cancel the shipping of the useless back panel.  I was told that this could not be done but if I called after receiving the back panel they would generate a return document and would pay for shipping.  I advised that if the back panel came, I would discard it rather than having to go to the trouble of returning an item that Weber knew wasn't wanted by the customer.  I was told that nothing could be done, but two days later, I received an Email stating that my shipment had been cancelled.  This points me to the conclusion that Weber customer service is less than adequate.

title: Good, but not like the old days.
text:
This is my fifth weber since 1984. I have owned a full-sized kettle, a Smokey Joe, a 2004 propane 2-burner, open cart Spirit (which I just replaced with the E-310). and a charcoal 22" Weber perform cart/kettle. What I can say about those four is that they were rock-solid. Nineteen years for the Spirit with only one failure - the igniter which went almost immediately. I replaced the cast iron grates and flavorizer bars once in those 19 years. No rust on the cooking box or lid; minor surface rust on a few areas on the legs. A spray paint with Rustoleum every three years and it looks new. It cooked very well right up until the last night I used it. I wish I could get the exact replacement.

The new E-310. 
Well maybe if I had never owned the 2004 Spirit I would be more satisfied. If I had to use one word to capture the difference in the two, it would be flimsy. 

The old unit was an indestructible beast. On the E-310 the thickness and weight of the cooking box and lid is a fraction of what it was. The grates and flavorizer bars are thinner and lighter. The burners and burner connecters are lightweight and move!  All the parts under the grates shake and rattle during normal cooking procedures. The stainless-steel side burners aren't completely stable (and they are not fold-downs). My neighbor next door has the cart version of the 310 and one of his side tables is permanently bent down. My previous Spirit side table was a composite material with a fold-up extension. Rock soild; you could pick up the grill holding onto it without a wobble. I wouldn't dare try that with the E-310.

And I don't get the fascination with stainless steel. It is thin and difficult to maintain in the long-term. I've had the unit for six weeks and there are already discolorations - and I use stainless steel cleaner wipes.

The metal base cabinet is lightweight.  Minimal force can bend the door. The magnet is not powerful enough to properly seal the doorWhere the supports meet the base, water tends to accumulate - a breeding ground for rust.

Now' after the first three uses they were fully seasoned - perfectly well. Steaks and burger have cooked very well. The burners spring to life using the igniter and spread instantly when burners 2 and 3 are activated. This is far superior than my previous Spirit. The unit reaches full heat very rapidly and cooks very well with just two burners if that is all the area I need. 

So, I can honestly say it is working fine. And frankly, I had read reviews that shared my concerns but I considered it the best of what is currently available. I'm just wondering what cutbacks in materials will mean in the long term.

Would I buy this model again compared to other brands in the same category? Probably would.

title: Fancy, Stylish, Portable, Compact
text:
This is a nice grill design for items that you will watch closely.  It is an attractive unit.  Its single burner design doesn't allow for a cooler place on the grill to get indirect heating.  Setting the heat only sets the rate of heating, not the temperature.  This makes it imperative that you periodically raise the lid to regulate the temperature for items that are thicker.  Flare ups are common as the lid is vented on both sides and the grease hole in the bottom is large.  This is an open single burner and heats up very quickly.   So, it takes some time to get used to this grill.  Once you understand how this grill cooks you can adapt your cooking method to achieve very good results.  
The grill is relatively easy to clean, but the grease on the bottom of the bowl can build up and periodic cleaning is essential.  
So far, we are satisfied with our purchase as it is small enough to be portable in our camping trailer and eliminates the need and mess of charcoal.  It produces a lot of heat and the squirrels can't get into it with the lid closed.  For our purposes it is acceptable but it would not replace a larger multi-burner unit temperature controlled unit for general outside grilling use.

Overall I think getting the original 22 inch is definitely more worth it than the master touch. For almost 300 dollars the quality wasn't really up to my expectations and the original is about half the price and can do what the master touch can do. If you grill everyday or something I guess this would be worth it for the ash catcher, char basket, and increased height but if you're a beginner or don't grill that much I would definitely recommend getting the original. Honestly the dome thermometer also is something I don't really look at so save the money and use it to buy an actual accurate thermometer for the ambient temp.

text:

I gotta tell you, the 22" Master touch is a gorgeous grill.  I purchased the additional rotisserie attachment and we enjoyed one of the best prime rib roasts we've ever had on Christmas day.  Can't wait to rotisserie some chickens on that.

text:
This is the third or forth Weber I  have owned. This one is obviously the result of trying to cheapen the product through foreign manufacturing. One-they have gone to one handle not two. This provides less places to hang BBQ utensils. It also makes it difficult to move if it has been recently used and is hot. Two-the lid is not as tough as in the past. My new lid slide off the back, landed in the grass and has deformed so I have to push it aggressively for it to seat to the base. (My old one hit the grass numerous times with no issues.) Three-the coating they are using is also cheaper. Where the one handle is tack welded onto the base it is rusting after two months (I got it for Christmas) My old grill is still in the edge of the yard and after nine years there is no rust at either of the two handles. Lastly-On my previous grill I could put the lid on and leave a crescent moon opening by leaving the lid ajar-it provided for another option for heat retention. This unit, if you try that the lid slides off-therefore hitting the grass and deforming the lid. It is also obvious that they are trying to hide the country of manufacture-the aluminium shield at the adjustable vent says"engineered in Palatine, IL" not manufactured in the USA. 
It is a sad epitaph to a once superior company and product.

I also bought the hose that lets me connect the unit to a 25lb tank as I have found that it gets very expensive to use 1lb bottles.   However, I found that it gets way to hot on even the lowest setting wrecking very good EXPENSIVE meat.   To check to make sure I was right I bought two 1lb bottles which worked great.   I have checked many stores to try to find an adjustable regulator to knock the pressure down but unable to find one with the correct threads.   I also checked the Weber site and could not find one.   Disappointing problem with and otherwise great product.  I have a Silver Weber at home that is over 25 years old and recommend it to all my friends but would not recommend the 1200Q  (we use it in our RV for 6 mths a year) because of the above issue.

title: PERFECT for two, EASY and FUN!
text:
When my husband went on the carnivore diet it became "too much" to clean up the stove of meat grease every meal and he suggested getting a grill.  I was intimidated by the thought of grilling every day (I'd never grilled before in my life at 52, LOL!), but the thought of a continuously clean kitchen encouraged me...and I'm SO HAPPY WE GOT IT!!!  

It's SUPER EASY to use, the perfect size for 6 1/3 lb burgers (although I usually cook 3 at a time). I LOVE the built in grill thermometer.  It helps a lot since just timing it doesn't account for ambient temperature and that does affect pre-heat and grilling times; it's winter in New England so whether it's 25 or 40 degrees outside makes a difference.

I recommend a stainless steel "fish turner" type of flipper; it's perfect for getting between the grill and the charred goodness of the burger so half of it isn't stuck.  Of course, having the grill hot enough and leaving it long enough before turning is essential, but the beveled edge of the fish spatula along with its thinness makes it almost a given that you're going to get all the yummy browned part on your plate.  Not that that's a review of the grill, just a tip.

title: Excellent grill

title: Terrible experience: buy at Home Depot!
text:
I love Weber Grills, and have owned several. I decided to replace my aging Weber propane grill with a new one and decided to buy it through Weber.com.

Big mistake. I knew I would have to put it together, so when I received it, I opened the box and the second part I took from the box was broken. There are dozens of parts, so at this point I decided I made an error by ordering from Weber.com, and called them to pick up my damaged product.

The first call ended with the CS rep saying he needed to 'escalate' my call because I wasn't willing to unpack the entire box and check if other parts were damaged. Escalation meant I would receive a call or email within 24 hours.

Seventy-two hours later I called and talked to a different CS rep who told me the first rep didn't escalate my request correctly, but now he was correcting it, and expect a call or email within 24 hours.

Ten days lately... nothing.

I have now initiated a complaint with PayPal. I am also on the phone with Weber right now, on hold, waiting for a supervisor.

Just buy it assembled at Home Depot

title: Best Grill Ever!

1. Love the easy access to the tank

title: What a Difference $200 Makes!
text:
We got the Weber Spirit E-210 Gas Grill several weeks ago and have used it extensively for grilling bratwurst, steaks, hamburgers, corn, vegetables, barbecued ribs--you name it. It has met our expectations in every respect. My impressions as follows:

THE GOOD

The grill is solidly built. The title of this review ($200) refers to a gas grill of a different make but similar size purchased by my daughter awhile back. She paid about $200 less for hers than we paid for ours, but the difference in build quality is huge! Hers, while it functions well, is primarily thin sheet metal construction. The Spirit E-210 is solid. I estimate that it is at least twice as heavy as hers and is obviously built to last. This holds true for cooking and burner surfaces as well: solidly made and heavy. Oh--just a quick mention. I spent half a day assembling my daughter's grill. We purchased ours already assembled--AND Ace Hardware helped us load it. 

It is compact. One of the criteria for us (retired couple living in Florida) was a grill small enough to be accommodated in a limited space. The Spirit E-210 has inside propane tank storage and side table flaps that fold down for storage. When not in use it occupies a space just a little over 2' x 2' x 3.5' tall, fitting nicely into a corner of our lanai.

It heats fast and evenly--no apparent "cool" areas once it was heated and ready to cook. It was amazing to watch the temp. gauge rise once we turned it on with both burners on high: the needle was close to the 600 degree mark in just a few minutes. The solid build of the unit, especially the cover which sits solidly on the frame, helps keep heat in instead of radiating a lot of it away. Additionally the burners are responsive: it can cook "low and slow" for ribs, or hot enough to produce a medium NY Strip Steak in less than 9 minutes. The indirect heat is nice as well. Though it gets very hot, no flame ever contacts the food (though grease flares will happen).

THE BAD

Well, maybe "The Not Quite Up To Expectations" would be a better title for this section, because there is nothing really bad about this unit. But...

The casters, while totally functional, seem a bit small for the unit. It is a heavy unit and casters possibly a bit bigger would be a big help rolling it over uneven surfaces, or in and out of our lanai. We have to lift up the end being rolled over the threshold--a minor annoyance, but still there. 

Another condition larger casters would help alleviate is that the wheel brakes on the unit (each front caster has a toe brake which can be set so the unit doesn't roll accidentally), can only be set with the front wheels at near 90 degrees to the unit. If not, the brake lever cannot be reached with a toe and we have to reach under the unit to adjust the wheel to the correct position. 

The warming rack, while perfectly usable, is a bit small. Maybe 6" wider would increase its functionality.

The gas bottle rides on a clip inside the unit that also functions as a measuring device to tell you how much gas is left. I've never used (or even seen) one of those before so I am just a little nervous about it...like a solution for which there is no problem. But hey! Maybe it is great. Time will tell.

THE UGLY

There ain't no ugly!

THE BOTTOM LINE

Frankly, so far this grill has exceeded our expectations...and we expected a lot! Obviously we cannot assess its longevity at this point but the good design and heavy build quality leaves little room for doubt that it will shine in that area as well. I'd certainly recommend it.

text:

title: Defective propane regulator gasket.
text: The propane regulator gasket for my grill has cracked after less than 1 year of use and is leaking propane and posing a severe safety/fire hazard. When I contact the warranty department, they keep asking for documentation which I have already uploaded. This is a dangerous product and Weber is failing to address my concerns. They have outsourced their customer service and it takes 24 hours to get a response between messages. I would love to be able to use my grill but can't. A simple gasket which should cost 50 cents requires replacement of a $75 part.

title: Great kettle!
text: The kettle is an excellent cooker and with a few added accessories it is possible to do a fine job of cooking most anything. I would highly recommend the charcoal baskets which can be used in many different configurations to achive separate cooking zones and effectively manage charcoal burn. The vents and ash catcher work very well, but removing the ash dump pan is a bit finicky. The only real ding I would mention is the wheels and legs are pretty cheesy for a premium cooker.  I replaced mine with a nice aftermarket cart with a table top and shelf plus a lid holder. I really appreciate Weber quality. I'be got a Weber Spirit gas grill that I've been cooking on for 10 years. With a once a year pressure washing it is still working  fine. I expect the same performance from the Kettle.

The cabinet and wheels are also nicer - the only challenge I have experienced in the placement of the LP tank inside the cabinet with it very difficult to place the tank.

text:
This is our second Weber grill. The first lasted 19 years with some parts being replaced.

You're supposed to be able to hang the grate on the side of the grill, but the center piece always falls out! I've also had to retrieve the fallen center piece from hot coals a few times, because it fits so precariously on the main grate. I ended up buying a ($40 Weber) replacement grate without the center piece just to save my sanity. The lid holder and the coal dividers for indirect grilling are great, though. The wheels are also a big upgrade. I hope it lasts another 9 years, I expect it will!

title: GOOD LOOKS, GREAT HEAT CONTROL & FRIENDLY DESIGN
text:
So far, I really like my Spirit II E-210 LP Gas grill. I’ve followed manual suggestion to allow for a 10-min preheating with gas set on max gas flow. This has worked great as temperature is sufficiently high for a great sear on steaks, burgers, etc. 

From a design standpoint, I love the lack of sharp edges or corners on the side shelves. Most grills I’ve owned had sharply squared off edges. These present almost guaranteed spots to rip grill covers, especially during winter seasons where the cold weather tends to make grill covers less flexible, and therefore prone to tears. The Spirit II has rounded, smooth plastic corners which should go a long way to prevent tears. 

I have a feeling that I’m going to get a lot of excellent use from this grill for a very long time.

title: A Great Entry to the Weber Grill Ecosystem
text:
I purchased this grill for myself as a birthday present (after a little gas-or-pellet grill debating) and I'm certainly glad I did. Easily the most even cooking grill I've ever owned. Heats up quickly to any temp I've needed so far and everything has been flavorful and beautiful (great sear marks!) 

It took me a little over an hour to assemble after taking 30 minutes or so to just lay out all the pieces. It's a sturdy unit and, even though there were numerous steps to the assembly process, it went together easily. I can say two people working together should be able to knock this out in 45 minutes or so. I also appreciate the way the packaging was done, very tidy, no dings or dents to any of the parts.

I'm a bit of a no bells and whistles guy when it comes to grilling, so even though the Genesis grills were a bit of a temptation, nobody should hesitate for a minute in purchasing the E-310. Those who are looking at the Spirit E-310 and the Spirit II E-310, just bear in mind a couple of things. The Spirit II (this grill) uses the G4 grilling system (grease pan in the middle, not offset to one side) and the Spirit II is the one that is OPEN underneath. Aesthetically for me, I like the more rugged looks of the Spirit II version of the E-310 but either grill should be fine. But, if you're like me and you need a reliable, easy-to-use gas grill (LP for me) for burgers, brats, chicken, steak, etc., I can say without a doubt the Spirit II E-310 will be a great choice!

title: Nothing rewards like quality
text:
I had purchased an Oklahoma Joe Tahoma 900, thinking it would get hot enough to be able to do both my grilling and smoking. And it can, but it is not really designed for that, and you go through a ton of charcoal to get it up to 500 degrees.

I had a weber spirit 3 burner before that I used lovingly for 10 years, but eventually it just was getting too hard to keep up and there was some rust, etc... 

Sooooo... I did a week's worth of research on getting a cheap gas grill for my weekday grilling (I grill something 3 or 4 nights a week) that is simple. Light it, wait until its hot and grill it.
I went to multiple stores (Lowes, Home Depot, Menards, Ace Hardware) and checked out the 'cheap' ones, and lets just say you get what you pay for. Some were okay, but I could tell they would be falling apart in a couple years. 

So, my recommendation is pay up for the quality. The weber E-210 is almost the perfect small deck/patio grill. Assembly was a little hard for my 60 year-old knees, but wasn't particularly hard (note: put something down underneath on a deck... I lost 2 screws that fell through the deck and had to go to the hardware store to replace). It lit and fired up the first time. I already have a Bluetooth remote meat probe, so no need to pay extra for the built in ones. 

Also, I liked that the propane tank hangs on the side with easy access. With my old Weber, it had a cabinet underneath (that was useless and just collected dirt and grime) and bending over with a heavy propane tank  and hanging it inside the cabinet was a pain. 

Two burners is more than enough for a family of 4 and you can be eating at the table in same time it takes to pre-heat a pellet grill or charcoal. Trust me... I've used them all.

title: Huge Step Up From A Portable Gas Grill
text:
I went 10-years without a full-sized propane grill after moving.  We started camping not long after the move, so I used my portable camping grill (from another brand) both at home and while camping.  Two years ago we bought a vacation property and got a Spirit II E-210 to use there.  It was a great choice because of the extra space, two burners, and moving away from 1-lb propane cannisters.  Heat is consistent and adjustable.  I also appreciate the larger wheels for moving the grill and the ability to fold down the left side table. The spring actuated propane gauge has worked well enough to keep me from running out while grilling.

This year we decided to upgrade our home grilling abilities and I looked to Weber again.  I considered the Spirit EX-315 at a membership store, but ruled it out because of the electronic temperature gauge and small wheels.  After ruling out that bigger model, it made sense to get the same Spirit II E210 as we have at our other place. It will be easy to switch back and forth between operating the two grills.

I'm giving this grill only 3-stars, and here's why.  First, almost all of the best in-grill accessories from Weber are made for the 300-series grills and above.  Second, two burners are not ideal for indirect cooking.  Third, Weber took out the iGrill feature to save money but didn't spend the money to print a 200-series user manual that doesn't reference this feature.  Fourth, this new grill runs at least 100-degrees hotter than our original grill of the same model.   And finally, the influence Weber has over the sales channels can create a poor purchasing experience.  I had multiple options and went with a locally owned franchise hardware store who a) assembled the fuel gauge wrong, and b) were very reluctant to address a pricing promotion that started very shortly after my purchase.

text:
I love these little bbq's! This is my 3rd one. My first one was the white lid one but when I moved in 2020 getting a moving truck was difficult so had to make choices on what I moved, unforntionaly the BBQ didn't make the move. When I got settled I ordered the red one, but last winter it got attacked by mice. I had to throw it away. This time I ordered the green one since the green matched some of my outdoor furniture. So here is the "but" It was delivered March 7 but because of the snow I didn't put it together. Finally end of April I put it together. The problem was the flame was not adjustable and I couldn't get any heat out of it to cook. It was well past Amazon return window so I called Weber and the very first person I talked with was very nice person and he walked me through some steps and then told me he would send a free regulator and it would take up to two weeks to receive it. I received a fuel hose in stead of the regulator.I called Weber back and the person that I talked with again was very nice person and he said he would send me the regulator but again that would take up to 2 weeks. I received the regulator but you need a special tool to get the regulator off, finally got one at home depot. So between the fixed ratchet and the very short screw driver I still cannot get the regulator off!! I asked a handyman for help and he was going to charge me $100. 
I am a widowed 71yo women on a fixed income and cannot afford to buy a new bbq this year. I am in tears this will be the first time in over 35 years that I won't have a bbq.

title: Great little grill
text:
We are an older couple who enjoy grilling in the warm months.  Because it’s just the two of us we have no need for a traditional large multi-burner grill.  I found the Q1200 on your website and thought it would be perfect so I ordered it.  It has turned out to be a great little grill.  Easy to control heat levels and enough grill space for a couple salmon fillets and a tray of vegetables!  Actually, we had our kids and their families over the other night and was able to grill all the burgers and hotdogs at once.  There were 10 of us in total, so this little grill really earned its keep.

If you are looking for a small easily moved and cleaned grill I highly recommend the Q series grills.  I believe they come in 3 sizes, a bunch of fun colors and are great easy to store.

I'm sure it's just fine if it's on a pallet with a dozen other grills, but the rim of the lid rests way too close to the perimeter/edge of the box.  All it takes is one mishandled drop of the box by a delivery person, and the lid is very easily damaged.  And I am not suggesting adding Styrofoam to protect the lid; rather, the packaging should be redesigned so that the cardboard is more than sufficient. title: The OG of Kettle Grills
text:
A Weber kettle was my first charcoal grill (talking early ‘80s), and it was a solid cooking partner for many years until I finally replaced it with a Brinkman. After some 25 years on that grill, I “upgraded” to a Char Griller offset smoker. Big mistake, as it wasn’t able to a) handle the heat from a wood fire and b) was frustrating to use as a direct charcoal grill due to the decreased distance between the fire and the food. By then, Brinkman was no mas, and I was stuck.

Ultimately it was decided that the smoking was going to happen on a Yoder pellet grill, and the food that really shines when cooked over charcoal was gonna happen on a new Weber.

Gotta hand it to Weber, they didn’t mess too much with what was already working. I appreciate the heat shield underneath the handle on the lid, and the temperature gauge is also a welcome addition. Get the Premium though, so you’ll have that handy ash clean out. It’s a safety issue really, since it helps prevent hot ashes/tiny bits of glowing coal from blowing around. Easy to disengage and empty, and you’ll only have to do that every 3 cooks or so.

The lid still sits nice and snug on the kettle’s bottom, so you can close things up when you’re done and the fire suffocates quickly (very handy for conserving charcoal). I also love the two hinged sections of the cooking grate, so you can add more fuel without having to lift the grate/food out of the way.

If I could change one thing, it would be the orientation of the under-lid hook to 0° from the handle as opposed to its current 90°. I’m used to it now, but it does pose a greater risk of skin-to-hot lid contact. The plastic grips attached to the handles do a good job of dissipating heat, but time will tell if they hold up like their hardwood predecessors. The wheels roll well and while also made of plastic, they’re not getting hit with the heat from the kettle.

When this grill isn’t in use I cover it with a Weber cover. A pretty janky cover, in direct contrast to the awesome kettle grill. It’s too short to adequately cover those plastic wheels and a little too roomy, with only a single Velcro loop to secure it. Any kind of wind causes it to loft right off. The material itself seems cheap, too. When it goes down I’ll shop around for something more substantial for sure.

First thing I noticed was the 3 burners were vertical rather than horizontal that I had been used to.  After starting to use the grill, I liked the configuration much better.  
Regarding performance, grill heats up quickly to 500+ degrees extremely fast.  I have cooked on high heat a couple of times and very pleased with performance.  Also, cooked ribs low a slow.  Spirit E310 maintained a constant low temperature - in indirect heat with 1 burner on - around 225-230 degrees. Great gill for reverse searing.  Can not be more pleased.

text: I couldn’t be happier with my Spirit E-310 Propane Grill. This grill has everything that I was looking for. From the enclosed easy access tank location to the super heavy duty cast iron grill plates to the 3 very controllable burners. I swore up and down that I would never buy a propane grill because I have always cooked on a Weber Kettle grill using mesquite coals and If it ain’t broke why fix it. I finally had to give in though, I live in the San Bernardino County Mountains Community of Crestline and my wonderful neighbors like calling the Fire Department every time I would light up my Weber Kettle Grill because of the smoke that the coals give off would trigger a freak out from my neighbors. So I gave in and purchased a Weber propane grill and now I am bbq’ing all hours of the morning, day and night and my neighbors only get to enjoy the wonder smell of cooking meat and the S.B. County Fire Department is no longer coming out to my house. It really is nice to just last minute decide to bbq burgers and not have to hassle with the lengthy time of waiting for my coals to be ready to cook on or have to drive down the mountain to a 24 hour Walmart at 10 pm just so I can bbq and enjoy the midnight sky. The whole process of getting the coals lit in the Weber chimney, emptying the lit briquettes into the holders and setting the food on the grid was an absolutely amazing and fun experience! title: Much Better Than Anticipated.
text:
Had two concerns when I purchased this grill. 
I thought it might prove too small. 90% of the time it is just my wife and I, so it made sense. However, it can comfortably cook for 6 or 8 and with little creative time management it will work for even more. 
I had heard concerns about longer times to heat up, due to just 2 burners. I have found it heats up just as quickly as my old Spirit 310. A bonus is that it doesn’t suddenly spike to 5 or 600 degrees. Easier to manage cooking temperature and cooks very evenly across the grill. 
My chicken doesn’t develop a tough, thoroughly cooked outer layer and the burgers are cooked evenly inside and out. I am very pleased with the performance. 
Another plus: With the tables dropped and cover on it doesn’t block much of the view from my deck. Easy to forget it is even there.

text:
I bought the E-210 two burner because the two of us rarely grill for more than two and we were replacing a three burner that was really two big. Small can some times not be good because I had a hard time installing a full gas tank as I couldn't maneuver in the small space to reach the tank hanger/gauge. The side wall of the grill is not strong enough to support the full tank so it deflects inside with the weight. This idea of measuring the level of the tank by weight is inaccurate and a waste of time as any one who has a gas grill knows that when fuel runs out it is time to change. And lastly, why is the back of the grill not fully inclosed? How much money can Weber save by eliminating a 24" * 18" piece of sheet metal? I can assure you the local cats and raccoons will soon discover the route to the grease collector and deposit it on the garage floor. 

With that being said, the good points. The grill is overall well made and sturdy. It lights immediately and heats up quickly. The grates are heavy and easy to clean. The grease collection system is well designed and easy to clean. (If you can keep the animals out. I'm having a metal screen made to enclose my grill fully.) Overall I am pleased and satisfied with my purchase.

title: Two q1200 grills fail in same way in a month
text: I am returning a weber q1200 - again. I bought one last fall and it was working great until a few weeks ago. It got used several times a week on our patio. The gas was not getting to the burner to light. I am religious about keeping it clean, making sure the burner holes are clear. One day it just would not light - no gas to the burner. The 5 gallon propane was full. That tank worked on my Nepoleon grill. I bought a new hose, still no gas to the burner. So I bought another Q1200 grill. This one worked for 2 weeks, then again - no gas getting to the burner. Verified it was not the tank or hose. I bought a gas sniffer detector just to verify if any gas was getting through. I saw on line about what to do to "reset" the regulator attached to the grill. Still no gas got to the burner. Also online saw that these grills having the regulator built in the grill fail alot of times. The only was the grill would work was when I attach the small propane cylinder to the grill. Not acceptable to only work with a small cylinder and not the refillable  (or tank exchange) method. So I am getting another Nepoleon travelpro 285 grill. I cannot trust that the weber q1200 will always work anymore with 5 gallon propane tanks.

title: What a great product!
text:
I bought my Spirit II E-310 from Amazon on a Prime Day Special.  The heavy shipping box had clear instructions as to how to open and remove contents.  The instructions for assembly were exceptionally clear and the pieces fit together perfectly.  Extremely well designed and engineered product and packaging.

Even though I previously had a Spirit II two burner, I learned how to properly start up the unit.  The instructions had me slowly open the propane gas tank valve and wait a bit to insure gas lines came upto proper pressure.  Then I cranked up the three burners until the temperature rose to 500.  Then I reduced heat to the cooking temperature.  


I have cooked salmon, chicken and flank steak and all were evenly cooked and the temperature held steady.


What a great product!

title: E-310 Continues Weber Quality and High Performance
text:
I have owned a Weber grill for over 3 decades and this latest iteration shares the quality and hopefully durability of the previous grills I've owned.  I chose the Spirit II E-310 because it seemed to have the most bang-for-the-buck in this class.  I'm not disappointed with the choice as it compares well to my old Genesis Silver B which I finally had to retire.  Assembly was relatively easy thanks to the included instructions and the available companion video app which further illustrated each assembly step.  If I have any fault with this grill it would be the wheels which are fairly cheap plastic wheels and actually fell off the grill the first time I had to move it.  I was able to put them back on and they've stayed ever since.

All in all, this is a high performing grill with a plenty of features that I'm still getting used to including the Crossfire ignition system.  The grill heats up plenty fast and clean up has been relatively easy.  The metal is a bit thinner than the Silver B but seems to retain heat (in July) well, even when turned to Low.  I'm quite satisfied with my purchase and would do it again.

title: Disappointment
text: I have owned a number of Weber Grills over the years, starting with a charcoal kettle grill. One of the things that I have been most impressed with all of my grills is the rigid steel construction and heavier weight of the overall grill and carts. This particular grill has been quite the opposite. I really do not care for the cheaply made cart and light weight feel of the lid and grill box. This grill, so far, has been a disappointment. I bought it at one of the "Big Box" stores and paid extra for assembly. The personnel at the warehouse must have been in a hurry and left off both of the metal back covers. This makes the cart flimsy and feel like a number of the lesser priced "knockoff" grills. I immediately reported the issue to Weber (4-6 weeks ago) and was assured that I would be getting both of the missing parts within 7-11 days. So far I have only received the smaller of the two parts. A follow-up by me 7-10 days ago was met with a reassurance that I would be getting the missing part and I just needed to be "patient." Well so far no panel and my patience is all by evaporated. It's truly sad that yet another "benchmark" company has elected to make their products below standards and no longer a cut above the competition.

text:
After researching  a lot, I chose this E-210 LP gas  grill , 1st because of Weber's warranty and reputation. 2ndly because it had fold down shelves. I've got a smaller deck and wanted a smaller footprint. The size is still big enough for a decent amount of grilling space. It's easy to fold the side shelves up or down and with a good cover and with shelves folded it tucks away nicely in the corner. It ignites immediately, heats up fast and seems to grill evenly. For the limited time used it did a great job on burgers and steaks. Longer usage on different foods is to be determined.  I had it assembled and delivered, with old grill hauled away for free so no hassles there.
The one glaring problem is there is only a short back panel on the back leaving a large opening. This allows wind to blow in, looks unfinished, and because we get critters, they probably will crawl into the grill. My dealer is ordering a second panel to install which should mostly eliminate that problem. It's a strange cost cutting decision because Weber's other grills have a full back panel.
All in all, for the cost and performance this is a great smaller grill choice and recommended. We'll see if it lasts as long as my old 35 year old grill.

text:
Since 2002 I’ve had the pleasure of grilling on Weber grills.  This is my third Spirit E-210 Gas Grill.
I appreciate Weber’s innovation over the years - and their commitment to quality components. I’m a “heavy user,” in that I use the grill four or five nights a week. It’s not usual for me to shovel a path through the snow to the grill in the winter. I have to confess my observations and experiences with Weber are overwhelmingly positive.  The rare issues I’ve had with my Weber grills have been external to the product.  The time when squirrels chewed on the rubber gas line, corrosive ocean-salt air, losing a part when moving from one house to another . . .All resolved with help from Weber’s excellent Customer Care representatives.  One last data point to consider when deciding a brand of grill: Weber’s Warranty.  In all my years of using my Weber grills I had an issue with a flavor bar.  The grill was still under warranty and the Customer Care representative sent a replacement. Easy.
In my opinion, Weber honors the values of integrity, quality and customer satisfaction.

title: Mixed review:  Good, Bad, and Ugly
text:
Good:  The grill itself is great with flop down shelves and sleek overall design.  Burner knobs and lighter respond quickly.  
Bad:  The wheel locks are hard to access with your foot.  
Ugly:  This issue is not about any visual presentation of the unit.  It is the placement of the propane tank in the cabinet.  My big complaint is the installation of the propane tank.  What would be seemingly an easy concept of placing the tank inside the cabinet and securing with a simple restraining system does not exist.  Rather the engineers and designers thought a system of hanging the tank on a weight hook that visually shows how much propane gas is left in the tank would be a great idea.  So what is the problem with such a clever idea?  Lifting a full propane tank onto the "hook" is nearly impossible unless you are an avid weight lifter or you can get the assistance of another person who can help you lift the tank from the back open side of the cabinet.  Normally we lift heavy objects with our body (torso) over and above the object.  In the case of placing the tank on the weight hook, the body of the solo lifter is in front of the cabinet with only their arms are inside the cabinet.  This arrangement is extremely difficult to do and bad for the back for one person to accomplish.  What makes it even more challenging is the existence of a large round hole in the floor of the cabinet just under the final placement of the tank.  The hole is large enough that the tank slips right through the hole during the attempt to place the tank on the hook.  So what is the purpose of the hole?  It allows the full tank to hang past the cabinet floor.  This hanging system is the ugly part of this grill when the existence of a tank gauge would be a better system of letting the owner know how much gas is still in the tank.

I'm extremely impressed with the Weber Spirit E310 BBQ. The build quality is outstanding, far superior to the entry-level grills I've owned in the past. It's much heavier and feels more solid, which speaks to the excellent material quality used in its construction.

One feature I particularly appreciate is the propane tank gauge. It's a simple but incredibly useful addition that takes the guesswork out of knowing when to refill the tank.
